# Preface

natural as well as spiritual and Divine things, which he has brought forth and bore witness to therein. However, for this reason alone, we do not desire that you should hold it in higher regard than is fitting, nor accept anything without testing it. No; instead, we gladly allow the saying of the Apostle Paul to apply here, where he says in 1 Thessalonians 5:21: **Test all things, and hold fast to that which is good.** For just as no wheat grows from the earth without having its chaff with it, so we also believe that the good kernels of truth in this book are still provided or mixed with some chaff and prickly awns <note>The "awn" is the hair-like needle or "beard" found on ears of wheat or barley; the publisher uses this agricultural metaphor to explain that the reader must separate the essential truths from the less important or "thorny" parts of the text.</note>, which a person of understanding will easily know how to blow away in order to make the good little grains useful to himself. And so, we leave it entirely to each person’s own testing and judgment, without taking any of it upon ourselves in the slightest. 

Regarding the appendix, we have had it translated from the Latin manuscripts <note>original: *Lateinischen Manuscriptis*</note> that a good friend shared with us for this purpose, and have had it printed with the work in the hope that it will also serve someone; not that we sought thereby to infect anyone with the <term>gold-fever <note>The original German is *Goldsucht*, literally "gold-sickness" or "gold-addiction." In the context of 18th-century alchemy, this was a common warning against seeking only material wealth (transmuting lead into gold) rather than spiritual transformation.</note></term> which is already rampant everywhere. No; rather, we wish from our hearts that all people might seek and find God instead of gold. However, because we are well aware that every person gladly strives and searches for something, we also consider it permissible, with proper modesty, to strive for such a noble art—of which we know for certain that God communicates it to some whom He recognizes as faithful to Him, and who also walk the right path to attain it and seek Him for it in humility. Yet, we do not present such small works as being of higher value than they are, and we leave them, just as with the others, entirely to each person’s own testing and judgment. With this, we heartily commend the beloved reader to the grace of God.

->Given at Homburg vor der Höhe,<-
->January 7, 1735.<-

## Of the Author.

->Sincere and kind reader!<-

Know that the prompting of a good friend led us 
quite miraculously to the composition of this 
work, not so that it should be openly presented 
to the world, but as something from which we might 
always take occasion for our secret and intimate 
conversation.

But since the First Part of this work has come to 
light against our will, we did not want to leave it 
alone, but rather accompany it with the Second and 
Third Parts; not doubting that this work, now that it is 
complete and the First Part has been corrected by 
us from its frequent errors, will be dear and pleasant. 
We seek in this work no glory or thanks, but rather 
the reader’s satisfaction, and that he may likewise 
recognize and find therein that which the wisdom 
of God has imparted to us; just as we then also hold 
it certain that this work will provide a holy 
pleasure to God-devoted minds. And a lover of

# Preface

easily recognize and understand that our intention is not directed toward teaching anyone how to <term>make gold <note>original: *Gold machen*. This refers to physical alchemy or chrysopoeia, the process of turning base metals into gold, which the author dismisses as a secondary or lesser goal.</note></term>, but rather our aim is toward something far higher: namely, how Nature comes from **GOD**, and how **GOD** may be seen and recognized within the same; and how, furthermore, from this knowledge the true, pure service of the creature flows as a rightful sacrifice of thanks toward the Creator. 

In this, however, a sincere lover of true, nature-consistent <term>Chemistry <note>original: *Chymie*. In 1721, the distinction between chemistry and alchemy was still fluid; the author uses the term to describe the study of natural substances to find divine truths.</note></term> will find very great guidance to walk upon the true path of Nature and to avoid the wrong paths; for we have not written so obscurely that a sincere and diligent mind should not see what we have aimed for. The <term>Kabbalistic characters <note>original: *Cabbalistische Characteres*. These are symbolic signs or letters used in mystical traditions to represent spiritual forces or natural elements.</note></term>, which we have used here and there in this work for certain reasons, will not be at all difficult to resolve for one experienced in this science. 

And let no one be surprised that we have made use of chemical signs, <term>terms <note>original: *Terminorum* (Latin).</note></term>, and modes of speech, because through these we can present what we wish to indicate much more clearly, distinctly, and understandably—and also more in accordance with Nature—than with <term>metaphysical terms <note>original: *Metaphysischen Terminis*. Abstract philosophical language which the author finds less practical than the "hands-on" language of the laboratory.</note></term>. 

With this, we then close this preface and hand this work over to the just judgment of the enlightened and **GOD**-devoted reader.

January 4, 1721.

The Author.

# Chapter One.

...be led, and here and there reveals itself through springs, from which the body of salt is then separated from its water by fire and presented to us.

§. 2. It is undeniable among all rational people that salt, as we consume it, is brought to us from the great sea through subterranean passages and fissures, and is separated from its watery nature through boiling; however, this does not prove its true origin in the slightest.

§. 3. And so that all foreign opinions on this point may be set aside, and the path be opened to the truth from the foundation of nature, we will first consider salt according to its material form and figure as it appears before our eyes. Of this, we generally have three kinds, which are fundamentally only one kind: namely spring-salt, rock-salt, and sea-salt. All three are absolutely identical in their nature and figure, although they differ slightly in appearance when unseparated from their foreign parts. A fourth kind could also be introduced, and not unjustly: namely, the common <term>Earth-salt and Mother-salt <note>The author uses the alchemical symbol 🜔, which typically represents Saltpeter or Nitre, considered the "miraculous" salt or the "mother" of all salts in early modern chemistry.</note></term>. However, even this can be purified by a simple manual process so that it becomes perfectly equal in figure, appearance, and property to the common spring-salt and the others mentioned; thus, all three are of one essence, nature, and property. Its figure is **cubic**, which is a sign of earthly bodies and weight, to testify that it has been mixed with earthly qualities while passing through the earth. Regarding its form, it is fundamentally transparent, and the more it is separated from foreign parts, the more it partakes of this heavenly, translucent form. It is fluid and flowing, so that it may pass through all other bodies quite easily. Its taste is sour and a little astringent, and it is of a drying nature and property, and cooling withal—although in its center it is nothing other than an **essential fire**, as shall be proven in what follows. We have thus briefly considered it as it lies before our eyes.

§. 4. We will now also look for its true Father and Mother, as the primary question here is to investigate its origin and essence more precisely so that we may recognize it fundamentally.

§. 5. Moses teaches us in the first chapter of <term>Genesis <note>original: *Genes.*</note></term>, where he describes the creation of this entire world or our solar system, that in the beginning, the Almighty God created <note>original Hebrew: *Schamajim veeth haarez*</note> **the heavens and the earth**. Here, Moses places the heavens—the spiritual, fiery waters—first, and this not without very singular cause; for they are the beginning of all things first created by God the Lord, or the "beginning of beginnings," which according to His...

# Of the Origin of Common Salt.

true essence is almost inscrutable to us, as its wondrous naming gives us sufficient reason to recognize; for Moses, or rather the Holy Spirit through Moses, calls this expansion <term>Schamajim <note>Original Hebrew: שמים (Shamayim), usually translated as "the heavens" or "the firmament."</note></term>, which is a composite name. It has been described by the oldest Rabbis, who were practiced and experienced in the true <term>Cabbala <note>Kabbalah, the Jewish mystical tradition that seeks to uncover hidden meanings in the Hebrew Bible.</note></term>, as being composed of <term>Asch <note>Original Hebrew: אש (Esh), meaning "fire."</note></term> and <term>Majim <note>Original Hebrew: מים (Mayim), meaning "water."</note></term>. To us, according to the outer letter, this is a truly wondrous and strange mixture—for how does it seem possible to mix two such entirely contrary things so harmoniously? Yet this is an eternal truth; it is only that this fiery water, or watery fire, without which no creature can live or be sustained, is sought and recognized by so few with any diligence. 

To describe this according to its entire sphere is not our current intention; moreover, such Divine secrets require a more experienced pen than ours. Yet we will not keep silent about the little that has been shared with us from the eternal light, so that we may successfully reach our intended goal: namely, the original generation of common cooking salt—whether it be sea, well, or rock salt, or even the "wild" earth-salt. All other salts, such as the <term>Vitriols <note>Sulfuric minerals.</note></term>, <term>Alum <note>A double sulfate mineral used in tanning and medicine.</note></term>, and <term>Sal Ammoniac <note>The symbol ⨁ refers to Sal Ammoniac, which the author defines as a compound of urine and salt.</note></term>, do not belong here, as the vitriols and alums are contaminated by metallic particles. <term>Sal Ammoniac</term>, however, is a composite being of urine and common salt, just as <term>Saltpeter</term> is a composite being of acidic, volatile, alkaline, and solid parts, as shall be proven in the following chapters. The <term>alkalines</term>, however, are closest to our cooking salt, as shall be proven in its proper place.

§. 6. Shortly before, it was mentioned that the almighty GOD in the beginning created the heavens, <term>Schamajim</term>, as the beginning of beginnings, or the element of elements: namely, the fiery waters. Thereupon Moses continues, and adds afterward, <term>veeth haarez <note>Original Hebrew: ואת הארץ (v'et ha'aretz), meaning "and the earth."</note></term>, and the earth, which was the second <term>Secondary Quality <note>A term from Aristotelian physics referring to properties that arise after the primary elements are established.</note></term>. For here <term>Water <note>Represented by the symbol ∇</note></term> and <term>Fire <note>Represented by the symbol Δ</note></term> are taken in one sense, as their signs here and the following discourse indicate; for the little line <term>a —⊖— b <note>This symbol ⊖ often denotes Salt or Earth; here it illustrates a boundary line that had not yet been drawn.</note></term> was not yet there—namely, the separation of the two (commonly called an "element")—so that the <term>Schamajim</term> might immediately find a solid body or object in which they could manifest and exert their power. In the 6th and 9th verses [of Genesis], Moses further describes the separation of the two other <term>Secondary Qualities</term>, such as the air and the water, from the earth, or rather the earth from the water. Thus, water was the first <term>Secondary Quality</term>, as will be proven hereafter. And the fiery water, or essential fire, would have kept its seat (as the lightest of all) in the Sphere of <term>Schamajim</term>, while the coarser and elemental fire took its seat in the center point of the earth; thus was the divi...

# The First Chapter.

...separation or partition of the so-called elements from the first beginning, <term>Schamajim <note>Original Hebrew: *Shamayim*, meaning "the heavens."</note></term>, was accomplished. That all things—as mentioned shortly before—have their life, essence, and preservation from *Schamajim* is proven by the 11th verse of the third day’s work [of Creation]. There, by Divine command and through the power of this "fiery water" (called by the most ancient philosophers the **universal Mercury** <note>In alchemy, the "Universal Mercury" or *Mercurius Mundi* is the fundamental animating spirit or "life force" of the universe.</note>), the earth brought forth all kinds of grass, herbs, and fruitful trees, etc., even before the sun, moon, or any stars were created. This was for the food and nourishment of all living creatures that were only to be created on the 5th and 6th days; for the almighty GOD demonstrated His wise order in this: that the living creatures He yet intended to create might simultaneously find nourishment and sustenance. 

On the 4th day, the sun, moon, and all stars were finally created as the proper distributors in the household of this great world, to communicate this divine power, life, and outflow of *Schamajim* to every creature according to its necessary requirements. Now the sun began, with full force through its <term>Atoms <note>Original: *Atomos*. In this context, it refers to the smallest physical particles or emanations of light and heat.</note></term>—which were nothing but pure fire—united with the watery atoms of the **☽** <note>The alchemical symbol for the Moon.</note>, to impregnate the air. The air then further communicates this heavenly seed continuously to the sea, which is filled with it to this very hour—and not the sea alone, but the entire globe of the earth. This is proven first not only by the **earth-salt** found everywhere, but also by the dew, frost, rain, and snow, which are all filled with it. §. 26. What we have spoken of here regarding the metals should also be understood regarding minerals in general, according to their kind and genus; anyone who has understood our previous points will require no further explanation on this matter. §. 27. For all these "Realgars" are almost the homogenous outgrowths of <term>Sun and Moon</term> <note>original: "Solis & Lunæ"; meaning Gold and Silver.</note> and remained stuck in the second degree of <term>Congelation</term> <note>Solidification.</note> due to a lack of either the right Salt or the right Sulfur. Nevertheless, they have still reached their intended purpose, for their degrees necessarily belong to this universal harmony, since nothing may happen without God's will; and what happens by His holy will has also reached its ultimate end.

§. 28. Now, before we proceed further, we must also speak of that wonderful mineral water, namely the <term>Coal</term> <note>original: "Steinkohlen." # On the Origin of Common Salt.

...as a precipitate of the sun’s rays in a purer lunar salt <note>original: "lunarischen Salz"; in alchemy, "lunar" refers to silver, suggesting a silver-based salt or a salt influenced by the moon's qualities</note>, combined with those sand- and stone-making waters that are constantly steaming up in the same places within Region E. These are the most well-known types, of which the first kind is nothing other than a sulfurous salt, or sulfur coagulated by a coarse vitriolic salt (see §. 23). This sulfur is more subtle than that of the roof-coals or pitch-coals, being mixed with a coarse loamy earth. Therefore, they are not stable but weather easily in the air and crumble into a fine dust <note>original: "Mulm"; a term for decayed, powdery mineral or organic matter</note>. Thus, they cannot be used effectively for smithing and other intense work involving fire <note>original symbol: ∆; the alchemical sign for fire</note>, unless one assists them by adding a clayey, salty earth—since salt is the "bond" of sulfur. If this is done, however, they can be used quite well, as the following sections shall prove.

The second <term>variety</term> <note>original: "Species"</note>, known as <term>roof-coals</term> <note>original: "Dachkohlen"; likely referring to shale coal or surface coal found in the upper layers of a mine</note>, possesses a coarser sulfur that is better coagulated by salt and mixed with a purer clay <note>original: "Letten"; a mining term for a fine, fatty clay or loam</note>; because of this, its <term>body</term> <note>original: "Corpus"</note> is more durable and holds together more firmly. These vary depending on the nature of the clay involved: if the clay is yellowish, the coal is brown, and this is exactly like wood that has been buried in the earth, and is therefore called charcoal <note>the author is likely describing lignite or "brown coal," which retains a wood-like structure</note>. Bluish and whitish-shimmering clays also produce many brown coals, though some lean toward black. Now, if the clay is black and iron-colored, the coal will also be black; these "roof-coals" are already suitable for smithing and all other necessities. However, if they are crushed small, they too can be improved with a clay impregnated with the proper salt, so that they burn more efficiently and for a longer duration. Their base <note>the floor of the coal deposit</note> is mostly a <term>seam</term> <note>original: "Flöz"; a horizontal layer of ore or coal</note> or a clayey, sometimes firm, and occasionally sandy rock, depending on the nature of the mountains and how they have weathered. These roof-coals often refine themselves within the mountains into a truly good fat-coal or pitch-coal.

The third kind, the <term>pitch-coal</term> <note>original: "Pechkohle"; a high-quality bituminous coal known for its shiny, resinous appearance</note>, consists of a coarser, almost metallic sulfur and a finer clay, similar to quicksand. These pitch-coals are the very best, especially those found nearest to this quicksand, for their earth is delicate and pure, most precisely mixed with the sulfur, and bound and fixed by the salt water. Therefore, they are harder and can withstand the fire for much longer.

Whoever denies what has been said here must be little experienced in the workings of the earth. It is certain that where mineral coal has the best deposits, one will find—both in its toughness and in the places where it settles—such a delicate, greasy clay mixed with quicksand. One will frequently find that the coal spreads over such a layer, and this is incontrovertibly the reason for the hardness and strength of the coal. That sulfur—namely, this slimy, burning substance—is an outflow of the subterranean fire <note>original symbol: ∆</note>, and how it is generated there, shall be seen below, where it makes a breakthrough through the crevices and passages of Region E. ## The Second Chapter.
### Of the Nature of Salt.

->§. I.<-

We encountered a brine in a well-known place which consists of the **first saline essence** <note>original: "primo salinischen Wesen"</note> (which we call common salt), as well as a delicate **vitriol** (which quality it took from the very rich, yet volatile copper-sand which covers the "roof-coals" <note>likely a layer of carbonaceous shale</note> of that place and also runs beneath them, as well as from the veins themselves with which the salt-springs are encased, consisting of a stone full of volatile, silver-bearing copper); and thirdly, from a volatile **acid or nitre** <term>Acido oder Nitro</term>. This latter quality the brine possesses through the power of its own internal magnet (from the first saline property) directly from the influences of the heavens. 

To help this brine, we found it then most useful to clarify or purify it with a **spermatic essence** <note>In alchemy, this refers to organic proteins or "seed" substances, such as egg whites or blood, used for clarification</note> instead of **bovine-colors** <note>original: "Rindesfarben"; likely referring to the use of ox blood as a traditional clarifying agent in salt-boiling</note>; however, the trick was that one must rub this essence well with the brine and thus perform the clarification. After the clarification, the **precipitation** <term>Præcipitation</term> consisted of **microcosmic salt** <term>Microcosm.</term> <note>A salt derived from urine: sodium ammonium hydrogen phosphate</note>: 3 parts; of **Lead** <term>♄</term> <note>The symbol for Saturn/Lead</note>: 2 parts; and 1 part **Alemzodar** <note>An alchemical term for Sal Ammoniac or a similar ammonium chloride salt</note>, or even one and a half or 2 parts. All of this we let flow into a **mass** <term>Massa</term>, and from it we scattered into a clarified pan full of brine standing in the boil—perhaps a pound and a half—and let it boil down thoroughly with it. Thus, from the red "wild water" obtained with bucket and rope, there precipitated a most magnificent, white, and durable salt with good profit, which no moisture could harm; rather, it became like a stone and surpassed all other known common salts in pleasantness and sharpness.

From these words *Urim Aesh Jah* (*Fire of the LORD*), the Persians, according to their dialect, named their holy fire *Orim-as-da*, and it was therefore held in such honor among them.

That fire is now a true Salt, we have proven with such irrefutable reasons in *Chapter I*, specifically *§. 18. 19.*, that even the gates of Hell can prevail nothing against it. Therefore *Mark* <note>original: "Marcus," referring to Mark 9:49: "For every one shall be salted with fire, and every sacrifice shall be salted with salt."</note> says: all men shall be seasoned with fire, and all sacrifices (that is, the sacrifice of the lips) shall be seasoned with Salt (that is, with a contrite and broken heart, in a fiery and yearning spirit). # The Third Chapter.

He is so necessary to us, indeed almost the most necessary and useful on the whole earth, and no art, science, or whatever it may be, can be devised where *Mars* <note>In alchemy, *Mars* is the symbol and name for the metal Iron.</note> could be spared; indeed, even most of our food and nourishment consists of him, as clearly appears from all the clayey and loamy earths from which bricks are fired, whose redness indicates nothing other than the presence of iron, which can also be separated from it by means of a good flux in a strong Fire ($\triangle$) <note>original: $\triangle$; the symbol for Fire</note>, however little of it there may be. That this clayey earth and yellow loam were once nothing but iron—which is daily torn more and more from its *minera* <note>The "minera" refers to the ore or the "womb" of the metal in the earth.</note> and root by the plowshare, and is brought to decay, bringing forth grass, herbs, roots, and all kinds of grain and fruit for our nourishment—is an incontrovertible proof. That the entire ground was once almost covered with iron ore, which weathered in this way over time, is clearly proven by the fact that one still finds such clods of iron ore here and there, especially in those places where the soil does not stand high above the drifting sands, and the sun's rays (the red solar Fire $\triangle$) <note>original: $\odot$rische $\triangle$; the "Solar Fire," referring to the heat and transformative power of the Sun</note> and the water of the drifting sands (which is a sand- and stone-making Water $\nabla$; see Chapter 1, sections 12, 13, 14, 15 regarding this) can easily reach it. Even if one wanted to admit an uncountable number of worlds, one after the other, one must still stop at some point; otherwise, this quite cruel absurdity would follow: that as long as **God** the **Lord** has existed, worlds would also have existed, and thus these worlds would have been co-eternal and co-existent with **God**. It would then follow that one must have always "hatched" the other, from which, in the end, they would actually become gods. 

O folly of the over-clever and stone-blind world! It remains certain that when it pleased the almighty **GOD** to create this world, that moment of beginning was the same to Him as all His infinity; thus, one could see no "past eternity" there, which would otherwise have been a fixed period of time—something that cannot take place in **GOD**. Light-Fire, became as it were a hideous and material darkness, in which Lucifer—who had now become Satan, that is, an adversary—along with all his millions, lacking the Divine Light, raged and stormed in a loathsome, dark, fiery form. ## Of the Fall of Lucifer.

§. 4. Now the Chaos consisted of the following figure (Fig. No. 55), namely in the dark, earthly, fierce Fire-Water <note>original uses the symbol for Fire: Δ</note> upon which the Spirit of GOD moved (*Gen. 1:2*). In contrast, the Shamayim <note>Hebrew: *Schamajim*, the heavens</note> is a lovely joy-light and light-water. In this Chaos, the rebellious spirit [Lucifer] with all his following was locked and shut away, and thus had to experience what it was like to be deprived of the Divine Light. This Chaos, with its enclosed, foul spirits, was nonetheless still that which had initially flowed out from the eternal Divine *Fiat* <note>Latin: "let it be done"—the creative command of God</note>, but it was inverted; instead of pure light, it was pure darkness and abhorrence. Yet, through Divine and uncircumscribed power, God could again make from this place—which had only become a curse incidentally through its ruler, Lucifer—whatever was pleasing to His eternal Divine Counsel.

§. 5. Now the text says in *Gen. 1:1* that in the beginning GOD (*Elohim* <note>a Hebrew name for God, often associated with justice and power</note>) created the heavens and the earth; that was now this aforementioned Chaos. Namely: the spheres or circles of Lucifer and all his created host had been brought back into this dark mixture by the righteous vengeance of the holy Divine Judgment. Within this mixture, the heavens and the earth were hidden—namely the three beginnings: the Sun <note>original symbol: ☉, representing the divine spark or sulfur</note>, Fire <note>original symbol: Δ</note>, and Salt <note>original symbol: ∗, the third principle of matter</note>. This is the Shamayim <note>Heavens</note>, which is Fire <note>original symbol: Δ</note> as well as Water <note>original symbol: ∇</note>, namely the secret Sun <note>original symbol: ☉</note>, or the essence created solely by GOD the Almighty, which is also three, made manifest in four <note>likely referring to the three spiritual principles manifesting in the four physical elements</note>. ## The First Day’s Work.

§. 8. Furthermore, the text says, *thus was evening, and thus was also morning, the first day.* This day was a first period of 24 hours, as clearly appears from the contrast with the fourth day's work, upon which the sun and moon were created, and thus the true night and the true day were first created through the orbit of the lights. The name "day" is given to both this first day and that fourth day in the exact same sense. Thus, on this first day, through the power of the revealed light, it was bright in one half-circle—that is, day—and because the coarser and darker elements remained below, it was simultaneously night in the other half-circle. Because nothing created exists or can persist without movement, (as Psalm 74, verse 16 <note>original: "v. 15"; German Bibles of the era often followed a different verse numbering than the King James Version.</note> says: *The day is thine, the night also is thine: thou hast prepared both the light and the sun,* ) this revealed light and darkness created the same distinction between day and night which the celestial lights created on the fourth day's work, as is clear and evident through the words of distinction used by the Holy Spirit through Moses, such as "evening" and "morning." The 3rd verse says: *Let there be light, and there was light,* etc. This was the aforementioned revelation of light and darkness, and furthermore, from this light were created all heavenly lights and bodies under the firmament, namely our solar system <note>original: "Sonnen-Systematis"</note>. ## The Fourth Day's Work.

Firstly, it is said that everyone is the interpreter of his own words; secondly, we are certain that if we wished to explain ourselves clearly on this matter, every rational person would agree with our meaning. ## The Fifth Day’s Work.

§. 30. The creatures of this fifth day’s work were everything that lives in the seas, lakes, rivers, and other waters, as well as in the air; as can be clearly seen in Genesis 1:20 to 23. The <term>mercurial</term> <note>In the alchemical tradition used here, "mercurial" refers to the principle of fluidity and life-force.</note> substances, namely all *plants* <note>original: "Vegetabilia"</note>, were the first to be separated or brought forth; after these came everything of a <term>saline</term> <note>The "saline" or salt principle represents the physical body or the medium of the sea.</note> substance, which includes all that lives in the seas and all other waters, as well as in the air. The <term>sulphurous</term> <note>The "sulphurous" principle represents the soul or the burning heat of life found in land animals.</note> substances, however, such as all animals of the earth, appear only on the sixth and final day. All these creatures, the fish and the birds, were—like the *plants*—glorious, pure, and perfectly healthy in their substance before the Fall of Man and the curse that followed. They were neither predatory nor inclined to cause harm. However, after the Fall and the Curse, everything within them was turned inward; their initial pure substance was wrapped and locked away in a coarser essence. Consequently, very little of that life-sap necessary for the preservation of human life can now be obtained from them. At this point, we should perhaps speak further of the various properties of both fish and birds—those that live in fresh water as well as salt water, and consequently of all birds. However, everything previously discussed will satisfy the reader. We only wish to add this: nothing seems more strange to us than that rational people make so much fuss and argument regarding the winter quarters or whereabouts of certain birds, such as swallows and storks. Yet their origin and creation in Genesis 1:20 is crystal clear. One can truly and irrefutably conclude that during the winter—the time of their absence—they must have their residence in deep lakes, warm marshes, and similar places; and there it remains, thus concluding this fifth day’s work. <note>The author refers to a then-common belief, supported by figures like Carolus Linnaeus, that swallows spent the winter hibernating in the mud at the bottom of lakes rather than migrating south.</note>

# Chapter Five

To say nothing of other famous rivers, such as the Danube and the Rhine among us Europeans, which carry such magnificent fruits as gold and wine (for which there are nonetheless more lovers than for Divine Truth) almost in abundance. # The Fifth Chapter

To set down all of these various opinions here would be an unnecessary and tedious task for us, as none of them serve our purpose. Furthermore, we do not wish to dissect the word <term>Eden</term> <note>Hebrew for "delight" or "pleasure"</note> nor the word <term>Kedem</term> <note>Hebrew for "east" or "ancient/before"</note> according to the <term>Cabbala</term> <note>A system of Jewish mysticism and scriptural interpretation</note>, as it would lead us far too away from our current intention; we wish simply to remain with the understanding of the Scriptures. The text says: God the Lord planted the garden in Eden, toward the east; it is more than well known to all who are familiar with the original language <note>Hebrew</note> that "Eden" signifies a place of all perfect delight. But where was this place? That is the question. The text says "toward the east"; but where was this east? Was it according to the rising of the sun, or, as the Rabbis would have it, in the direction toward which Adam’s face was turned when he was created? Was it in the land of Canaan, or some other lovely region of Asia?

We answer that neither the one nor the other has hit the mark, for in *Genesis 2:10* it is written that a river went out of Eden, which then divided into four main streams. Now, where are this main source and the primary rivers that sprang from it hidden? From the very beginning, this has caused no small amount of trouble for the majority of men—especially those whose wisdom rests upon certain man-made dogmas. According to them, one stream must be the Ganges, another the Nile, and so forth. This is especially so because Holy Scripture mentions certain lands which these main rivers are supposed to flow around and water. Here one might well say: *Make it rhyme [or I’ll eat you]*, etc. <note>original: "Reime dich 2c."; a German idiom for forcing a connection or argument that does not naturally fit.</note> One flows toward the south and begins in the north, the other begins in the south and flows toward the north, and so on. Is that not a strange source from which these forced "main streams" are supposed to flow or originate?

We wonder, since they have gone to such trouble over these famous rivers, why they have forgotten the *Rio della Plata* in America? Not to mention other famous rivers, such as our European Danube and the Rhine, which carry with them such magnificent fruits as gold and wine—for which there are far more lovers than there are for Divine Truth. If one further asks how it comes to pass that today the sources of these "main rivers" are directly opposite one another and so terribly distant from each other, the answer given is that the <term>Great Flood</term> caused this, along with other such miserable bungling <note>original: "Stümpeleyen"</note>, which are more worthy of laughter than of serious zeal. But rather than detaining ourselves any longer with so many confused opinions, we wish to return to the text as the eternal truth.

# The Fifth Chapter.

§ 35. Now we return again to the end of the preceding 33rd section, where we heard what a glorious creature the human Adam was; in what glorious light and radiance, in perfect accordance with the will of God, and thus in true holiness and righteousness, in indescribable gentle stillness, peace, and joy he stood. In this state he might have remained eternally, provided he had not lusted against the prohibition of his Creator, who had formed him so gloriously. When God the Lord had created him so gloriously after His image and likeness, and had made him a ruler of this entire universe <note>original: *Universi*</note> (from which Lucifer had fallen), and had given him Eden as his throne, He commanded him that he should not desire, much less eat, of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, under the unavoidable penalty of temporal and eternal death; on the other hand, he might freely enjoy everything else, even the tree of life in the middle of the garden, and rule over all creatures and things above and under his throne.

Earlier in this chapter, the fall of Lucifer and its cause were discussed at length, as well as how this seat of Lucifer in this present world was changed, and how the human Adam was created in Lucifer's place to rule and fill this world. Now, when Lucifer saw this glorious creature, Adam, as a king of this powerful machine <note>original: *Machinae*; here referring to the complex, divinely ordered structure of the physical and spiritual world</note> (from which he had been cast out on account of his pride), his wrath and envy were ignited against this man, seeking to pull him out of this great glory into his own ruin and expulsion. He therefore dispatched his deputy, the lord and prince of the air, Beelzebub (since Lucifer himself lies locked in the fiery pit with chains and bonds of darkness until the day of final judgment) to provoke the human Adam against God's will and commandment. 

He took his opportunity with the man because he saw him alone; he showed or pointed out to him all the kingdoms of this world, suggesting what use all of this was to him if he were so alone. Conversely, if he would seek to multiply himself into innumerable millions, then he would only then truly be able to rule over this world; and this he could accomplish by his own power, as such a powerful king of his own property (this great universe), according to all his own will. And so he provoked the man, so that he lusted within himself and for his own great glory against his Creator, and generated disobedience against the eternal God in his imagination <note>In this context, "imagination" refers to the creative, formative power of the soul to visualize and bring about a state of being</note>, and strived after a form <note>original: *Specie*</note> in which he might release his power and multiplication, and possess this world by his own authority, and thus set himself against his God and King. In this, Satan presented to him that he, as an immortal spirit breathed out directly from God, was eternally immortal and could suffer no decay or death. Whereby sin was actually, yet spiritually, generated in Adam.

### §. 37. ###

Once this section is completed, it will be necessary for us to answer several questions—posed by the wise, as well as the inquisitive and the foolish. The holy text speaks of this in such a way that the matter cannot be easily settled by the bare letter alone, unless one seeks the true mystical understanding within it. Thus, the text says of these trees in **Genesis 2:9** that God the Lord brought forth from the earth of the Garden of Eden all kinds of trees (Note!) and also the Tree of Life in the midst of the garden, as well as the Tree of the Knowledge of Good and Evil, etc. Here we see as clear as day that these two trees were not imaginary beings, but were and still are actual trees (from the earth in Eden), and that both bore fruit. Christ the Lord also promises in **Revelation 2:7** <note>original Latin: "Apoc. II. v. 7"</note> that he will give those who overcome to eat of the Tree of Life, which is in the midst of the Paradise of God. Since they are real trees, what then is the "Life" in the one, and what is the "Knowledge" in the other that brought death? Both are essential properties in these trees; and we have heard in detail above how Lucifer fell—namely, he lusted after his own beauty, power, and glory...

## Chapter Five ##

...brought forth everything in perfection and purity, without any curse, death, or corruption. However, the current dark, tangible state, which gives birth to death, caused the Fall of man. Since the entire creation, up to its present material or tangible state, was completed within the Six Days, it follows indisputably that man was not only created on the sixth day but also fell on that same day and was cast out of Eden. Anyone who is not pleased by this explanation may search in the "heathen dust of the schools" <note>original: "heydnischen Staube der Schulen" — a disparaging reference to academic or scholastic theology which the author views as spiritually dry or worldly.</note> to satisfy their whims, as we are far too few to please everyone—especially since the Lord God Himself satisfies no one, or at least very few.

The third question, concerning the way to the **Tree of Life** in the Garden of Eden: it would perhaps not be necessary to answer this, because within the entire spiritual hierarchy, the location of the Garden in Eden is established here or there on our earth (though it is said to have been destroyed and washed away by the Great Flood with all its waters). Thus, the way there must not be unknown to them—unless new geography does not wish to agree with the old and has paved a way for them to the wrong place. However, we shall let them keep their Paradise and still briefly answer this question.

It has been explained extensively before how, through the bonds of the visible and tangible elements, acting like firm clamps, all original <term>Light-Beings<gloss>Licht-Wesen: The spiritual, radiant form of humanity before the Fall, which was later "clothed" in material flesh.</gloss></term> were wrapped and locked away. Also, how after man was surrounded with this <term>elemental body<gloss>elementarischer Leib: The physical body made of the four elements, subject to decay and death.</gloss></term>, he could not remain in Eden (because he had consumed nothing from the **Tree of Life**), for this elemental body could not find its proper nourishment there. Thus, he was driven out to this place. Therefore, as long as this destructible elemental body exists, there is nothing to be said of the way to the **Tree of Life** in Eden.

However, as soon as this body is laid down in corruption through death, man—who was created from the dust of the earth of Eden—is released and liberated once more. This applies to those who enjoy the true **Bread of Heaven** and are thereby reunited with their original state, the Divine Light and eternal life of joy. Saint Paul teaches this most gloriously in **1 Corinthians 15, verses 36 to 50**, where he reveals this whole mystery openly and without concealment. This path is then revealed to them and no longer blocked; so much for this question.

Indeed, a very important matter could have been discussed here, namely the different states of the deceased. This was also our initial intention, but as the work has already grown larger "under the pen" than we originally determined, these and similar highly important matters must remain set aside for now, whereby also, at the same time, the adversaries—

The Cherubim are spoken of in few places in Scripture, yet they are described in such a way that one can indisputably conclude they have a human form and are also powerful spirits. These are stationed toward the **East** <note>original: "Aufgang" — literally "the rising," referring to the direction of the sunrise or the Orient.</note> to guard the **Tree of Life**. How many of them there were is not easily gathered from the literal word of Scripture; nevertheless, from the circumstances of the mysteries of the Old Testament, it can be concluded with certainty that there were two of these powerful spirits, doubtless with their subordinate heavenly hosts. Their weapons are the terrifying fire-flames of the **wrath of God**. These now guard the way in the East (as spoken of above) so that from this <term>animalistic world<gloss>thierischen Welt: A term used in mystical theology to describe the fallen, material state of existence where humans live by physical instincts rather than spiritual light.</gloss></term>, before the reunification with God through Christ and the laying off of corruption and the curse, nothing can approach the Tree of Life. <note>(*) When we consider how the Lord God, on the sixth day of creation, first created all the animals and creeping things of the earth, and thereafter (presumably) toward evening created man; and further consider how, according to the testimony of Moses, God only then planted the Garden of **Eden** and placed man therein to till and to keep it; then also brought all animals and birds to the man that he should give each its name, which he then did, and only after this fell into a deep sleep, in which sleep God created the woman from him, and brought and joined her to Adam after he had awakened again; after this, the woman first engaged in a conversation with the serpent and was seduced by it to eat of the forbidden fruit, which she then, having already eaten, also seduced Adam into eating. Whereupon they first became aware that they were naked, wove aprons of fig leaves to cover their shame; fled before the voice of the Lord when they heard it, but were then called by the Lord, judged, and finally clothed in animal skins and banished from **Paradise**, etc. Thus, it is not easy to believe that all this occurred still on the sixth day of creation, unless one also believed that the days of creation were not common days of 24 hours, but of a much longer duration. For all things which happen in a natural way require a natural time and duration, and thus it was impossible for these things, of which Moses makes mention—from the creation of man to his banishment upon the cursed earth—to have happened in several <note>The catchword "Stun-" indicates the next page begins with "Stunden" (hours).</note></note>

In death, as if in a nightly sleep, he is refreshed and prepared and awakened for the final Seventh Time, as his **Sabbath**, to celebrate it in a joyful state with **Christ** his **Savior**, the heavenly **Adam**, who has brought back everything that was lost in the first **Adam**.

### Chapter II.

### On the Origin and Production of both Celestial and Earthly Sulfur.

->§ 1.<-

Regarding the origin and production of sulfur: we do not speak of the common variety alone, from which one prepares sulfur-sticks <note>original: "Schwefel-Hölzlein," refers to early matches or fire-starters tipped with brimstone.</note> and the like; rather, our intention is to speak of that <term>△: Sulfur</term> which is of one origin and essence with <term>⊖: Salt</term> and <term>♀: Mercury</term>. To report something of this secret wonder-<term>△: Sulfur</term> and light is now our purpose, and how from this the earthly, destructive, and, as it were, all-killing <term>△: Sulfur</term> was produced through Lucifer's fall. <note>In this theosophical context, the fall of Lucifer is believed to have corrupted the pure, celestial elements into their harsh, physical forms.</note>

->§ 2.<-

Now, some who have seen the aforementioned part and read this might interpret it as something unnecessary for us to write something special about <term>Sulfur</term>

<header>Chapter I.</header>

...we have undertaken here; and that we might have a similar intention regarding <term>☿: Mercury</term> <note>alchemical symbol for Mercury</note>. To such a person, the answer is that if he carefully considered the work of Creation, he would spare himself such unnecessary interpretations.

§. 3. The holy text says: **In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth.** <note>Genesis 1:1</note> Here the text clearly speaks of two distinct beings: namely, the dark, enclosed <term>△: Fire</term> <note>alchemical symbol for Fire</note> or "fat fire-clump," and then the salty, spiritual (that is, Triatic) light-<term>🜍: Sulfur</term> <note>alchemical symbol for Sulfur/Light-Fire</note>. In this, we must again remind the pseudo-wise man <note>original: "Klügling," a dismissive term for someone who thinks they are smarter than they are</note> that he should not be vexed that we wrote so much about the red and white, masculine and feminine, solar and lunar <term>△: Fire</term> in the preceding First Part, and have now undertaken to write of it anew in this work. Rather, we ask him to first wait patiently for the end of this work; then everyone shall be permitted to root through it with the snout of their over-cleverness as much as they please, and likewise to grunt against it according to all their mental talents. Nevertheless, according to Pilate's words to the malicious Jewish people, it shall remain as it stands: namely, **"What I have written, I have written."** <note>original Latin: "Quod scripsi, scripsi," John 19:22</note>

§. 4. But to return to our purpose and to follow the holy text herein: it is well worth considering why the Earth, as the dark, stinking fire-clump <note>original: "△ Klumpen"</note>, was placed immediately after the creation of the Heavens, as the pleasant light-<term>🜍: Sulfur</term>? That this is not merely a requirement of the language’s nature, but rather the Holy Spirit’s way of speaking to indicate high mysteries, is sufficiently known to those who are even slightly versed in Hebrew. For, according to the nature of that language, it could just as well have been said: **The Earth and the Heavens**, as it was said, **the Heavens and the Earth.** Therefore, it is first necessary to consider this more closely.

The original text, however, uses two contrasting terms here: **Image** and **Likeness**. Now, my portrait <note>original: "Contrefait," an older term for a likeness or portrait</note> or a statue modeled after me certainly shows my **Image**, but not my **Likeness**; otherwise, the portrait or statue would also have to possess my understanding and all other qualities of my spirit and soul. Whosoever has received in the spirit any true knowledge of Revelation 21:9 and knows who the Bride, the Wife of the Lamb, is, will also recognize what was indicated by the "Image" and "Likeness." # Of the Origin and Generation of Sulfur.

Everything that shines casts forth its rays, whether it possesses its light from within itself or has borrowed it. In <note>Genesis 1:16</note>, the Moon is called a light, with the addition "the lesser"; however, astronomical investigations prove that the Moon has no other light than the extent to which it is illuminated by the Sun. Accordingly, the words of the holy text would only be understood with a distinction—namely, only insofar as the Moon receives its light from the Sun. But Holy Scripture states a unique distinction in clear, plain words: *And **God** made two great lights: the greater light to rule the day, and the lesser light to rule the night; he made the stars also, etc.* And thus, the Moon was intended to be a light to rule the night. Holy Scripture is truth, and in no place does it use such hyperbolic figures of speech; it matters not how the Moon may be viewed through telescopes <note>original: *Fern-Gläser*</note>. For just as in bright sunshine at high noon, a small burning wax candle, removed two to three thousand paces from our eyes, cannot possibly be recognized as burning—even though one can actually see and recognize its body through a good perspective glass <note>An early term for a telescope</note>—it nevertheless is and remains a true burning light. In just such a manner, the Moon is also a true light, regardless of the fact that the stargazers cannot recognize it as such. However, it can by no means be denied that it receives its bright, waxing and waning light from the <term>Sun</term> <note>symbol: ☉</note>, as the center-point of all light known to us outside of the Light of Heaven; nor can it be denied that its essential, innate light is thereby obscured and suppressed.

To be sure, a pedantic skeptic <note>original: *übersichtiger Klügling* — literally a "superficial clever-clog"</note> will object and say: if the Moon truly had its own independent light, one would surely have to recognize it at night on that part which was not being looked upon by the Sun, especially since the bright light of day could provide no cause for interference? Certainly, this objection carries no small weight, especially when one relies on experience and the evidence of telescopes; however, it is not our purpose here to investigate how far these are to be trusted in this matter. Instead, we refer again to Holy Scripture and to what we have already said above regarding this. Beyond all this, it is as clear as day and manifest to the eyes of all the world that when the Moon is new during clear weather, one can actually distinguish and recognize its entire body, through its whole circumference, by a dark fiery redness <note>This refers to the phenomenon now known as "Earthshine" or the "Ashen Light," where the dark part of the moon is faintly visible</note>. That the Moon's body cannot always be recognized by the eyes in this way is caused by the increasing, powerful light of the <term>Sun</term> <note>symbol: ☉</note>. Thus, it remains firmly established by us, along with Holy Scripture, that the <term>Moon</term> <note>symbol: ☽</note> is a light in and of itself (namely, a weak and dark one). <note>1 Corinthians 15:41</note>: *There is one glory of the sun, another glory of the moon, and another glory of the stars; for one star* <note>original: *ein ** [Stern]*</note> *excels the*

§. 43. Now, one might well wish to know what this angelic food consists of, and how its consumption takes place? ## The Second Chapter.
## On the Utility and Use of Heavenly Sulfur.

->§. 1.<-

No one should seek in these writings to learn how to make sulfur matches or threads, for we shall speak of a far different utility and use than that of this old wives’ handiwork, or of ointments for scabs, or how the so-called Spirit from <term>Sulfur</term> <note>original symbol: 🜍</note>—squeezed out by the gold-thieving alchemists and their guild-associates—is to be made. In the preceding chapter, we spoke of two sulfurs, the heavenly and the earthly; now we wish to speak of the use of the heavenly, as much as is known to us through the grace of **God**. That the heavenly <term>Sulfur</term> <note>original symbol: 🜍</note>, as well as the earthly, is the cause of coagulation and consequently of corporeality, no true investigator of nature will be able to deny. The true art of separation <note>The author uses "Scheide-Kunst," an early term for chemistry and alchemy.</note> teaches this openly when one dissolves and brings back bodies without the violence of fire (or those so-called corrosive, hellish <term>solvents</term> <note>original: "Menstrua"—alchemical liquids used to dissolve solids.</note>, which do not separate but rather destroy through executioner-like torture).

->§. 2.<-

How the poor, gold-greedy pot-boilers <note>original: "Sudel-Köche"—a derogatory term for amateur or fraudulent alchemists who worked without proper knowledge.</note> toil and plague themselves to find a <term>solvent</term> <note>original: "Menstruum"</note> to fundamentally dissolve <term>Gold</term> <note>original symbol: ☉</note> and all other metals, and on the other hand to make the volatile bodies fixed! Indeed, one finds among them so many strange processes running contrary to nature, concerning such strange things striving against one another, that Folly itself could not invent anything more foolish. It is such that with these stained papers, one could heat the room of an entire garrison through a whole winter. Yes, it is hardly possible to describe how much <term>Gold</term> <note>original symbol: ☉</note> and <term>Silver</term> <note>original symbol: ☽</note> have not only been utterly destroyed and chased through the chimneys by such hellish torture, but also, under this pretext, have been made invisible by their "thief-claws" without the wonder-stone of the yet-undiscovered siskin’s nest <note>A folkloric reference; the siskin's nest was said to contain a stone that made the owner invisible. Here it refers to the elusive Philosopher's Stone.</note>. If nature were known to them, their folly would soon be made manifest, and they would see how entirely different an essence this universal dissolving thing is—and also that it is not a composite thing, but

Thus, they remain stone-blind without any knowledge, and are leaders of the blind spirit, until they all fall into the pit of temporal and, alas! all too often, eternal ruin.

...just as wheat, after it has become ripe, must be cut or mown by the sickle and scythe, brought into the barn, threshed, ground, leavened, kneaded, and baked into bread; yet, if one has neither house, yard, field, barn, nor oven, and thus cannot put all this knowledge into practice, this does not in the least hinder the fundamental science of it. Why then should we say to such a wise-pretender: why did we not do or make this or that ourselves rather than just chatting about it? Fool! To one He gives perfect knowledge, to another simply the ability to do this or that, without any fundamental understanding or science of the things necessary for his work and business. For example: A shoemaker makes his shoes from leather, the preparation of which is known to him; yet he knows as little of the animal's (from which the skin was taken for his leather) essential properties as we currently know of the secrets of the Chinese Emperor. Furthermore, we are not obligated to give anyone an account or answer for what we may have done in this matter, or what we still intend to undertake, if God grants life and health.

The Hebrew **Mago-Kabbalists** <term>Mago-Kabbalist: A practitioner who combines Magia (divine wisdom) with Kabbalistic interpretation of scripture</term> provide a completely different description of the dwelling of these wonderful creatures, as well as the **Throne of God’s Glory**, or of the **Divine Vision**, of which the Psalmist says in Psalm 16:11: **In your presence is the fullness of all joy.** They also show, through their **Sephiroth** <term>Sephiroth: In Kabbalah, the ten attributes or emanations through which the Infinite (Ein Sof) reveals itself and interacts with the universe</term>, the various workings of the Divine Majesty upon all spirits, angels, and earthly creatures. I never knew you: depart from me, you evildoers!** And furthermore, what is read in Acts 19:13, 16 about the sons of the Jew **Sceva**, who were **Devil-Banners** <term>Devil-Banners: Exorcists or "conjurors" who attempt to bind or command spirits by ritual means</term> and presumed to drive out devils in Jesus' name, which turned out very badly for them: such things and the like belong to the aforementioned damnable class of the **misuse of the Divine Name**. Excellent information on this subject could be shared with the seekers, provided it did not lead us too far from our purpose; it must therefore remain set aside until another opportunity.

# On the Nature, Benefit, and Use of Terrestrial Sulfur.

Common sulfur <note>original symbol: △</note> likewise has its power herein; however, he who does not know how to well-unite it with red gold <note>original symbol: ☉</note> in the first degree of fixation and the fire <note>original symbol: △</note> of lead <note>original symbol: ♄</note>, and afterwards apply it to silver <note>original symbol: ☽</note>, will skim little fat from this broth <note>a German idiom meaning to reap little benefit</note>. But note that the same can be performed neither in a crucible nor in cementation boxes, much less in your foolish and wondrous furnaces. Yet we remind you that these are not to be used all together and at once, but only as the matter requires; no recipe <note>original: Rec.</note> seems to fit our purpose. The species follow accordingly, namely: salt <note>original symbol: ⊖</note>, nitre <note>original symbol: Φ</note>, vitriol <note>original symbol: ⊕</note>, alum <note>original symbol: O</note>, and sal ammoniac <note>original symbols: ∗ □</note>. These, prepared according to the art and made firm, are very useful; their acid <note>original: Acidum</note> is highly harmful. The tartar <note>original: Tartarus; potassium bitartrate</note> must be elevated, and the vitriol washed in its water <note>original symbol: ∇</note> and turned to redness <note>original: ad rub., short for "ad rubrum"</note>. Furthermore, one must have the fixed oils of the salts <note>original: "Sen.", likely an abbreviation for "Salen" or "Semen" (principles)</note>, likewise of antimony <note>original symbol: ♁, here rendered as δ</note>, iron <note>original symbol: ♂</note>, and copper <note>original symbol: ♀</note>, yet prepared without any corrosive means, but only through a common <term>solvent</term> <note>original: Menstruum</note> known to all the world, and lastly and especially the prepared thing mentioned above in Chapter III, § 1. If the artist has all these pieces at hand, he can be assured that he will perform wonders in <term>cementation</term>. Yet, as already stated, the correct art of cementation—not in crucibles or boxes—must be known to him, as well as the metal that is to be cemented. Whoever rightly understands what we have said about the species up to this point will not expend his labor and costs in vain. However, we fear that for most, it has not been said clearly enough. Yet we are assured that we have spoken the truth, and indeed, all too redundantly.

**§. 10.** Above in § 4, we made some mention of how pyrites <note>original: Kieß</note> (as a sulfur <note>original symbol: △</note> fixed in the first degree) is useful in smelting, which is likewise to be performed by common sulfur <note>original symbol: △</note>. In regard to its stygian <note>original: $\sigma$ig-lialiſchen; likely "stygialischen," meaning hellish or corrosive</note> substance in the fire <note>original symbol: △</note>, it dissolves all metals without distinction and divides them into the smallest particles, just like a parting-acid <note>original: Scheid-Waſſer; nitric acid</note> or aqua regia <note>original symbol: ∇ Reg.; "royal water," a mixture of nitric and hydrochloric acid</note>. Before its corrosive spirit or smoke, no metal—indeed, hardly even gold <note>original symbol: ☉</note>—is truly safe, as daily experience teaches. Therefore, he who has not rightly learned the proper additives, fire, hearth, and all manipulations for such smelting will have to pay enough "tuition" <note>original: Lehrgeld; a metaphor for learning through costly mistakes</note> through the greatest losses. However, that iron <note>original symbol: ♂</note> and copper <note>original symbol: ♀</note>, lawfully cemented with sulfur <note>original symbol: △</note> and subsequently properly used in large-scale smelting, create quite uncommon benefits, is not yet known everywhere. This work is suitable only for poor ores. The lover [of the art]...

### Chapter Three.
<meta>catchword: Wider- (Against-)</meta>

One can be assured of this, to their greatest pleasure, through a **crucible test** <term>crucible test: a small-scale trial to determine the purity or composition of metals</term> using such cemented **antimony** <note>original symbol: ♁</note>, **copper** <note>original symbol: ♀</note>, **gold** <note>original symbol: ☉</note>, **iron** <note>original symbol: ♂</note>, and **silver** <note>original symbol: ☽</note> mixed in the proper proportions. When covered with **vitriol** <note>original: Vitr.</note> and kept in the **fire** <note>original symbol: △</note> for several hours according to the art, the results are certain. However, the practitioner must be familiar with the correct **reduction flux** <note>a substance used to promote the melting of metals and the removal of impurities</note>, otherwise he will suffer a loss of his **silver** <note>original symbol: ☽</note>. 

As for what else **sulfur** <note>original symbol: 🜍</note> causes in ores during **roasting** and **smelting**, one hears of it, unfortunately, at all smelting works. For this reason, they are accustomed to roasting their ores—which are often very pyritic and sulfurous—in all manner of ways before smelting. But the damage caused in some places by ignorant roasting is felt most painfully in the purses of the **mine owners** <note>original: Gewercken</note>. If these good people knew how to properly judge the **sulfur** <note>original symbol: 🜍</note> in their ores (specifically, its nature, and whether it contains much raw **mercury** <note>original symbol: ☿</note> fixed in the first degree, or what kind of **realgar** <term>realgar: a naturally occurring red arsenic ore</term> is attached to it), they would surely conduct their ore-burning or roasting differently. They would not then blow the greater part of the metal into the air along with the arsenic-like sulfur during both the roasting and the smelting. 

One finds, indeed, in certain mining writings as well as at certain smelting works, instructions on how this or that should be added to the ores so that the aforementioned corrosive spirits might be "exhausted" and, as it were, fixed along with the metal. However, because the hoped-for effect does not always follow, people not only stop thinking about such methods, but they also abandon the path entirely and continue singing the same old song. Why is this? These good people perform such work in a purely mechanical way, or according to the custom of the trade. If the workings of Nature were better known to them, they would follow Nature more closely with their additives, roasting, and smelting, and would thus achieve something far more useful than has happened until now. 

Take, for example, common **sulfur** <note>original symbol: 🜍</note> and **mercury** <note>original symbol: ☿</note>; when these are melted together and afterwards **sublimated** <note>original symbol: ♁irt</note>, they yield a beautiful **cinnabar** <term>cinnabar: a bright red mineral (mercury sulfide) used as a pigment and the primary ore of mercury</term>. This the **chemists** <note>original: Chymici</note> call "mercury bound by sulfur." But we ask: is the mercury bound by the sulfur, or the sulfur by the mercury? In truth, you good people are mistaken, for we wish to convince you through the properties of sulfur that it is **mercury** alone and only that can, as it were, bind the sulfur. For you cannot in any way deny that the burning nature of sulfur cannot be taken away (unless you kill and destroy it entirely), no matter how foolishly you approach it—whether by **sublimation** <note>original symbol: ♁iren</note>, distillation, or whatever all those foolish things are called—its burning property remains. But if one has turned it into cinnabar with **mercury**, its burning and igniting nature is significantly subdued without any destruction or "killing," as is clearly evident in the cinnabar. Must you not, unless you wish to call white black and black white, without—

# On the Nature, Utility, and Use of Earthly Sulfur.

...[one must] admit that both **sulfur** <note>original symbol: 🜍</note> binds the **mercury** <note>original symbol: ☿</note>, and especially that the latter binds the former? From this, you can now understand what we do not intend to describe so specifically here—namely, what both **sulfur** <note>original symbol: 🜍</note> and **mercury** <note>original symbol: ☿</note> lack, such that they do not become perfect metals. In **cinnabar** <term>cinnabar: a toxic red sulfide of mercury, the primary ore from which mercury is extracted</term> they only achieve a likeness of metal in its form, and only something that, as it were, allows itself to be hammered. We could provide another and clearer comparison through the example of **glass**; however, to go further into this would be too extensive, so let it remain with the first comparison. Meanwhile, the lover of glass-making can diligently reflect upon its composition and structure.

**§. 11.** Common **mercury** <note>original symbol: ☿</note> is still of an all too coarse and **salty** <note>original symbol: 🜔</note> watery property; therefore, it can do nothing more with **sulfur** <note>original symbol: 🜍</note> than to contract or coagulate it, and to lock up its inflammatory power. But if one knows how to give this **cinnabar** another and much nobler **mercury** <note>original symbol: ☿</note>, and to unite it with the same—which can happen quite easily—then one will find an artificial (we will not quite say **philosophical**) **mercury** <note>original symbol: ☿</note> of no small utility to those who know it. Only let one not be mistaken, nor let oneself be led astray by the **cinnabar-work** of deceptive **recipe-peddlers** <note>original: "Process-Krämer" — refers to charlatans who sold fake alchemical procedures</note>.

**§. 12.** Let no one think, however, that the aforementioned humble comparisons were only cited simply regarding **sulfur** <note>original symbol: 🜍</note>, **mercury** <note>original symbol: ☿</note>, **cinnabar**, and the like. Rather, all of this aims at something higher. Whoever does not wish to understand from this how to improve the old, useless traditions in the greatest roasting and smelting processes will never be able to be helped. **Pyrite** <note>original: "Kieß"</note> clings to almost all ores, which is a **sulfur** <note>original symbol: 🜍</note>; but if the ores are not sulfurous or pyritic, then another **realgar-like** <term>realgar-like: containing arsenic disulfide, often appearing as a ruby-red mineral</term> nature clings to them, such as white or red **smelter-smoke** <term>smelter-smoke: "Hütten-Rauch," a historical term for arsenic trioxide vapors that condense in furnace chimneys</term>, **tutty** <term>tutty: "Tutia," an impure form of zinc oxide collected from smelting furnaces</term>, etc. **Copper** <note>original symbol: ♀</note> ores generally have the most **sulfur** <note>original symbol: 🜍</note>; **iron** <note>original symbol: ♂</note> ore has less, unless it is very pyritic; on the other hand, **silver** <note>original symbol: ☽</note>, **tin** <note>original symbol: ♃</note>, and **lead** <note>original symbol: ♄</note> are more **mercurial** in nature.

**§. 13.** In the preceding §. 10, we mentioned something of the effect of **mercury** <note>original symbol: ☿</note> upon **sulfur** <note>original symbol: 🜍</note>, about which we could still cite much that is useful on this occasion. However, because it would make this work too extensive, we must pass over it for now. We take the **sulfur** <note>original symbol: 🜍</note> back into hand and say that when one **calcines** <term>calcines: "verzundert," the process of heating a metal until it oxidizes and turns into a crumbly scale or powder</term> **gold** <note>original symbol: ☉</note> and **silver** <note>original symbol: ☽</note> with it in a certain way, one can bring these fixed metals, through repeated labor, to the point where their dust dissolves in every **liquid** <note>original: "Liquore"</note>. Such a thing is not to be rejected in **medicine**. And this powder—provided one has worked correctly—cannot be brought back [to its metallic state] because the **calcination** has taken away the noble **mercury** <note>original symbol: ☿</note> of these metals, and only their **mercurial-sulfurous** essence remains. This is why these powders are so easily dissolved in all fluid substances. What the **sulfur** <note>original symbol: 🜍</note>...

### The Third Chapter.

...causes harm to **silver** <note>original symbol: ☽</note> is known to everyone; but what a certain **sulfur** <note>original symbol: 🜍</note>, which nature has merely coagulated in common **water** <note>original symbol: ▽</note>, is capable of when paired with fine **gold** <note>original symbol: ☉</note>, and how it transforms that **gold** <note>original symbol: ☉</note> into an excellent red **salt** <note>original symbol: 🜔</note>, is not known to everyone. Nor will every person find this **sulfur** <note>original symbol: 🜍</note>, which is here named contrary to the common order.

**§. 14.** In the first part concerning **gold** <note>original symbol: ☉</note>, we mentioned **pebble-stones** <term>Kießling-Steine: likely referring to quartz pebbles or pyritic stones found in riverbeds</term>; we must mention them again briefly here, though without describing their different varieties, as that would be impossible. Their wonderful generation was already discussed in the first part on **gold** <note>original symbol: ☉</note>; here we only wish to mention those stones that one often encounters in very high mountains, which are frequently composed of many thousands of small, multicolored pebbles. Thousands of people see this, but the smallest fraction of them understands the cause. We do not wish to cite what various **authors** <note>original: "Auctoribus"</note> have reported on this here and there.

Whoever knows the cause of the earth's solidity, and why **bricks** (though they are often fired from entirely black earth) become so beautifully red through **fire** <note>original symbol: △</note>, will also easily understand the cause of the clumping together of so many small pebbles in coarse sand, or often in a whitish, loamy earth. In particular, they will understand why the **sulfur** <note>original symbol: 🜍</note> of **gold** <note>original symbol: ☉</note> is coagulated into such a deep red. The craft of **soap-boiling** shows us how, through an alkaline lye, all fat (which at its core is nothing but a pure **sulfur** <note>original symbol: 🜍</note>) curdles together and becomes a hard soap.

This irrefutable mechanical proof should overturn many a person's whimsical **Physical Principles** <note>original: "Principia Physica"</note> and point them toward the true foundation of nature. However, imagination—especially that bred by supposed high scholarship—is an incurable evil. Just as one sees daily among **fools** <note>original: "Thoren," referring to the mentally ill or "deluded" in a historical context</note> who imagine they are this or that person, so it goes with most people regarding their once-formed opinions. 

Yet we say once more: this simple and humble analogy of **soap-boiling** holds more depth than many are able to imagine. If many understood what we have pointed to here, the poor **ores** would not be treated so "executioner-like" <note>original: "henckermäßig," meaning brutally or destructively</note> at the **smelting works**; instead, one would learn to better understand the **fluxes** <term>Zuschläge: materials added to ore to lower the melting point and help separate the metal</term>. 

But at this point, many poor simpletons will immediately grin at us and mockingly ask where they are supposed to obtain all the **gold** <note>original symbol: ☉</note> and **lead** <note>original symbol: ♄</note> to assist the sulfurous, light ores (according to their delusion of our teaching)? But not so fast to the turning point, you poor little creatures! Only the shepherd knows how to lead you to the necessary **fodder** <note>original: "Aetzung"</note>, for not everything that is green is good grazing for you. Analogies indeed suggest the matter, but they are not the matter itself—a principle that many **theologians** <note>original: "Gottes-Gelehrten"</note> should likewise find most necessary to observe.

->### On the Nature, Use, and Utility of Earthly Sulfur.<-

There is a great difference between the shadow and the essence. Learn to know nature and its produced species <note>original: "Species," referring here to the different outward forms or varieties of natural substances</note> well; then you will rightly understand what we are pointing toward, for your own honor and the benefit of your neighbor.

§. 15. That common **sulfur** <note>original symbol: 🜍</note> cannot be easily dissolved by any liquid essence is known to almost everyone; but that one can easily and completely dissolve it into a red juice in a lye which has been sharpened to the highest degree by **lime** <term>Kalck: quicklime or calcium oxide, used here to create a highly caustic alkaline solution</term> (one will surely understand what we are speaking of), and afterward, through a certain **solvent** <note>original: "Menstruum"</note>, draw a tincture or balsam from this solution—this is not quite so common. This is provided that one knows the right lye, as well as the **solvent** <note>original: "Menstruum"</note>, which in no way wishes to unite or mix with the lye; if so, this balsam is easy to prepare. And if one further brings this to the thickness of honey, and then further cooks or **cements** <term>cementirt: a process of heating a metal in contact with powdered reagents to alter its properties</term> a volatile **silver** <note>original symbol: ☽</note> therein according to the degrees of nature—or whatever else one wishes to call it according to the **art of gold-making** <note>alchemy</note>—one might hope for no small pleasure from this work. What then would the heavenly, wondrous **sulfur** <note>original symbol: 🜍</note> described above in Chapter II not accomplish, if a true artist proceeded with it according to the simple path of nature? However, know this: if you do not know how to well-prepare the aforementioned volatile **silver** <note>original symbol: ☽</note> and how to make it corporeal again after the cooking, you will have nothing but loss from it. Now, he who knows the art, let him not betray the master, lest both fall into contempt; for while this work is in itself simple and modest, it nonetheless has something great behind it, only that this work requires a long time and patience.

§. 16. If we had the desire to make ourselves known through **process-writing** <term>Proceß-Schreiben: the practice of publishing specific, step-by-step alchemical recipes</term>, we would here describe a work with **sulfur** <note>original symbol: 🜍</note>: namely, how the same is to be entirely dissolved in a certain oil (though it stinks like hell), and then how to draw it out of this oil again through a certain lye, so that all its slimy, stinking impurity remains behind in the oil; then further: how to draw an excellent tincture out of this lye through a noble **solvent** <note>original: "Menstruum"</note>? However, as already mentioned, **process-writing** is not our way; enough has already been said to one experienced in **sulfur** <note>original symbol: 🜍</note>. But to others, who think they have "already smelled this pepper" <note>a German idiom meaning they think they are already experienced or clever enough to understand the trick</note>, we assure them that they will hardly reach this little side-stream without a faithful guide, as such a thing may be called by many different names, yet quite clearly, even if it is not understandable to just anyone.
