# Of the Nature, Utility, and Use of Earthly Sulfur.

Soot (which, because it is a **Sulfur** <note>original symbol: △; here referring to the flammable principle</note> that is very harmful to ores, seems somewhat absurd) works wonders with volatile ores, the cause of which one experienced in nature will easily grasp; but he who does not understand the correct practice with soot should leave it be, unless he wishes to carry away harm, shame, mockery, and scorn instead of benefit. The closest relative of chimney-soot likewise does its part with volatile ores, provided one knows how to help the one as well as the other with their necessary mercuriality. But enough of this, as we do not wish to act as a smelter here, though we must still remember that common **Sulfur** <note>original symbol: △</note> is able to increase **Copper** <note>original symbol: ♀</note> in a certain way, namely when one uses a quarter-pound (1 part) of **Sulfur** <note>original symbol: △</note>, the **Copper** <note>original symbol: ♀</note> then becomes a stone <note>matte; an intermediate product in smelting</note> with half of the **Sulfur** <note>original symbol: △</note>, which, after it has first been made black through right science and then further into copper, will show that the **Copper** <note>original symbol: ♀</note> has received a considerable increase from the **Sulfur** <note>original symbol: △</note>: and this work can give a seeker much useful information.

§. 19. Above in §. 13 we considered the transformation <note>literally "wonderment"</note> of **Gold** <note>original symbol: ☉</note> and **Silver** <note>original symbol: ☽</note>: now we wish to consider **Antimony** <note>original symbol: ♁</note> with only a few words. When one calcines it <note>verzundert: heating to form a scale or oxide</note>, its combustible **Sulfur** <note>original symbol: △</note> departs with the **Mercury** <note>original symbol: ☿</note>, which is the cause of the emetic power <note>original: "vis emetic:" – the property that induces vomiting</note> of **Antimony** <note>original symbol: ♁</note>, and its golden **Sulfur** <note>original symbol: △</note> remains alone; what is now to be performed with the same in the **Fire** <note>original symbol: △</note> (especially if one knows how to catch its combustible **Sulfur** together with the **Mercury** during calcination), namely when it is reunited with its separated parts after they have been washed by the **Antimony's** <note>original symbol: ♁</note> own vinegar—of this we wish to say nothing now, because the vinegar of **Antimony** <note>original symbol: ♁</note> is required for it, the preparation of which is not known to everyone.

§. 20. However, **Antimony** <note>original symbol: ♁</note> is not alone endowed with a noble **Sulfur** <note>original symbol: △</note>, but **Iron** <note>original symbol: ♂</note> also has an excellent and fairly fixed **Sulfur** <note>original symbol: △</note>, and almost the most of its substance consists of this; of its **Mercury** <note>original symbol: ☿</note> there is very little, but of **Copper** <note>original symbol: ♀</note> it has somewhat more. Now, the **Sulfur of Iron** <note>original symbol: △ ♂</note> is of excellent quality, both in medicine and in alchemy. ### On the Nature, Utility, and Use of Earthly Sulfur.

§. 27. From a pure ore of Venus <term>Minera Veneris</term> <note>Latin for copper ore; in alchemy, the planet Venus is associated with the metal copper.</note>, one can also prepare a balsam through distillation that is not to be rejected. However, one must know how to properly prepare the copper ore so that it can release this balsam during distillation. In this way, an oil or balsam can be distilled from all ores, and these can rightfully be called "just" or "pure." This occurs when they are soaked and doused—without any foreign substance—only with the Water <term>$\nabla$</term> <note>The downward-pointing triangle is the alchemical symbol for the element of Water.</note> from Eden. This must be understood correctly, as it is easy to be deceived in this matter; only as much should be used as is necessary for their softening and putrefaction <note>"Putrefaction" in alchemy refers to the breaking down of a substance to release its inner essence.</note>. We already foresee that many will turn up their noses at this and the preceding section; however, we shall have to laugh at them, as we are more than well-assured that all of this will not be understood by just anyone. Those, however, who have walked not on the deceptive paths of the sophists, but on the path of Nature, will be able to understand all of this perfectly, as it is described for them more than clearly and brightly. Whoever has prepared these oils of the metals in this way will be able to perform something extraordinary, not only in the animal kingdom but also in the mineral kingdom.

§. 28. We will now pass over the Fire <term>$\triangle$</term> <note>The upward-pointing triangle is the alchemical symbol for Fire.</note> of the remaining metals and minerals, as we believe enough has already been said to the lovers of truth in the preceding sections. Nevertheless, we do not wish to leave the mineral kingdom entirely; rather, we wish to turn a little toward the oils—though not strictly to the mineral oils. Instead, we shall take as our object that vegetable wonder, Salt <term>$\ominus$</term> of Tartar <term>Tartarum</term> <note>Tartar is the potassium bitartrate crust found in wine barrels; alchemists considered it a "middle salt" connecting the plant and mineral worlds.</note>, which can rightfully be called a middle salt of the vegetable and mineral kingdoms. Even the peasants know that Tartar is a salt. We are not speaking of its salty substance here, as that has already been addressed elsewhere; rather, we wish to speak only of the Fire <term>$\triangle$</term> of Antimony <term>$\unicode{x2641}$</term>. All laboratory workers know that Tartar gives off a great deal of stinking oil during distillation. This, however, is far from being the secret Fire <term>$\triangle$</term> at which we are aiming here. ### Chapter Three.

[Crea]tures are simply composed of the elements or secondary principles proportionally according to their kind; such as the fish and all feathered fowl from the element of water; all animals, cattle, and creeping things from the earth. Thus, they actually have no part in the darkness, except in so far as man, through his Fall, brought the curse upon all nature—yet drew damnation alone upon himself. Therefore, man possesses far more of the principles of darkness and damnation than any other creature. On the other hand, within this shell of darkness, damnation, and corruption, man also possesses—above all other creatures—the noble heavenly jewel: spirit, soul, and body from Eden (namely, dust from the earth) locked away within. 

Therefore, the flesh and blood of a man united with **GOD** is, through heavenly radiation, much more glorious, excellent, and useful than that of a man walking according to the principles of darkness and the impulse of **Satan**. We see a likeness in the glorious radiance of **Moses**, when he remained with **GOD** the **Lord** on Mount **Sinai** for forty days and nights; no human eye could endure his magnificent glow, even though he had not yet laid aside his elementary essence and still required food and drink like all other men. 

Furthermore, we see that the dead bones of that excellent man of **God**, **Elisha**, still worked wonders and revived a deceased man (*2 Kings 13:21*); this serves as a magnificent prototype showing that the death of **Jesus Christ** shall give life again to all those who have "fallen asleep" in a state of blessedness. 

On the contrary, it is of a completely different nature with the possessed man in the land of the **Gadarenes** (*Mark 5*), who dwelt only in the stinking, unclean tombs, led a loathsome, desolate, and dark life, and was a dwelling place for a legion of devils. His flesh and blood—before redemption through **Jesus Christ**—would have been highly harmful and dangerous to the body and soul of another person. This fact is well known to all sorcerers, who carry out their sorceries upon men and livestock through such devilish <term>mumial</term> subjects <note>The term "Mumia" in alchemical medicine refers to the vital life-force or "balsam" residing in the physical body. It was believed this essence could be extracted or manipulated for both healing and, as mentioned here, dark magic.</note>. These victims can in no way be healed except through pure, true <term>Divine Magic</term> <note>In this context, Divine Magic refers to "Theurgia" or spiritual alchemy—the use of divine power and natural laws for healing, contrasted against "Goetia" or black magic.</note>. For such healing, something <term>mumial</term> is specifically required from certain people, through which the harm inflicted can be turned back upon the head of the sorcerer. Even **Satan**, with all his cunning, cannot prevent this, provided one well understands the "fire of judgment" and the human <term>Mumia</term>—though this is a secret that, for certain reasons, cannot and will not be disclosed here.

Colors have no such internal light, therefore [according to Descartes] they are not essential colors, but only an appearance-essence based on the disposition of the parts of their <term>object</term> <note>original: "Vorwurfs"; in this context, the physical substrate or material upon which color appears</note>.

Is that not a fine way to philosophize? Had the good Lord Professor properly considered the difference between an indwelling light and the dark body of a color, he would not have philosophized such silly stuff with *Descartes* <note>original: "Cartesio"</note> against the nature of the distinctness of things. Let the sunbeams fall through a glass *prism* onto various boards—white, red, black—and the appearing rainbow colors of the prism will in no way be able to change the essential colors of these boards. Thus, a great distinction is to be made between something that merely appears and something that is actual or essential.

But the aforementioned <term>Professor of Mathematics</term> <note>Referring again to Descartes</note> thinks he has brought a peculiar proof of his proposition when he says: if colors were something essential, they would also have to shine in the dark. But should a philosopher reason thus? How many innumerable things are there in nature that do not shine in the dark? Are they then not those very things until the $\odot$ <note>The astronomical symbol for the Sun</note> or another light illuminates them? Are these not conclusions that must be drawn according to such philosophy filled with empty wind?

A juice from a herb, let it be colored however it may, when applied to different objects—hard, soft, porous, or dense—will retain the same color on all of them, regardless of the different disposition of their parts, however the sun may shine upon them. And who would let themselves be persuaded by the most subtle philosophy of *Aristotle* or *Descartes* that in spring the green leaves of a tree, and the peach and cherry blossoms, are green, purple-colored, and white only during the day because of the sunbeams, and were not the very same at night? Truly, one could go mad over such subtle "study-closet philosophy" lacking true knowledge of the origins of natural things. Yet, it is herewith sufficiently proven that colors, both by day and by night, are something essential, and not merely something appearing according to the condition of the parts in the visible object. §. 16. In connection with the recently cited text from Luke, it would not be absurd to make some mention of the dispute between the two Protestant <note>original: *evangelischen*—at this time referring to the Lutheran and Reformed (Calvinist) churches</note> churches, since the one comes quite close to Transubstantiation <note>the Catholic doctrine that bread and wine turn into the actual substance of Christ's body and blood</note>, while the other, on the contrary, goes a bit too far in the opposite direction. Now, the former wishes to maintain that the Lord Christ, through the omnipotence of His divinity, stepped into the midst of His disciples through the closed door which was opened to Him; they do this so that their doctrine of "in, with, and under" <note>original Latin: *in cum & sub*—referring to the Lutheran view that Christ's body is present alongside the bread and wine</note> might be better defended. They do not consider that there is a very great difference—in terms of movement and effect—between a spirit and a glorified body, such as the Lord Christ had at that time. To present this somewhat understandably through a comparison, take a good <term>🜎</term> <gloss>Sal Ammoniac</gloss> <note>a salt used in alchemy, ammonium chloride</note> and prepare from it a perfectly rectified spirit, and from the remaining <term>🜔</term> <gloss>Dead Head</gloss> <note>original Latin: *Caput Mortuum*—the useless residue left after distillation</note>, according to the art, a pure, clear glass, as an image of our glorified, translucent body. Fill this glass with its spirit, but leave it unsealed; then place this glass into another glass or vessel, merely tied at the top with paper. You will then actually find that the volatile spirit will gradually evaporate, but its transparent body (namely the glass) in which it was poured cannot penetrate through in the same way. This comparison is indeed taken from a spirit and a body that are quite coarse and far too material when compared to the heavenly ones; nevertheless, an enlightened eye will be able to see into the true mystery through this.

§. 17. That the Lord Christ already had a glorified body at that time is something no upright theologian would doubt; otherwise (unless his brain is displaced by a stubborn prejudice), he would be made to blush with shame by the passages in Mark 16:19 and Acts 1:9. Nevertheless, the Lord Christ says to His disciples, when they were of the opinion that it was a spirit: "Touch me and look at me well; for a spirit has not flesh and bone, as you see that I have." From this it is indeed incontrovertible that even a glorified body remains tangible, and consequently also requires a certain place according to its entire extension and dimension; otherwise one would have to claim, contrary to St. Paul's clear words, that Christ was not yet glorified at that time. However, how false this is the Apostle declares irrefutably in 1 Corinthians 15:42, which is also indicated by what Christ says in John 17:5 in His Passion sermon. Those good gentlemen would not need to fabricate such a strange "penetration through closed doors" for the body of our Savior if they would only wipe the dust of the schools <note>referring to academic scholasticism</note> from their eyes and consider the passages in Luke 24:16 and John 21:4 without their usual damaging logical arts.

§. 18. Otherwise, they would have answered their opponents with weapons quite different from **Scholastic Theology**—namely, with its syllogisms, distinctions, definitions, exceptions, and whatever other quackeries may belong to the useless grandstanding of the learned. The fact that the greater part of the Reformed gentlemen denies the appearance of spirits and ghosts clearly proves that they know how to do violence to the Scriptures just as much as their opponents do. They treat the Bible like a **wax nose** <note>A common 17th-century idiom meaning something that can be twisted or shaped to fit any argument</note> that must be turned and bent to support their own wisdom (which is merely cobbled together through human art). One side ascribes too much to the words of Holy Scripture, adding things that—according to spirit and truth—will never be found therein. The other side, however, through overly refined figures of speech, takes away the essential power of those words. This is caused by nothing other than the stubbornness of their imagined wisdom and the prestige and authority of their predecessors. The first group was sufficiently answered in the preceding Sections 16 and 17. The others, meanwhile, might do well to consider the words of Christ in John 6:32, 33, and further in verses 48 to 51, and from 53 to 58. For these were too coarse and irrational thoughts, to the shame of the Majesty of Jesus Christ. To completely remove such irrational thoughts from them, Christ the Lord says in the aforementioned chapter, verses 62 and 63: *What if you then see the Son of Man ascend to where He was before?* This is as if He wanted to say: from this you shall surely recognize that I am not speaking to you about the eating of this flesh of mine, when you see that I shall leave this world again and ascend back to where I came from, and [give] you my flesh for your imagined...

# The Fourth Chapter. #
### 254 ###

...physical consumption here below, as the following verse clearly explains, where Christ speaks: *It is the Spirit who gives life; the flesh profits nothing. The words that I speak to you, they are life.* <note>John 6:63</note> From this—and the previously mentioned description of a spiritual body, which, due to its limited extension, requires a certain place and therefore, contrary to the essence of independent existence, cannot be multiplied out of its unity so that it could be present and eaten in many thousands of specific places at once, even on a single Sunday—it clearly and undeniably follows that everything which even remotely tastes of **Transubstantiation** <term>Transubstantiation: The doctrine that the bread and wine of the Eucharist are changed in substance into the actual body and blood of Christ, a view the author rejects as "fabricated."</term> is a vain, fabricated entity. 

But that Christ the Lord truly gives Himself to our spirit, soul, and eternal body, according to His heavenly humanity (Oh, what an arch-heretical way of speaking! will be shouted here; why? because the glory and majesty of God in Christ Jesus has not yet been properly recognized), as food, is undeniably stated in verses 32 and 33 of John 6, which read: *Moses did not give you the bread from heaven; but my Father gives you the true bread from heaven; for the bread of God is He who came down from heaven and gives life to the world.* <note>John 6:32–33</note> 

However, how this occurs remains hidden from us in this mortality as a divine mystery, until we shall one day lie at the table with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob in the kingdom of heaven. In the meantime, we are instructed by Christ simply to believe this without the man-made transformation of bread and wine, as He says in John 6:54: *Whoever eats my flesh and drinks my blood has eternal life:* and previously in verse 47: *Amen, Amen, I say to you: whoever believes in me has eternal life;* and verse 48: *I am the bread of life.* With this, we now turn back to our intended purpose.

§. 19. We have proven the difference between the abodes <note>original: "Behältnisse," referring to the various places or states where souls reside after death</note> of man after his death in the preceding 10th and 11th sections, and in the 12th, 13th, and 14th sections from the New Testament, that there truly are ghosts or spirits <note>original: "Gespenster oder Geister"</note> that appear to living people; furthermore, that a glorified body has its specific dimension and extension, and therefore also requires a certain space or place according to it, and consequently is also comprehensible, as is undeniably evident through the most holy body of Jesus Christ which rose from the dead. This being firmly established, the question now is: what then is a ghost or spirit (for these are taken here as synonymous words) according to its substance and essence? Furthermore, how can they appear in certain places, as well as at a certain fixed time?

# On the State of Man After His Death #
### 255 ###

...to imagine the nature of a spirit than that which Christ the Lord Himself gave us when He said to His fearful disciples in Luke 24:39:
> **Look at my hands and my feet, for it is I myself; touch me and behold me well; NB: for a spirit does not have flesh or bones, as you see that I have.**

If, therefore, a spirit has no flesh or bones, it is not a composite being but a most simple essence that cannot be seen or observed with any physical eye (do not be too hasty in judging these last words until we have first said more), "no more than an evaporating <term>rectified volatile spirit</term> <note>original: "Spirit. Volatil. rectif." — an alchemical term for a highly purified, fast-evaporating substance</note> which, however, before it evaporates or flies away, may be quite properly observed or seen in its body or etheric <term>vehicle</term> <note>original: "Vehiculo" — referring to a "spirit-body" or carrier that allows the soul to interact with the physical world</note>. (Our meaning here must be well understood, otherwise quarrelsome fools will find cause for conflict.) A spirit is intelligent, singular, subtle, nimble, and faster than our thoughts, penetrating everywhere, bright, pure, clear, inviolable, and invisible to physical eyes in and of itself. Accordingly, when an angel appeared, he took upon himself a body from the <term>Ether</term> <note>original: "Æthereo" — the "fifth element" or the substance of the heavens</note> according to his measure and figure; otherwise, he would have been unbearable to physical eyes in his angelic independence. The same applies to the appearance of devils, not that they, like angels, may take upon themselves a perfect body from the purest ether, but rather from coarse elementary vapors, and even then, imperfectly and deficiently; thus, a devil cannot take on a perfect human form, but it has always been found mixed with the limbs of cruel animals, according to the ideas of this animal world. This is because Satan, through his fall, was cast out from the circle of all spiritual and physical creatures; thus, in and of himself, he no longer possesses the slightest form of any heavenly or earthly creature, but according to his devilish form and essence, as the center of God's wrath and of dark, cold fury, he is unbearable to all creatures.

§. 21. From what has been said until now, one will more easily grasp the appearance of ghosts (or spirits); not that they take on a body which they then abandon after the appearance, as angels do, but rather they have and retain—as mentioned above—a <term>volatile rectified spirit</term> <note>original: "Spir. rectific."</note>, an <term>etheric vehicle</term> <note>original: "Vehiculum"</note> (or whatever else the school-philosophers, puffed up with empty words, might prefer to call it), as the bond by which our spirit and soul are so firmly and—outside of death—so inseparably linked with our body. And this is the true reason why a ghost of the departed may be seen by us. But why they appear, and often in the clothing in which they walked during their lives, shall now be explained.

# The Fourth Chapter #

§. 22. Regarding this question: why do ghosts or spirits appear in certain places and only at a certain time? (For we are not speaking here of those ghosts mentioned in the <term>Book of Wisdom</term> <note>original: "Buch der Weisheit" — also known as the Wisdom of Solomon, a deuterocanonical book of the Bible</note> 17:3, 4, 15; where verse 4 says: *And mournful ghosts with hideous faces appeared to them etc.* verse 6: *But there appeared to them a self-burning fire <note>The symbol $\triangle$ is the alchemical shorthand for the element of fire.</note>, full of dread: then they were terrified by that same ghost, which they could not bear to look upon, and considered that which they saw to be worse than it was.*) Therefore, before we prove this, it is necessary to speak of the independent reality of true faith—not, however, as it is described in the schools. Paul describes faith in Hebrews 11:1 thus: *Now faith is the foundation of things hoped for, and an evidence of things not seen.* And Paul cites many mighty effects of this faith throughout this whole chapter, and NB. in verse 27 he says: *By faith he (Moses) left Egypt, and feared not the king's wrath, for he held fast, as one who saw the Invisible.* verse 32: *And what more shall I say?* verse 33. NB. *Who through faith conquered kingdoms, practiced righteousness, obtained the promises, stopped the mouths of lions.* verse 34. *Extinguished the power of fire <note>original symbol: $\triangle$</note>, and the edge of the sword; were made strong out of weakness, became valiant in battle, turned to flight the armies of the foreigners etc.* Thus, according to Paul's teaching, faith is a firm assurance within a person of that which he does not see or has not seen; or a true <term>impression of the imagination</term> <note>original: "impressio imaginationis"</note> of those things that are not seen, as if they were truly and actually being seen. A blind man does not see the sun with his physical eyes, yet he is entirely assured through his <term>imaginative power</term> <note>original: "per vim imaginativam"</note> that it illuminates the day, just as if he saw it physically. A covered concave mirror cannot receive the sun's rays and reflect them back; it is exactly the same with our souls and <term>minds</term> <note>original: "Gemüth" — referring to the seat of emotions, will, and spiritual thought</note>, namely that as long as a person does not cast out and banish everything earthly from himself, the Holy Spirit cannot work, nor can the person reflect his <term>Imagination</term> back into God—that is, he cannot believe.

§. 23. Our <term>Imagination</term> <note>In this context, "Imagination" is not mere fantasy, but a creative spiritual faculty that "images" or gives form to spiritual truths.</note> is nothing other than a radiation of our mind (namely of the spirit and the soul) onto this or that thing, through which radiation the object is grasped according to its entire substance, and is imprinted and embodied in our mind. From this, the person receives a perfect assurance of the essence of the object, that it is thus and not otherwise: for those things which can be seen and felt by us, and thus judged according to these senses, require

# Of the State of Man after his Death. #

...of faith: thus one must not believe that an oak tree is a <term>bratwurst</term> <note>The author uses this humorous, earthy example to show that faith must be grounded in the nature of the object, not just fancy.</note>, even if the most subtle philosopher could prove such from the armory of his excellent <term>syllogism-making</term> <note>original: "Schlußmachery"—a pejorative term for logical hair-splitting or overly complex academic reasoning</note>; for the difference in the nature of these two objects shows tangibly that it is not true.

§. 24. Regarding true faith, however, and spiritual *imagination* <note>In this 17th-century context, "imagination" refers to a creative and perceptive faculty of the soul, rather than just "making things up."</note> and the radiance upon spiritual things, it is of the aforementioned quality, with the difference that here the *imagination* is often led and guided toward invisible things through visible ones. Therefore Paul says quite clearly in *Romans 1:20*: *For since the creation of the world, his invisible attributes are perceived and seen in the things that are made, namely his eternal power and Godhead, so that they have no excuse.* Furthermore, the circumstances of a matter also guide our imagination or faith, so that one can be assured and certain of this or that; *that is*, one can believe it. Thus we firmly believe that the <term>Great Mogul</term> <note>The Mughal Emperor of India, a common 17th-century example of a distant but real power.</note> in India must be a rational human and not an elephant, though we have never seen him; this is because humans are governed by humans and not by irrational animals. Since we are bound to believe this firmly according to the circumstances, we simultaneously form an image of his great power, splendor, and glory, etc. On the other hand, our imagination cannot possibly comprehend, *that is*, believe, that the surface of the great world-ocean, like our earth, is divided into mighty kingdoms, principalities, and lordships, inhabited by various peoples and ruled by powerful <term>potentates</term> <note>original: "Potentaten" — rulers or monarchs</note>; because this runs contrary to the nature of this *element*. Therefore, faith is founded solely upon those invisible things that actually and truly are, and yet shall be—namely, that such things are grasped through the rays of our *imagination* and imprint a perfect image upon our spirit and soul, so that we need no longer have the slightest doubt in the matter. That is then called believing firmly; and thus faith is nothing other than a firm grasping of invisible things through our *imagination*, or an impression made by a strong mental image. But the more a person’s *imagination* is filled and veiled with vanity, the less it will be capable of radiating into spiritual things, and through such radiation, sinking into them and uniting with them inseparably. Therefore, a godless person does not believe in the righteous vengeance and the strict judgment of GOD, because his *imagination* only radiates into sinful vanities, as <term>originated</term> <note>original: "geurständet" — a term likely from the mystic Jakob Böhme, meaning "having its source or origin in"</note> by the devil, and thereby mixes itself with *Satan*; whereas a pious person sinks with his whole *imagination* into GOD as the original source of all perfect joy, peace, rest, and eternal delight of the soul—that is, he perfectly believes in the Almighty GOD as He reveals Himself in His Word

### The Fourth Chapter. ###

...and works he has revealed. And so, after death, each person is drawn by the rays of their <term>Imagination</term> <note>In the 17th-century sense, "Imagination" is a formative, spiritual power that shapes reality, not just idle daydreaming.</note>, as if by a powerful magnet, to wherever they had focused their imagination during their life. There, the same occurs as is written in *Revelation 14:13*: *For their works follow them.* That is to say, the works performed by each person during their life will follow them in death as undeniable witnesses and lead them to their deserved place, there to await the Final Judgment. The effects of our imagination are unsearchable and almost incomprehensible, as daily experience with pregnant women has taught. For what strange effects has their imagination, or the power of their mental image, not wrought upon the fruit of their bodies? Among other examples, one woman saw someone's hand being chopped off; whereupon she immediately gave birth to a child who was likewise missing a hand—as if it were freshly severed and still bleeding—yet the hand was found neither in the afterbirth nor in any other place. There are many more such terrifying and unbelievable examples, all of which would be impossible to recount. If it is now asked: did the child ever have the hand or not? Was it lost through the mother’s powerful impression of imagination? And where did it go? In short, the radiance directed toward this or that object is the power of our spirit and soul; whoever understands this well will be able to perform wonders in both true and false (or devilish) <term>Magic</term> <note>original: "Magia"</note>.

§. 25. That faith—whether for good or evil—consists of a powerful imagination is further proven by the fact that no human can imagine (that is, believe) a thing that has not existed from eternity, nor can exist in eternity. On the contrary, our imagination immediately imprints upon the mind an idea of every matter, whether spiritual or physical, as soon as we hear of it (provided it is something essential or capable of existing), even if the object is absent, so perfectly and firmly that we believe in it. This being established, we return again to the question: why do spirits or ghosts appear? For this, we must first remind the reader of what was said above regarding <term>Sheol</term> <note>The Hebrew term for the grave or the dwelling place of the dead.</note> and <term>Bor</term> <note>The Hebrew term for "the Pit," often used synonymously with the underworld or a state of spiritual depth.</note>; namely, that in every place, circle, or vessel, there are levels of joy or of mourning, depending on whether they are closer to or further from the <term>Streams of Belial</term> <note>A biblical reference (Psalm 18:4) to the "torrents of destruction" or the depths of the abyss.</note>. Study with all diligence the figure of the <term>Great Mystery</term> <note>original: "Mysterii magni"</note> (Fig. 9), as a diagram of great secrets. Furthermore, one must well consider that a person's journey into that world is not of the nature taught in the schools and from the pulpit—namely, going directly into perfect bliss to contemplate the majestic glory of God, or into the fiery pool in the streams of Belial. ### Concerning the State of Man After Death. ###

...in my Father's house are many rooms, etc. <note>original: "Vatters Hause sind viel Wohnungen 2c." Refers to John 14:2.</note> Namely: (1) The outer courts of the Lord, of which David speaks in the 84th Psalm; (2) Abraham’s Bosom; (3) Paradise; (4) The New Jerusalem; (5) The New Heaven and the New Earth; (6) Zion; (7) The Kingdom of God. Thus, Christ promises the thief in Luke 23:43 Paradise, though the thief had asked for the Kingdom—that is, the highest degree of blessedness. For although he "imagined" into Christ <note>The author uses "imagine" to mean a profound spiritual focusing or anchoring of the soul's essence.</note> and took hold of Him in faith, he did not yet possess the kind of preparation through earnest repentance that the justice of God requires, because he had spent his life in sheer wickedness until that very moment, as he himself confessed in verse 41 when he said to his companion: "for we receive what our deeds deserve," etc. But because he took hold of Christ through a powerful illumination of his Spirit and believed that He was the Son of God—who would not remain in death but could lead him out of it and free him from the anguish of Hell—Christ accepted him into grace. He promised to take him into Paradise as the third degree of rest, a place Christ himself intended to occupy until His victorious ascension above the highest heavens.

§. 26. In the Second Epistle to the Corinthians 12:2, St. Paul says he was "caught up to the third heaven, into Paradise." It does not follow from this that there are only three heavens or degrees of blessed rest; he merely says he was caught up *as far as* the third heaven, but did not reach the others, as is evident from the text. Furthermore, that dead boy whom Elijah raised, and the one who returned to life through the dead bones of Elisha in 2 Kings 13:21; likewise the dead man of Nain raised by Christ in Luke 7; the little daughter of the ruler of the synagogue in Luke 8; and Lazarus, called back from the grave in John 11; as well as Tabitha raised by Peter in Acts 9 and the youth Eutychus brought back to life by Paul in Acts 20—all of these, we say, had only reached the first degree of rest. They were in the first circles of the outer courts of the House of the Lord (Psalm 84 and 116), because their <term>Imagination</term> <note>Again, referring to the soul's formative power and spiritual focus.</note> or spiritual focus had reached no further. And of this the Book of Wisdom says in Chapter 3:1: "The souls of the righteous are in the hand of God, and no torment shall touch them." These all exist in a state of rest from which they cannot return to this world or the circles of darkness except by the power of God. (Therefore Abraham says to the rich man in Luke 16:26: "And besides all this, between us and you a great chasm has been fixed," etc.) This is because their <term>Imagination</term> (namely, their faith) was immersed in God and had united with Him.

# The Fourth Chapter. #

...[human things] clung to them at their death: the soul's anguish caused by the burden of sin indeed drove them toward Christ; however, the strict, constricting hardness of their **imagination** <note>In the mystical tradition of this period, "imagination" is not "make-believe," but the formative power of the soul's will—the "inner focus" that anchors the soul to a specific reality, whether earthly or divine.</note> pulled them toward this or that earthly thing. He snatched the prisoners of those enclosures from death and, after His victorious resurrection, led them in triumph into the outer courts of the Lord, into Abraham’s Bosom, and into Paradise.

Here we must go a little further and answer those learned theologians and their followers who, regarding the state of such souls, argue against the fundamental truths of Holy Scripture that we have presented thus far. They conclude that if (according to the premise of Holy Scripture) these souls were to attain rest and blessedness after their purification, such blessedness would then have to be credited to them not as grace, but as a merit <note>The author is refuting the idea that suffering in the afterlife "earns" salvation; he insists it is still a gift of Christ's grace.</note>. Well aimed, but wide of the mark! Outside of Christ and through faith in Christ, there is no rest or blessedness, neither in heaven nor on earth; this remains firm against all the power of hell and the devil. Since we have proven in all our writings that in those places after this life, the soul must break through via faith in Christ and thus become a partaker of His most holy blood and death, all blessedness—whether won through faith in Christ in this life or the next—is no merit of the sinful creature. Rather, it is a gift of grace through the most holy suffering and merit of Jesus Christ. # Chapter Four.

...and the 3rd section of this chapter. That the earthly or elemental body consists of <term>Salt</term> <note>represented by the symbol ⊖</note>, <term>Fire</term> <note>represented by the symbol △; often used here to represent the "Sulfur" or soul-principle</note>, and <term>Mercury</term> <note>represented by the symbol ☿</note> requires no proof for those who understand. The <term>Salt</term> is and remains the most solid and constant part in the dissolution of all created being; it refines itself in the <term>Fire</term> to become ever higher, more beautiful, and more transparent. Hidden within this earthly <term>Salt</term> is the supra-earthly heavenly <term>Salt</term>—the "dust from the earth" or the body that is indestructible for all eternity. However, this body cannot appear or be revealed until the Day of Resurrection, as Paul undeniably testifies in 1 Corinthians 15, where in verse 35 he raises the question:

> But someone might say: "How are the dead raised, and with what kind of body do they come?" Answer, v. 36: "You fool! what you sow does not come to life unless it dies. v. 37. And what you sow is not the body that is to be, but a bare grain," etc. v. 44. "It is sown a natural body, and it is raised a spiritual body."

There is a natural body, and there is also a spiritual body. These crystal-clear sayings <note>literally "sun-bright sayings"</note> require no explanation; rather, it is evident from them that within our natural, perishable body, a spiritual, imperishable body is also buried. This spiritual body—created from the spiritual elements or first principles—shall alone rise again, just as a grain of wheat placed in the earth does not emerge in its previous form, but pushes forth a body entirely unlike itself, as its stalk, ear, blossom, and fruit prove. But why must the glorious, imperishable body rest with the perishable one in the grave until its resurrection? This must be sought in the first man, Adam. Namely, because the whole Adam—and in him all his descendants (ideally) <note>meaning in their essential form or potentiality</note> in body and soul, and consequently also the inner spiritual body—sinned against God, the justice of God (which is entirely incomprehensible to us) required that this entire creature be subject to punishment.

§. 32. All the world knows that in every seed, only its smallest and most subtle part is necessary for reproduction; and when this part or germ is removed, the entire remaining body of the seed is of no use. One understands this even better in the process of growth. This physical body then rots and perishes completely, so that henceforth, for all eternity, no bean or acorn may ever again come from this cast-off body. Our body is of the same nature: namely, that within it, the spiritual body is so subtle and hidden that it cannot be seen or recognized by any physical eye, until the time when Christ the Lord, the Sun of Righteous-

### The Fourth Chapter.

...original source of all corruption <note>referring to the devil or the root of sin</note>, shall cease in its instruments and exist no more for eternity; instead, its instrument or the seduced part—namely, poor mankind—shall remain alone and suffer eternally. §. 34. Regarding the nature of the damned, incorruptible bodies, [arising] from the principles of darkness, this has already been somewhat touched upon in the preceding. This, then, in eternity, without the heavenly Fire <note>symbolized by △</note> of life or light, can never again be unlocked, separated from its accidental nature or foreign additions, elevated, and transfigured, but remains subject to the passion of the dark Hell-fire <note>symbolized by △</note> as long as these dregs and their rot retain a disposition or tinder suitable for burning. Of this, **Isaiah 30:33** says: *For the pit has been prepared since yesterday, indeed it is also prepared for kings; which the **Lord** has made deep and wide enough: and there are piles of wood, fire <note>symbolized by △</note>, and wood in abundance within; the breath of the **Lord** will kindle it like a stream of sulfur.* Or rather, both are dissolved back into their original state by the light-fiery <note>△</note> water <note>symbolized by ▽</note> of life.

That three distinct events are being asked about here by the Lord's disciples cannot be denied by any reasonable person—unless they have learned, through some **scholastic maneuver** <note>original: "Scholastischen Fechter-Streich," literally a "scholastic fencer's trick," referring to complex theological arguments used to obscure simple meanings</note>, to pull these questions apart or pack them together. ### The VII. Chapter.

## Of the Torment of the Damned.

->§. 1.<-

But in what will this torment and torture actually consist? Regarding this, there is much disputation, and many are of the opinion that because the devil is a completely spiritual substance, he cannot be harmed by any material fire; likewise, the godless—because Paul says in 1 Corinthians 15:44: *It is sown a natural body, and will rise a spiritual body* etc.—would not be able to feel any elemental fire. Now, regarding the opinion of the former: we have already reported in the first chapter, § 12, in what manner the devils and the godless will be tormented by this elemental and simultaneously spiritual fire, ignited by the breath of the Lord like a stream of sulfur (Isaiah 30:33 <note>The author references the "breath of the Lord" like a "stream of sulfur" from Isaiah 30:33 to explain how spiritual beings can be affected by a form of fire.</note>). This can be presented even more comprehensibly by the following analogy: if one were to put a proportionate amount of a highly <term>rectified spirit<gloss>a highly concentrated, volatile alcohol or essence</gloss></term> into a large globe, and at the same time build, or could build, a coal fire inside it, the heat and the power of the fire would distress, press, drive about, and expand the spirit everywhere within this sphere, yet it could never destroy it for all eternity. This is because destruction runs contrary to the nature of a spirit; thus, as long as the fire in this sphere has fuel to burn, the spirit locked within would be distressed and tortured.

### The Eighth Chapter.
XV.

...one would naturally wonder why people have so terribly erred regarding this Holy Revelation, if one did not clearly see the reasons: partly their zeal for their imagined religion, partly their prejudices, and partly that people have too often flattered themselves in their own self-conceit. Furthermore, they have not properly considered the division of this magnificent Revelation, and especially because all sects (or "religions," as they are called) harbor such conflicting opinions regarding the 1,000 years <note>original: *Apoc. XX.* refers to the Millennial Reign described in Revelation 20</note>. Consequently, those to whom the Spirit of God has granted some enlightenment in this matter have been persecuted as <term>arch-heretics</term> <note>A term for the "worst" kind of heretic, often used by the institutional church to justify the severe persecution of mystical or dissenting thinkers</note> even to this day, because this doctrine seemed to conflict with the established religious formulas of those "good people."

All named periods in the prophetic prophecies are hidden terms before their fulfillment, which Divine Wisdom has reserved for itself alone. They remain inscrutable until the appointed time, as is said in **Daniel 12:4**: *But you, Daniel, shut up these words, and seal this book until the appointed time; then many shall run through it, and knowledge shall be increased*; and in verse 9: *For these things are closed and sealed until the appointed time.* It is as Christ the Lord says in **Matthew 24:36**: *But of that day and hour no one knows, not even the angels in heaven, but my Father only*; and in **Mark 13:32**: *indeed, not even the Son.* For this reason, the following words from **2 Peter 1:20** <note>The original German text cites 1 Peter 1:20, but the quote corresponds to 2 Peter 1:20</note> should be considered with special attention: *But you should know this first, that no prophecy of Scripture is subject to one's own interpretation.*

According to **1 Corinthians 2**, *the Spirit of God searches all things, even the depths of God; so also no one knows what is in God except the Spirit of God* (verse 12), *so that we may know what has been given to us by God* (verse 13), *but with words taught by the Holy Spirit, comparing spiritual things with spiritual.*

# On the Revelation of Jesus Christ.

<margin>XV, XVI. etc.</margin>
Within this time, which is divided into seven parts, is contained everything that shall happen to the Church of Jesus Christ until the end of all time. It is evident from history that the seven congregations in Chapter II and III—namely those in Ephesus, Smyrna, Pergamum, Thyatira, Sardis, Philadelphia, and Laodicea—existed in Asia <note>Referring to the Roman province of Asia, modern-day Turkey</note> at that time and were afflicted with the decay mentioned therein. Generally, however, these are prefigured to Holy John as seven epochs of all congregations throughout certain times, and what would occur with them until the end.

§. 4. A beginning is made with the Angel of the congregation at Ephesus. This congregation is highly praised and lauded in Chapter II, verse 2, with these words: **I know your works** etc. verses 3 and 4: **but I have something against you, namely that you have left your first love** etc. Furthermore, this period includes the opening of the seal in Chapter VI, verse 2, namely the rider on the white horse with the bow and the crown, who went out to conquer and that he might conquer; just as many were conquered and became believers through the teaching of the Gospel in this period. Also fulfilled in this period is the trumpet of the first angel in Chapter VIII, verse 7, signifying the horrible persecution under the pagan Emperors until Constantine the Great, <note>Constantine I (reigned 306–337 AD), the first Roman emperor to convert to Christianity.</note> foreshadowed by the words: **Then there was hail and fire, mingled with blood, and it was thrown upon the earth, and a third part of the trees were burned up, and all green grass was burned up;** this indicates the multitude of martyrs, both among the teachers and the entire congregation. Thus, contained herein is the first Apostolic Church, when the pure teaching of Christ and his Apostles burned in the full △ <note>The triangle symbol △ was often used as shorthand for "fire" or "glow." original: "△ der Liebe" / "glow of love"</note> of love, as is evident from the histories. Because the cruel persecutions affected all congregations, they learned to pay heed to the Word through trials, and there was very little deviation from Apostolic purity until roughly the middle of this time—namely in the 2nd Century—when the overseers and elders in the congregations raised themselves up and usurped a ruling office. This occurred in Alexandria after the death of Mark, <note>Referring to Saint Mark the Evangelist, traditionally the founder of the Church of Alexandria.</note> where the overseers or bishops were gradually elevated above the other elders, whereas previously one was like the other, and thus they were equal. From this, jealousy arose; from jealousy, hatred; and from hatred, persecution and lack of love, and thus the beginning of the subsequent clergy or so-called <term>hierarchy</term> <note>The author views the transition from equal elders to a ranked priesthood as a spiritual decline.</note> was fathered. Therefore, Christ the Lord says: **you have left your first love, repent; if not, I will come and push your lampstand from its place;** namely, I will take my grace and Spirit from you. In this regard, it is also praised that they hated the works of the Nicolaitans; <note>An early Christian sect mentioned in Revelation, often associated by later commentators with moral laxity or illicit compromise with paganism.</note> and this period is contained within the first 312 years after the birth of Christ our Lord, namely until the commencement of the reign of Constantine the Great, that is, until the year 312.

### Chapter Eight.

...after the birth of our Lord and Savior *Jesus Christ*, and this boundary <note>original: *Terminus*; a fixed point in time</note> is certain and unshakeable, in that we set the birth of *Jesus Christ* in the year of the world 3960 according to a certain author <note>original: *Auctore*</note>, as elaborated in our chronology, and for that reason is well worth noting. Regarding the division of the periods <note>original: *Periodorum*</note>, however, since we have allocated 312 years to each, the 21st paragraph below should be studied with all diligence. For it must be known that we do not present this determination of times as a settled matter, because we cannot say with certainty <note>original: *determinative*</note> that a so-called period will have exactly 312 years. We have rather taken this as a sort of target date <note>original: *quasi-terminum ad quem*</note>, not only to prevent excessive rambling, but also to show the devotees a path by which they might more sharply contemplate these world-days from the Holy Scriptures, especially from those times already passed and fulfilled.

Consequently, the tribulation of this time was very hard and heavy, consisting of all kinds of erroneous teachings, the tyranny of priests, murder and bloodshed, rebellion, and all manner of persecution, so that in these times the true Church was truly tested.

# The Eighth Chapter.

...is commonly understood as our Sunday, although this is a great error, as the first Christians knew of no Sunday; this has already been established by impartial scholars and is also evident from the words of *Paul* in *Galatians 4:10* and *Colossians 2:16*. Therefore, the Day of the *Lord* of which the Evangelist speaks here was something entirely different; it was called the Day of the *Lord* because on that very day, *Christ* the *Lord* revealed to *John* all occurrences from that day until the end of all times, in order to show them to His servants (verse 1). This was done so that not all people without distinction should find the understanding of these mysteries, but only the true servants of *Jesus Christ*. 

In the 3rd verse, *John* calls blessed those who read, hear, and keep the words of this prophecy. In the 4th and 5th verses, he wishes grace and peace to the seven churches in *Asia* (which at that time were under seven particular bishops or overseers) from him who is and who was and who is to come <note>original: "von dem der da ist und der da war, und der da kommt." *John* wishes this grace and peace from three: first from him who is, etc.; from the seven spirits, etc.; and from *Jesus Christ*, etc. From this it is evident that by the seven spirits, the Holy Spirit is to be understood in seven unique divine miraculous workings. Since God the Father is named through "him who is," just as *Jesus Christ* is named separately by *John*, and especially since *John* wishes divine grace and peace from the seven spirits as well as from the Father and *Jesus Christ*, it follows that the seven spirits are and can be none other than the Holy Spirit in His sevenfold miraculous power. 

In the 7th verse, *John* describes the manner in which *Christ* shall come; but in the 8th verse, a deep, unfathomable mystery is hidden. There it stands: I am the Alpha and the Omega, the beginning and the end, says the *Lord*, who is and who was and who is to come, the Almighty. In the 4th verse, this same phrase is found: "who is and who was and who is to come." That this is to be understood as *God* the Father is indisputably seen from the contrast in the 5th verse, where we read: "and from *Jesus Christ*." That the name *Ehyeh* <note>original: "Ehjeh," a transliteration of the Hebrew 'I AM'.</note> "he who is," etc., and *El Shaddai* <note>original: "El Schaddai," Hebrew for 'God Almighty'.</note> "the Almighty *God*," is attributed to Him, the only true *God* and Father, remains beyond all contradiction. 

But now *Christ* speaks here in the 8th verse of Himself, as is evident; from which it must be indisputably concluded that the essence of *Christ* and of the Holy Spirit must be without any beginning or end, just as the Father—who is and who was and who shall be—one God, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, in a unity incomprehensible to us. # The Eighth Chapter

...a lion’s mouth, for the dragon had given him his power and his throne and great authority. To understand this verse, Daniel 7 is very necessary, in which four tyrannies—or powerful empires—are shown to Daniel under the form of four cruel beasts: a lion, a bear, a leopard <note>original: "Pardel"</note>, and a grey, strong, terrifying beast with large iron teeth. These serve as a true archetype, showing that in the Beast (or the Antichrist) alone, all the power, tyranny, and cruelty that the dragon held over all peoples, crowds, heathens, and languages would flow together. Therefore, the Beast is described as a combination of those four cruel beasts mentioned previously: namely, that it was like a leopard, its feet were like those of a bear, and its mouth was like a lion’s mouth. However, its power, throne, and authority, which the dragon handed over to it, are the fourth beast of Daniel 7:7, 19, etc. 

In this regard, we cannot help but remind the reader that many have committed a great error in the interpretation of Daniel 7. They believe the fourth beast signifies the fourth or Roman Monarchy alone. However, verse 23 clearly says the fourth beast will be the fourth kingdom on earth, which will be *different* from all those other kingdoms (namely, it will consist of a mixture of spiritual and worldly power), and it will devour the whole land, tread it down, and crush it. That the Beast (or Antichrist) possessed—and still possesses—the highest and most powerful monarchy on earth, before which all the kings of the earth have bowed their knees (and for the most part still cringe before it), requires no proof at all. It is world-renowned that its power and authority extend over all parts of the globe, setting up and deposing kings, murdering, oppressing, and robbing them, and handing their kingdoms over to tyrants. In short, it devours everything, and what cannot be devoured within its Sodomitic cloisters <note>original: "Sodomitischen Clausen." Likely a polemical reference to the perceived corruption of monastic enclosures.</note>, it crushes with its fierce claws.

§. 40. But Daniel 7:24 continues and says: After them another shall arise; he shall be different from the previous ones and shall humble three kings. This is still in the future, in the Laodicean Period <term>Laodicean Period<note>In historicalist theology, this refers to the seventh and final age of the Church, characterized by lukewarmness and preceding the final judgment.</note></term> and in the "hour of temptation" that will come over the entire world, as clearly shown from the following 28th verse:

# On the Revelation of Jesus Christ.

§. 57. But before we proceed further in this chapter, we must speak a little more regarding the parable of the Kingdom of Heaven through the ten virgins with their lamps, because this parable certainly belongs here. However, because it is full of extraordinary mysteries, it would require a book of its own; such lengthiness, however, is not appropriate here. Therefore, we shall strive for brevity as much as possible and only bring forward that which is useful to our purpose. We say, then, that Christ the Lord aimed this parable at the final time shortly before His coming. The wedding signifies the <term>1,000-year Kingdom</term> <note>Also known as the Millennium, a period of peace and Christ's reign on earth described in Revelation 20.</note> of Christ, Chapter XX. That five wise and also five foolish virgins are described here depicts the very last state of the Church for us in the most perfect way. And (1) that half of the Church—on account of the above-mentioned conversion of Israel and the heathens <note>original: "Heyden"</note>—will then be wise, that is, upright believers and true lovers of Christ; the other half, however, will be foolish, that is, those who, according to outward appearance and outward church-fashion, will appear to be as good believers as the wise ones. They will almost, in fact, be able to boast along with that Pharisee in Luke 18:11:

> O God! I thank you that I am not like other people—robbers, the unjust, adulterers—or even like this tax collector <note>original: "Zöllner"</note>, that is, common sinners. I fast twice in the week, and give the tithe of all that I have.

In short, one will see nothing outwardly but pure holiness in words and deeds among them: reading diligent prayers, singing, going to church, coming to the Lord’s Supper at the times appointed by the visible church, and diligently participating in everything else that belongs to the outward appearance of things—and what has been gradually invented by men along with the <term>stone churches</term> <note>A common Pietist critique referring to institutionalized religion that prioritizes physical buildings and rituals over the "living temple" of the heart.</note>. And therefore, they are called virgins before all others who live in the works of the flesh (which are recounted by Paul in Galatians 5:19), because they have filled their lamps with the <term>righteousness of outward works</term>, but not with the righteousness from faith through the love of Jesus Christ. Thus, at that time (not counting the true Antichristian rabble), half will be found to be true believers, and the other half sham-believers, who, despite all their self-chosen ways, will likewise be as concerned as the wise ones to participate in the Marriage of the Lamb. Therefore Christ says: "They who took their lamps"—namely all ten, in order to be ready for the wedding.

§. 58. Furthermore, the text says: *The foolish took their lamps, but they took no oil with them. But the wise took oil in their vessels along with their lamps.* It is especially to be noted here that the foolish took their lamps just like the wise, yet without oil; but the wise took their vessels along with their lamps and oil. This is to indicate that the <term>deluded- and work-believers</term> <note>original: "Wahn- und Werckgläubige"</note> (the foolish) will be just as concerned as the wise to join in...

By contrast, the wise take this not only for their lamps but also in their vessels, to replace the depletion of their lamps, so that they might not be lacking during the delay of the bridegroom—should it be said in the hour of heavy temptation: *The Lord delays His coming.* Regarding this light of faith, Christ the Lord says in Matthew 5:16: *Let your light shine before men, that they may see your good works and praise your Father who is in heaven.*

§. 59. These will indeed also hear the voice, but they shall not come out before the 1,000 years are over. Instead, during such a time, they must await complete purification through faith in Christ, until they also gradually come to rest, so that at the last Great Judgment they may also enter into general eternal salvation; regarding which more will be said in the following Chapter 20.)

§. 9. Here we must again take **Fig. I.** before us; there **i. k.** is the expanse or the heavens of Mars ♂, Jupiter ♃, and Saturn ♄. Then **l. m.** is the expanse or heavens of Venus ♀ and Mercury ☿, and **m. h.** is the heaven or expanse of the Sun ☉; The Moon ☽, however, is **e.**, the Earthly Circle or heaven, which nevertheless possesses all heavens above and below it as an expanse or distinction between Water <note>original: "Majim (▽)"</note> and Fiery Water <note>original: "Asch Majim (Aigen △ ern)"; "Asch" refers to the Hebrew 'Esh' for fire, and 'Majim' for water.</note> as the figure shows. Here it must be known that these heavens or expanses are not of one single essence, but **NB.** each one is a particular fluid being, entirely distinct from the others, and therefore they can in no way mix with one another. Just as a vegetable oil, an oil of Vitriol <note>original: "Ol. 🜔 per deliqu." - Oil of Vitriol produced by deliquescence, a process where a salt absorbs moisture from the air to become liquid.</note>, and a Spirit of Wine <term>Spirit of Wine: A high-proof alcohol produced by distillation.</term> simply will not mix with one another to become a single substance—no matter how much one might shake them together in a glass—they will always perfectly separate from one another as soon as they are allowed to stand still. Thus, the Oil of Vitriol will stand at the bottom, the vegetable oil upon it, and the Spirit of Wine at the very top. 

The same condition applies to all the heavens or circles, both in our Solar System and in all the upper, innumerable systems; namely, that every star has its own fluid circle from which it was generated and in which it, as it were, swims. Nor can it move from that circle into another circle above or below it (because these are entirely contrary to its essence, according to the aforementioned comparison) so long as this world stands; rather, it must constantly swim or run in its own. More regarding this can perhaps be mentioned in the chapter on Astrology. 

Because the original Mercury ☿ is not at all obtainable by us in this state of mortality—not even in its form as Fiery Water <note>original: "Asch Majim"</note>—we must look to how it first became **Bdellium** <term>Bdellium: Mentioned in Genesis 2:12; in this context, it refers to a semi-crystalline or resinous spiritual substance that has "thickened" from the divine light.</term> in Eden. The text says that the Gold of that land is good, and there also Bdellium and the **Onyx** stone are to be found. ## Chapter II.
# Of the Utility and Use of the Heavenly Mercury.

->§. 1.<-

In this chapter, we shall deal with the matter quite briefly, because the utility and use of the heavenly <term>Mercury: ☿</term> has for the most part been reported in Parts I and II. Its general utility is that it is the spirit and sustainer in all sublunary <note>literally "below the moon"; refers to the earthly realm subject to change and decay</note> creatures. As soon as this <term>Mercury: ☿</term> has departed or been driven away, the body is dead, as is demonstrated in <term>plants: vegetabilia</term>; for, as soon as the <term>Mercury: ☿</term> or spirit is distilled away from them by the <term>art of separation: Scheide-Kunst</term> <note>an early term for chemical analysis or distillation</note>, the plant is brought out of its substance; thus, no creature down here can exist without this heavenly <term>Mercury: ☿</term>. Just now we have called the spirit a <term>Mercury: ☿</term>, not that we wish to be understood as meaning the original heavenly one, for that is a bird of a different feather. The spirit of a vegetable, animal, and mineral body is called a "Mercury" as a counterpart to the heavenly one (namely, according to their physical principles, wherein the heavenly <term>Mercury: ☿</term> is hidden in an airy <term>Water: 🜄</term>), and just as a highly rectified spirit divides bodies into the very smallest particles (but does not melt away their primary essence—as such melting or dissolution is possible only for the heavenly <term>Mercury: ☿</term> alone), so the heavenly <term>Mercury: ☿</term> is able to dissolve bodies in all three kingdoms <note>Animal, Vegetable, and Mineral</note> into their first essence, or immature form, without any coercion or force, as was said of the heavenly <term>Fire: 🜂</term> in its proper place.

For as long as it is locked and contained within a single cloud alone, it cannot ignite, because no pressing or rubbing motion is yet present. One sees this in powerful thunderstorms: the clouds within them run against each other and roll about from below, above, and all sides. There, this fiery <note>alchemical symbol: $\triangle$</note> matter ignites and not only flashes violently but also—having been compressed—this fire shoots down from the hollow clouds with cruel force like a heavy cannon, shattering, smashing, and indeed often igniting and consuming everything it encounters.

§. 8. The cruel rattling and thundering, however, is caused by the violent tearing of the clouds. This is heard as long or short, strong or weak, depending on whether the bang caused by the breach encounters many or few hollows in the clouds—just as a gunshot in many connected valleys is heard much louder and longer than on a flat field. The hard crackling, however, which follows immediately upon a lightning strike, is also caused by the bolt in its rapid breakthrough of the air, just as a fired cannonball creates an almost identical crackling as it passes through the air. But after the aforementioned bolt has descended and the quick crackling is past, the thundering first follows in the hollows of the clouds, as if in deep valleys. 

From this, anyone who loves truth—and not dreams or vain delusions—will be able to be satisfied regarding the cause of lightning and thunder. # On the Use and Benefit of the Heavenly Mercury.

Indeed, this mercury can be brought forth from all creatures, because they can all together be reduced into a water <note>alchemical symbol for water: 🜔</note>—that is, ultimately reduced to a water <note>alchemical symbol: 🜔</note> through the proper art of alchemy. Yet such a mercury <note>alchemical symbol: ☿</note> is not their first essence, but rather a third form of that first essence. From these, gold <note>alchemical symbol: ☉</note>, silver <note>alchemical symbol: ☽</note>, as well as iron <note>alchemical symbol: ♂</note> and copper <note>alchemical symbol: ♀</note> can be extracted, depending on how the water <note>alchemical symbol: 🜔</note> was conditioned by the "ideal" or "virgin" earth. From this, a lover of truth will recognize that it is not common mercury <note>quicksilver</note>, but the original universal mercury <note>alchemical symbol: ☿</note> that is the true principle of all metals and minerals. This universal spirit sinks itself into the water <note>alchemical symbol: 🜔</note>, is then led into the subterranean clefts, and once it encounters a legitimate <term>matrix</term> <note>A "matrix" or "womb" is the specific geological pocket or mineral environment where a metal forms.</note>, it allows itself to be shaped into this or that metal or mineral by the subterranean fire <note>alchemical symbol: 🜂</note>.

§. 12. Here, however, we must remind the reader that although we said in the previous section that common water <note>alchemical symbol: 🜔</note>, fire <note>alchemical symbol: 🜂</note>, and mercury <note>alchemical symbol: ☿</note> were not the true principles of mineral growths, but only their "third" principles, this is to be understood in a certain way. Specifically, they are indeed their true principles insofar as they congeal within the bowels of the earth; but beforehand—through the sinking of the universal or very first principle (which is water <note>🜔</note>, fire <note>🜂</note>, and mercury <note>☿</note>)—they are "ideally" begotten in the water. According to the proportions and weight found there, they are coagulated within this or that clay <note>original: "Letten," referring to the moist, mineral-rich clay found in mines</note> into this or that metal. Hence, depending on which principle has the upper hand, the metal becomes heavy or light, brittle or malleable. For instance, in gold <note>☉</note>, silver <note>☽</note>, tin <note>♃</note>, and lead <note>♄</note>, mercury <note>☿</note> has the upper hand, and thus they are heavier than the others. In copper <note>♀</note>, iron <note>♂</note>, and common mercury <note>☿</note>, sulfur <note>🜍</note> prevails, which is why they are lighter. One finds the truth of this at the large smelting fires, for there one sees the arsenic—that is, the metallic water <note>🜔</note>—rising from all kinds of ores as a thick smoke, settling in the furnace as well as in the vaults designed to catch this smoke or dust. The sulfur <note>🜍</note>, however, burns brightly out of the melting ores and metals in the form of blue, red, green, and brown colored flames; one can also extract it from mercury <note>☿</note> or cinnabar ore in the true form of fire <note>🜂</note>. The water <note>🜔</note>, however, does not appear "alive" <note>liquid</note> in the ores and metals because it has been coagulated by the oiliness or sulfur <note>🜍</note> of the ore; but once the metal is brought into flux by the power of the fire, one recognizes its fluid nature <note>original: "🜔alität," a play on the word "quality" using the water symbol</note>. Mercury <note>☿</note> can also, as previously mentioned, be extracted through the proper art of separation <note>chemistry/metallurgy</note> so that it remains a natural, liquid mercury <note>☿</note> even in the cold.

The more one strives to find words to make this essence completely perfect and comprehensible—as clearly as two and three make five—the darker and more confused one only makes it. §. 17. §. 21. If the Mercury <note>Here referring to the volatile components of the antimony ore</note> sinters together <note>clumps or partially melts into a mass</note>, you must constantly grind it small again. Continue with this calcination—the longer, the better. When it is enough (which one must learn from experience), grind it once more as finely as possible, spread it upon a glass plate in a cellar, and let it stand until it dissolves <note>deliquesces, or turns to liquid by absorbing moisture from the air</note>. Then, extract all saltiness from it with a simple, common brandy <note>original: "Brandwein," referring to distilled spirits or alcohol</note> (but certainly not with Vitriol <term>original symbol: ⊕</term> <note>often used to represent vitriol or certain salts</note>, as is commonly done, which is an effect running contrary to nature). Proceed further as is customary, and you will obtain a genuine Salt of Antimony <term>original symbol: ⊖ ♁ii</term>.

§. 13. Namely, we once, together with a trusted friend, made the Regulus of Antimony Martialis <term>original symbol: ♂us</term> <note>a "regulus" is the metallic heart of an ore; "Martialis" indicates it was made using Iron (Mars)</note> at the same time and hour. Our wind-furnaces stood side-by-side against a wall in a laboratory, where one furnace was perfectly equal to the other; we also used the same kind of coal and the same quantity, likewise the same Antimony, Iron <term>original symbol: ♂</term>, and Salt <term>original symbol: ⊕</term>. We also placed our composition into the Fire <term>original symbol: △</term> in the same quantity at the same time and minute, and likewise kept it therein for the same duration. Nevertheless, we obtained a quarter-pound more of the "regulus" for every pound of composition than our friend. Whoever can guess the Fire that we used in our furnace (for we both had the same, and yet not the same, Fire <term>original symbol: △</term>) will likewise be able to accomplish this. This Fire was mentioned in a certain place in the second volume of the work on Jupiter <term>original symbol: ♃</term> <note>Tin</note>, where one may search for it. There are many kinds of ignitions in this lower world. The first fathers of the human race ignited their Fire <term>original symbol: △</term> partly through flint-stones, partly through two pieces of wood or steel and iron rubbed together, and partly through the rays of the sun; to which, in the new post-Flood world, other ignitions have been added, such as lightning bolts and even strange mechanical motions <note>original: "Motus mechanicos"</note>. Therefore, a lover of this art must reflect on what kind of ignition is necessary for his intended works. This is to be noted.

<meta>This page continues the discussion on astrological practice. <header>Of True and Natural Astrology.</header>

§. 5. First, it is necessary to know that ancient and modern **astrologers** <note>original: *Astrologi*</note> have assigned certain properties to the twelve fictional celestial houses or regions of the heavens. To the **1st house**, they have assigned life, its stability, and everything pertaining to its essence. To the **2nd house**, that which is granted for profit and sustenance, fortune and prosperity. In the **3rd**, they have placed brothers, sisters, close relatives, and short journeys. In the **4th**, the condition of the parents, and all immovable property, as well as wealth within and above the earth. In the **5th**, one finds small children, friends, a life of pleasure, a happy state, and further travels. The **6th** contains the household, servants, small livestock, illnesses, and thefts. The **7th** holds within it marriage, the state of matrimony, dealings with women, secret enemies, war, etc. In the **8th house**, death reigns: there one finds inheritances, burial, and enmity. The **9th** deals with religion, divine service, and all spiritual matters, scholarship, and long journeys. In the **10th** is found scholarship, all kinds of **professions**, <note>original: *Professionen*</note> arts, sciences, dominion, governments, and what belongs thereto; also, this house is dedicated to the mother and grandmother, just as the fourth is dedicated to the father and ancestors. The **11th** indicates special friends and friendship, honor and promotion, the happy outcome of all human endeavors, and fertile or unfertile times. In the **12th house**, one finds imprisonment, an evil and violent death, all enmities, and ruin or damage from large livestock and animals. All of this may be consulted more extensively in the works of the **authors**, <note>original: *Autoribus*</note> as we only cite here what is useful for our purpose.

§. 6. We proceed, therefore, to the **judgment** <note>original: *Judicio*</note> of the aforementioned **nativity**; <note>original: *Nativität*; a birth chart or horoscope calculated for the moment of birth.</note> whereby, above all things, it must first be considered: whether the born person will survive the first four years—the **years of nurture** <note>original: *annos nutritionis*</note>—in which the human body, due to its great delicacy, is subject to the most dangerous accidents, or not? Indeed, it would be a great piece of tomfoolery to want to **prognosticate** a great and long-lasting happiness for a newborn when the limit of life (as much as one can surmise from the position of the stars) consists of the very shortest **term**. <note>original: *Termino*</note> We have known enough of such nonsensical fools who have predicted for a newborn not only a very long life but also great happiness, when those same infants survived, some for barely a few days, others for only a few weeks. In particular, a few years ago, such a boastful **windbag** <note>original: *Windfänger*; literally "wind-catcher," a term for a braggart or someone full of "hot air."</note> **erected** such a lying theme for one of the greatest princes of this world, even though this prince reached a lifespan of barely a quarter-year. But what does it help! The world wants to be deceived. He who likes to dance is easily whistled to. <note>A German proverb meaning that people are easily persuaded to do or believe what they already desire.</note> One should therefore consider the following five **significators** <note>original: *Significatores*; specific planets or points in a chart that "signify" or represent specific areas of life.</note> (indicators): (1.) the **horoscope**, <note>In traditional astrology, the "horoscope" refers specifically to the Ascendant, or the degree of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon.</note> or the

The **Moon** (☽), whether it is in <term>fall or detriment</term> <note>original: *casu vel detrimento*; these are positions in the zodiac where a planet is considered weak or poorly placed</note> (see Section 16 below), or whether it makes a bad <term>aspect</term> <note>the geometric angle between two planets</note> with **Saturn** (♄) or **Mars** (♂)? Here, Saturn and the Moon stand close together, and the Moon is almost "under the rays" of Saturn; this indicates a weak, <term>phlegmatic</term> <note>in the four humors theory, this implies cold and moist, often associated with lethargy or susceptibility to illness</note> brain, subject to <term>falling sickness</term> <note>original: *fallenden Sucht*; an old term for epilepsy</note>, especially since Mars (♂) and **Mercury** (☿) are in <term>opposition</term> (☍) to the Moon. Had this not been the case, the child would hardly have survived for a few days because of the influence of Mercury, Saturn, and Mars from the 1st and 7th houses. (4.) Both of the "fortune-bringing" planets, **Jupiter** (♃) and **Venus** (♀).
