If they stand collectively, or for the most part, happy and well, it signifies the opposite. But if they stand partly happy and partly unfortunate, it indicates that the newborn will indeed be preserved, yet with great hardship. Because Saturn (♄) in this birth is in the **Ascendant** <note>the degree of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon</note>, in the house of life, and Mars (♂) is in opposition in the 7th house; Jupiter (♃) is in the 8th house in opposition to the Moon; and in the 2nd house, Jupiter is in <term>conjunction</term> (☌) with Venus and Mercury, which are **occidental** <note>original: *occidentales*; setting in the west after the sun</note>, as can be seen on the general chart. Saturn and the Moon are **oriental** <note>original: *oriental*; rising in the east before the sun</note>, but still under the earth; thus, it is to be concluded according to nature that this birth will have a very short life. And indeed, the child did not survive its second year.

§. 7. Furthermore, long experience has also confirmed the following natural rules: (1.) That when Saturn, Mars, and the Moon are in conjunction (☌), the child may hardly live a month. A conjunction in the 8th house with a poorly aspected Ascendant—or the Moon in the 4th house viewed from a <term>square</term> (□) or opposition (☍) by Saturn and Mars—indicates that the mother endured a life-threatening birth. (2.) The Sun and Moon in any <term>angle</term> <note>original: *cardine aliquo*; the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses, which are the most powerful points in a chart</note> in a good aspect to Jupiter or Venus, indicates health and long life. But the opposite is true when they are unfortunate, such as in fall or detriment (see Section 16 below), or in conjunction with Saturn or Mars, or wholly or partly in square or opposition to them in <term>cadent houses</term> <note>original: *abfallenden Häusern*; the 3rd, 6th, 9th, and 12th houses, considered the weakest</note>, such as the 3rd, 6th, 8th, and 12th. Thirdly, when in a daytime birth the Sun, and in a nighttime birth the Moon, stand free of all bad aspects, the newborn may be successfully raised. But when the **Lord of the First House** <note>original: *I. Dom.*</note> and the ruling light (the Sun by day and the Moon by night) are poorly aspected, the newborn will hardly reach their 4th year; unless the **Lord of the Ascendant** <note>original: *Domin. Ascendentis*</note> stands happily in an angular house. (4.) When the Sun or Moon are with Saturn or Mars in an angular house in conjunction or opposition, the child is born dead or at least half-dead. (5.) When the Ascendant is in the <term>term of a malefic</term> <note>original: *termino Malefici*; specific degrees of a sign ruled by Saturn or Mars</note>, within the bounds of Saturn or Mars or a malignant fixed star, and is further aspected by another through a square or opposition.

Likewise also the **Moon** in the 6th or 9th House in <term>square</term> or <term>opposition</term> to **Saturn** or **Mars**. (12.) If the **Moon** is in the 1st House without a <term>sextile</term> (*) or <term>trine</term> (△) from **Mercury** (☿) or **Venus** (♀), the newborn will not live long after birth. (13.) Whereby it is to be noted that **Saturn** is contrary to life, while **Mars** is contrary to nourishment and preservation. Whoever knows how to apply the aforementioned rules with <term>a grain of salt</term> <note>original: *cum grano salis*</note> in their <term>judgment</term> <note>original: *Judicio*; the final astrological assessment</note> will seldom grasp in error. Only after this follows the second question: namely, how long will the life extend? Whereby it can simultaneously be observed: whether the birth is [capable] <note>catchword from next page: *tüchtig*</note> for the investigation of natural secrets and the philosophy of spirits...

...whether they will be capable and skilled or not? Since this question belongs to the 1st House (I.); namely, when it has **Jupiter** (♃) <term>ascending</term> <note>rising on the eastern horizon</note>, but **Saturn** (♄) <term>descending</term> <note>setting on the western horizon</note>, the person is perfectly suited for all mysteries; the opposite, however, occurs when **Saturn** is ascending and **Jupiter** is descending. For example: the previously mentioned birth had the opposite, namely **Saturn** ascending and **Jupiter** descending. See the *Speculum Astrologicum* <note>original: *Specul. Astrolog.*; likely referring to a common "Mirror of Astrology" textbook of the 17th century</note>. Therefore, had this child remained alive, they would have been entirely unfit for the <term>secret philosophy</term> <note>hermetic or occult wisdom</note>; but rather inclined toward sorcery. Experience has certainly confirmed that such a constellation contributes greatly to this. Even Leah, Jacob's wife, knew of this in her time, when she cried out at the birth of her first son by Zilpah in Genesis 30:11: *Ba-gad* <note>original Hebrew: בגד</note>, that is, "fortune rises" (happiness is coming), the Star of Justice, the constellation of **Jupiter**, which among the Hebrews is called the good planet (*Mazzal tov* <note>original: *Massal tof*; literally "good constellation" or "good luck"</note>) because of its singular goodness and bliss. And she called his name Gad. These births are especially qualified for the aforementioned high sciences when they have **Jupiter** in the 1st House in good <term>aspect</term> <note>geometric relationship</note> and constellation, and when **Saturn** in the 9th House <note>the house of religion and philosophy</note> is well-regarded by **Mercury** (☿). Of such people, one can say they have something divine about them.

§. 8. Now we come to the second question, namely: How long will a person live? Regarding this, one finds such strange and confused, as well as unfounded and truly sinful rules among the astrologers, that one could fill an entire book with them alone. For a true Christian, this must remain firmly established: that the almighty **GOD** has set a certain limit of life for every human being until natural death, which is known only to Divine Omnipotence alone, and to no creature, neither in heaven nor on earth; nor may it be exceeded by even a hair’s breadth by any creature, provided that the person leads their life according to Divine will and calling. No stargazer can ever fathom the goal of this ordinary <term>Fate</term> <note>original: *Fati*</note> through the interpretation of the stars. One can perhaps make a conjecture based on the <term>temperament</term> <note>the physical constitution or "humors" of the body</note>, insofar as the confluence of the stars concurs, whether it will be long or short. But to set a specific determination for the year, month, day, and hour, we consider—according to the fundamental rules of Holy Scripture—to be a sinful and damnable audacity. However, violent and extraordinary death is of a different nature. (Natural death comes through all kinds of illnesses, or in old age through the eventual extinguishing of life-forces.) It is true that violent death, just like natural death, is known to the Divine, unchanging Omniscience in its constant omnipresence (otherwise called eternity, a term we intentionally do not use here), but it is not preordained by <term>intentional will</term> <note>original Latin: *ex propositita voluntate*</note>. No <term>Theosopher</term> <note>a student of divine wisdom or mystical philosophy</note> will ever doubt this. And this, we believe, is actually...

# On True and Natural Astrology.
Ccc 2

actually the so-called <term>Predestination</term> <note>the theological doctrine that all events have been willed by God, usually with regard to the salvation of some and not others</note>; namely, because (as previously mentioned) it was known to God in His omniscience. For to **Know** is one thing, and to **Will** and **Be Able** is another. However, these words—**Foreordained** and the like—are too harsh and run contrary to the essential goodness and mercy of God. Citing the words of Paul in Romans 9 does not help here; for Paul speaks there in a metaphorical way <note>original: "Gleichnißweise"</note> against the reasonings of our flesh regarding the inscrutable ways of God. He argues that if God wished to use His unrestricted omnipotence, what could He not do with us miserable humans (whom He created out of free will and can likewise turn back into nothing)? When Adam fell from Eden into this earthly realm, he and all his descendants became subject to the influence and governance of the stars with his <term>elementary body</term> <note>the physical body composed of the four elements (earth, water, air, fire), as opposed to the spiritual body</note>. Now, if a person lives not according to the Spirit but according to the flesh, and thus lives in enmity against God, he remains subject to the drive of the stars and follows merely their inclination until the end <note>death</note>, as far as they are able to set his limit through God's providence. Almighty God allows this to happen according to the person's own will, so that the person may hereafter realize what it means to live according to God's will or his own. Just as Adam experienced it in the Garden of Eden, to our collective temporal and eternal ruin, through his own willing.

§. 9. From what has been said before, one will easily be able to grasp how far a God-devoted person may go in inquiring about a long or short life without causing offense. Against this, all the examples of past events cited by <term>astrologers</term> <note>original: "Astrologis"</note> to maintain their fabricated rules (which are unfounded in nature) are of no help at all. For here the common saying holds true: namely, that Satan sells and peddles countless lies by means of a single truth. So that we may avoid these dangerous cliffs and reach the safest port through the wind of truth, it is first necessary to seek the chief indicator of life in the following table, which the Arabs called the <term>Hylech</term> <note>an Arabic astrological term for the "giver of life" or the point in a birth chart that determines the longevity of the person</note>; namely, the position of the Sun and the Moon by day or by night.

This **Hylech** now indicates the length of the years of life through its **dispositor** <note>the planet that rules the zodiac sign in which another planet is located</note>, which is the **Lord of the Nativity** <note>original Latin: "Dominus Geniturae"; the planet with the most influence over the entire birth chart</note> (how to find this? see below in § 16). Namely thus: if this **dispositor** stands in an **angular house** <note>original Latin: "cardine"; the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses, considered the most powerful positions</note>, it indicates the *greater* years of life of the **Hylech**; in a **succedent house** <note>original Latin: "succedente"; the 2nd, 5th, 8th, and 11th houses</note>, the *middle* years; and in a **cadent house** <note>original Latin: "cadente"; the 3rd, 6th, 9th, and 12th houses, often considered the weakest</note>, the *lesser* years. 

However, if neither the Sun nor the Moon were in one of the aforementioned houses, whether by day or by night (which would be something extraordinary), then one takes the **Lord of the Nativity** as the **Hylech**, and the planet that is closest to it in dignity as the **dispositor**, and proceeds as mentioned before. This path is generally much more reliable than wanting to take the Sun and Moon alone as the **Hylech**. Namely, that one always takes the **Lord of the Nativity** as the **Hylech**, and the one closest to it in dignity as the **dispositor**. But if no planet were the **Lord of the Nativity** (<insert>Note: The Sun and Moon can never be Lords of the Nativity</insert>), then one proceeds with the Sun and Moon as mentioned before.

§. 10. But whoever is not satisfied with what was mentioned before and enjoys vain effort may seek his pleasure in **Direction** <term>a method of "progressing" the birth chart forward in time to predict when specific life events will occur</term>, the rules of which he must follow according to the astrologers—though to list them here would go against our current purpose. We shall therefore proceed to the **manner of death** according to the influence of the stars. Here, particular attention must be paid to the 6th, 8th, and 12th houses, and which planets are located within them. (2.) What aspects or "rays" <note>the angles of light cast between planets that determine their relationship</note> fall into these houses? (3.) The **lords of the signs** <note>the specific planets that rule the zodiac signs</note> within these houses. (4.) What kinds of signs are in these houses: violent or benign? (see below, §. 17.) (5.) How the **Horoscope** <term>the Ascendant or 1st house, representing the self</term>, its ruling planet, and the **Lord of the sign of the Horoscope** <note>original Latin: "Dom. signi Horoscopi"</note> are configured. (6.) How **Saturn** and **Mars** are positioned in relation to the **Moon**, whether in **Square** (□) or **Opposition** (☍), or when they enter into these aspects with it; this is to be sought in the **Ephemerides** <note>astronomical tables showing the daily positions of celestial bodies</note>, as well as in common calendars.

Accordingly, a **violent death** is indicated by the following:
(1.) When the **Sun** (☉) or **Moon** (☽) is in the 8th house <note>the house traditionally associated with death</note> in a violent sign.
(2.) When one of the same is within 5 degrees of a **conjunction** (☌) with a violent **fixed star** (those of the nature of Saturn or Mars; see below §. 20); also when the lord of the 1st or 8th house is in conjunction with the Sun or Moon.
(3.) When one of the **Lights** <term>the Sun or Moon</term> <note>original Latin: "Luminum"</note> is afflicted by a **malefic** <term>an "evil-doing" planet, typically Saturn or Mars</term> <note>original Latin: "Malefico"</note>, and the other light is in conjunction with the other malefic in a violent sign or with a violent fixed star.
(4.) If the Sun or Moon is afflicted by one malefic such that the other malefic is simultaneously afflicted, or stands in a violent sign, so that one of the malefics additionally afflicts the Sun, Moon, or the 8th house.
(6.) When the Moon is in **Taurus** (♉︎), **Gemini** (♊︎), **Libra** (♎︎), or **Scorpio** (♏︎) such that the sign sits in both the 7th and 8th houses simultaneously.
(7.) When a malefic is in the 10th house in a malefic sign.
(8.) When one malefic is in a **cardinal point** <note>original Latin: "Cardine"; the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses, which are the strongest points of a chart</note> in square or opposition to a violent fixed star, while the other malefic is in the 8th house.
(9.) When a malefic is in the 8th house, or the Lord of the 6th or 1st is **harmed by a malefic** <note>original Latin: "a malefico læsus"</note>, or the Lord of the 8th is himself a malefic and stands in a violent sign, and one of the Lights is afflicted by the other malefic or stands in a violent sign.
(10.) When the **Lord of the Horoscope** is in the 8th house in **detriment or fall** <note>original Latin: "in detrimento vel casu"; positions where a planet is weak or poorly placed</note> in a violent sign with an evil fixed star, and one of the Lights is afflicted by a malefic.
(11.) When the lords of the 1st and 8th houses are poorly positioned throughout. 

These, then, are the principal observations; any remaining useless subtleties and long-winded details may be sought in the works of other authors. If none of the aforementioned circumstances are found, then a natural death is to be presumed.

(2.) One of the malefics in the 8th house...

§. 12. Now follow some other notes belonging to the **I. House** <term>the 1st house or Ascendant, which represents the individual’s body and personality</term>. And (1.) concerning the **Complexion** <term>the physical constitution and temperament of the person born</term>: Regarding this, one finds such strange rules among the **Astrologers** that it is almost impossible to make sense of them, and nearly everything results in fabricated **Principles** <note>original Latin: "Principia"</note>. We have always followed the following nature-bound path. For example, let us take again the birth mentioned above (§. 4.), upon which the general chart was constructed. There, **A.** is the Globe of the Earth, and the point under the **Meridian** <term>the imaginary line passing through the North and South poles and the zenith of the birth location</term> is the place of birth; everything else—the 12 houses, the positions of the planets, the signs of the **Zodiac**, and so forth—is clearly shown in the figure.

There, **Saturn** (♄), the **Sun** (☉), **Venus** (♀), and **Mercury** (☿) stand in the **Occident** <note>the West, where the sun sets</note> or descent, and they cast their rays very obliquely <note>at a sharp, weak angle</note>. **Saturn**, the **Sun**, and **Venus** in particular are therefore not of such strong effect as they would be if they were **Oriental** <note>rising in the East</note> or stood near the **Meridian**. This is provable by the sun's rays, for at high noon they ignite and burn much faster and more powerfully through a **burning-mirror** <note>a magnifying lens or concave mirror used to concentrate sunlight to start a fire</note> than if they fell very obliquely from the East or West through the burning-mirror. Because the aforementioned planets are already in the VII. house and very near the western point, their slanted radiation to the **focus or place of birth under the meridian** <note>original Latin: "ad focum oder locum nativitatis sub meridiano"</note> is very weak and slight.

In contrast, **Jupiter** (♃) stands in the VIII. house and shoots its rays much more sharply toward the place of birth. From this, it is naturally concluded that the person must have become of a **Jovial** <term>good-tempered, cheerful, and healthy, like the planet Jupiter</term> mind and complexion, especially since **Jupiter** is in the house of **Venus** (♀), though they would have also participated somewhat in the nature of **Mars** (♂) and **Mercury** (☿). Therefore, their complexion would be Jovial, yet somewhat hot-tempered, loving of merriment, and ingenious. From **Saturn**, the **Sun**, and the **Moon**, which at that time already stood beneath the earth (whereby their **rooting** <note>original Latin: "radication"; the ability of the planet's influence to "take root" at the birth site</note> at the place of birth was hindered), this birth could receive nothing. And because **Libra** (♎) is a house of **Venus** and the **exaltation** <note>a sign where a planet's influence is heightened</note> of **Saturn** in the **Horoscope** <note>the 1st house</note>, this indicates very slippery desires, especially since **Saturn** stands with the **Sun**, **Venus**, and **Mercury** in **Libra**.

However, if all or most of the planets stand above the earth, one looks solely at the one that radiates most perpendicularly upon the place of birth, especially when that planet is **in dignity** <note>original Latin: "in dignitate"; positioned in a sign where it has natural strength or power</note>. For in this case, one must especially reflect upon this—namely, the **Dignity** and the **Lord of the birth**. Whoever follows this nature-bound rule will not apply his effort in vain but will find satisfying benefit.

§. 15. Now, for astrologers, the rest depends mainly on the timing: when should this or that occur? For this purpose, they invented **Direction**, which is the measurement of the equatorial arc <note>original Latin: "arcus æquatoris"</note> between two stars or other points that indicate the matter one wishes to know. # ->On the True and Natural Astrology.<-

Here, Mars, because he possesses 8 strengths, is unquestionably the Lord of the Geniture <note>original: "Domin. Genit." or Dominus Geniturae; the planet that carries the most influence in a person's birth chart</note>. Because Saturn is closest to him in dignity, and thus both are malefic governors of life <note>original: "malefici gubernatores vitæ"; planets traditionally associated with hardship or endings</note>, the native <note>the person for whom the chart was cast</note> had little hope for a long life, especially since Saturn and Mars have 15 dignities <term>Dignities are points of strength a planet gains based on its position.</term>; on the other hand, the remaining planets have 24 debilities <term>Debilities are points of weakness.</term>, and thus the good is outweighed by 9. However, because the birth did not have both life-cutters <note>original: "abſciſſores vitæ"; planets that signal the end of life</note> directly opposed to it, the native—since the Sun, according to the above teaching in §. 9, is the Giver of Life <note>original: "Hylech"</note> and Mars is the Dispositor <note>the ruling planet of the sign where another planet resides</note> in an angle—could have hoped for a very long life. But if one wanted to take the Lord of the Geniture (namely Mars) as the Giver of Life (as mentioned there), then Saturn would be his Dispositor; and because Saturn is in the Ascending Angle <note>the 1st House, the most powerful point of the eastern horizon</note>, he would have granted the native the greater years <note>original: "ann. majores"; a traditional calculation of a planet's maximum lifespan contribution</note> of Mars, namely 66 years.

### Chapter Four.

...valiant <note>The text begins mid-word, likely completing "ritterliche" (knightly) or "ehrliche" (honorable) from the previous page.</note> soldiers, great captains, hot-blooded, irascible, lovers of weapons, those who do not like to be subjects, and those who disregard wealth. But if Mars $\mars$ stands poorly, he makes truly cruel people, great robbers, the bloodthirsty, those inclined toward sorcery, the boastful, the vengeful, and blasphemers; in short, evil people.

$\odot$ Sole Signifier, in a perfectly good state. Hot-blooded, magnanimous, wise, chaste, faithful, just, loyal friends who have truthful dreams, very ambitious, respectable, and serious. But if the Sun $\odot$ is weak, all that is good is corrupted.

$\venus$ Signifier, in a fortunate state. Beautiful, well-formed, cheerful lovers of all merriment, merciful, peace-loving, inclined to all pleasure, haters of strife and anger, and devout people. But Venus $\venus$ in an unfavorable state makes fearful ones, fornicators, and the unchaste, who squander everything with harlots.

$\mercurius$ Signifier, well-configured and positioned <note>original: "bene configuratus & affectus"</note>. Indicates excellent talent <term>Ingenium</term> <note>Natural intellect or creative genius.</note>, a love of study, teachability, and shrewdness; seekers of secret arts and sciences, cunning, and cautious ones who love commerce and mathematics, as well as music, painting, and sculpture. Mercury $\mercurius$ Weak <note>original: "Debilis"</note>; inconstant, treacherous, thievish, lying, malicious, stammerers, and procurers.

$\leftmoon$ Signifier, well-positioned <note>original: "bene posita"</note>. Scorners, the vain, and the inconstant. Poorly positioned <note>original: "Malè posita"</note>. Fearful, useless, agitators, and even perhaps fools and simpletons.

#### 8.) Of the Planets in the 1st House.

> Saturn $\saturn$ or Mars $\mars$ in the 1st house or in sextile $\sextile$ with it, and if they are "foreign" <term>peregrini</term> <note>A planet is "peregrine" when it has no essential dignity (strength) in its current zodiac position, making it wander or act unpredictably.</note>, they make very suspicious people.
>
> Saturn $\saturn$ or Mars $\mars$ in the 1st house in Leo $\leo$, Aries $\aries$, Sagittarius $\sagittarius$, or Capricorn $♑$; makes cruel, predatory people.

> Venus $\venus$ in the 1st house in Cancer $\cancer$, Aries $\aries$, Leo $\leo$, or Capricorn $♑$, and if she is in dignity <term>dignitate</term> <note>A planet in "dignity" is in a zodiac sign where it naturally thrives and exerts a positive influence.</note>. Indicates honorable and laudable people.
>
> Saturn $\saturn$ or Mars $\mars$ in the 1st house in movable signs <note>Also known as "Cardinal" signs (Aries, Cancer, Libra, Capricorn), which represent initiation and change.</note>; inconstant people, lovers of the common folk and their ways, and especially Mars $\mars$ makes hot-tempered people.

The fixed signs <note>original: "beständige Zeichen" (Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, Aquarius)</note> in the 1st house indicate stable people; but double-bodied <term>bicorporea</term> <note>Also known as "Mutable" signs (Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, Pisces), which were thought to have a dual nature.</note> signs indicate cunning, shrewd people who nonetheless love music. And so much for the planets. But their remaining properties—should anyone desire to know them—such as: gemstones, metals, times for work, animals, numbers, people, children, diseases, cures, human limbs, smell, taste, colors, etc., let him seek these among the authors who have dealt with this. Likewise, what singular effect this or that planet might have in each house? But because all of this is not useful to our purpose, and for the most part consists of unfounded inventions of pagan curiosity, we have intentionally chosen not to include it.

Regarding this table, we must remind the student <note>original: *Liebhaber*—literally "lover" of the art, common terminology for a dedicated amateur or student</note> that in the use of judgment <note>original: *Judicio*—the formal interpretation of an astrological chart</note>, they must at all times pay heed to which triplicity the aspect occurs in, and then direct themselves in the judgment according to its property. What unspeakable benefit this table will bring in practice <note>original: *Praxi*</note> to the student who knows how to use it according to our rules, we wish to pass over for the sake of brevity <note>original: *Weitläufrigkeit*</note>; just as the extensive benefit and use of the same is not reported here in full detail, because all of this would make the work too voluminous. Practice, however, will teach the student everything.

->### The Fourth Chapter.<-

So that one does not lack the most prominent Fixed Stars in the **Judgment** <note>original: "Judicio"; the final astrological analysis or reading of a chart</note>, we have attached the preceding necessary table. From this, one can see, according to **longitude** and **latitude**, into which **House** <note>One of the twelve divisions of an astrological chart representing different areas of life.</note> each Fixed Star should be placed. The Fixed Stars listed here are sufficient for our purpose. **α.** and **β.** are the Latin and Arabic names. **γ.** The nature of the Fixed Stars <note>The planetary quality or "temperament" assigned to the star.</note>. **δ.** Their latitude: **S.** for Northern <note>original: "Septentrionalis"</note> and **M.** for Southern <note>original: "Meridionalis"</note>. **ε.** The degrees of longitude in the signs of the **Zodiac** in which the Fixed Stars stand. **ζ.** The star's **Right Ascension** <term>Right Ascension: The distance of a point east of the First Point of Aries, measured along the celestial equator.</term>. **η.** The difference, or how far the star has moved forward in 100 years <note>This refers to the precession of the equinoxes, where stars appear to shift positions slowly over centuries.</note>. Since this table was established for the year 1668, and 50 years have passed until the present year—which is half of 100—one must add half of that difference to the longitude of the star to find its true location. **ϑ.** is the **declination** of the star, either **S.** for North or **M.** for South, and **ι.** is the difference for the same in 100 years, observing the aforementioned note on longitude. **κ.** whether the difference is to be added or subtracted. **λ** is the **magnitude** or size of the star.

**Practice.** If one now wishes to know: In which House in the above **Scheme** <note>An astrological birth chart or diagram.</note> should the **Head of Medusa** <note>original: "Caput Medusæ"; also known as the star Algol.</note> be placed? First, look in the preceding table for the star's longitude, which is found at 21° 35' **Taurus** ♉. The difference for its forward movement is 1° 37'; half of this is 48' 30". When added to the previously found longitude, it makes 22° 23' 30" **Taurus** ♉. Now, look in the chart to see where **Taurus** stands. It is found in the **VIII. House**. Thus, say that the star **Medusa’s Head**, which is of the nature of **Saturn** ♄ and **Jupiter** ♃, stands at 22° 23' 30" in the 8th House, and therefore in **Taurus**. This signifies the most dangerous state for one's life and the very shortest lifespan, as was indeed proven in this birth. And it is **NB.** <note>abbreviation for "nota bene" or "note well"</note> to be carefully observed: whenever **Medusa’s Head**, the **Eye of the Bull** <note>Aldebaran</note>, the **Bright Star of the Whale's Tail** <note>Lucida Caudæ Ceti, or Deneb Kaitos</note>, or similar **Saturnine** or **Jupiterian** stars are found in the 8th House with a **Malefic** <note>A "bad-acting" planet, traditionally Mars or Saturn.</note> like **Mars** ♂ or **Saturn** ♄, or likewise in the **1st House**, it certainly signifies a quick death and the shortest of lives. However, if these stars are found in the 1st House alongside the indicators of a long life mentioned above, the person born will be of a cruel, murderous disposition, being very quick to cruelly murder themselves or others. In short, these are very desperate people, unless the malice of the aforementioned stars is softened by **Benefics** <note>Helpful planets, like Venus or Jupiter.</note> and their **Aspects** <note>The geometric angles between planets.</note>.

# Chapter Four.

Now, if one wishes to find the **rising or setting amplitude** <note>original: "Amplit. ortivam vel occiduam"; this is the angular distance along the horizon from the true East or West point where the Sun rises or sets.</note> for the pole height of 51° 6' on June 21, one first seeks the degree of the Sun on the given day in the above-mentioned **Solar Ephemeris Table** <note>A table showing the daily positions of celestial bodies.</note>. There, one finds 0° Cancer (♋). Seek this 0° in the preceding Table of Declinations; in the right-hand column above Cancer, one finds 23° 31' 30", which is the **maximum solar declination** <term>maximum solar declination</term> <note>The furthest point north or south of the equator reached by the Sun, occurring at the solstices.</note>. Now set it into the rule as follows, and operate as is customary with the logarithms of sines and tangents. (1.) Subtract your **pole height** <note>Geographic latitude.</note> of 51° 6' from a **quadrant** <note>A 90-degree arc.</note> of 90°:

### Of True and Natural Astrology.

...by 15, for that is exactly how much the **Zodiac** <term>Zodiac</term> <note>The belt of the heavens divided into twelve signs, through which the sun, moon, and planets appear to move.</note> passes through the **meridian** <term>meridian</term> <note>The imaginary circle passing through the celestial poles and the point directly above the observer; when the sun crosses it, it is local noon.</note> in one hour, which makes 8 [hours] 10' 32". However, since according to the proportion of Archimedes <note>The author is referencing the Archimedean approximation of Pi as 22/7 to calculate the relationship between a circle's circumference and its diameter.</note>, the circumference of a circle relates to its diameter as 22 relates to 7, so the **Earth’s** diameter (the circumference of which amounts to 5,400 German miles) would be 1,718 2/11 miles; multiplying this by 80 makes 137,454 6/11 miles, and that is how much the diameter of the **Sun** [☉] would then have to be—yet it still lacks 810 miles to reach the aforementioned total of 146,640.

**U.** The fourth **Saturnian** lunar circle. At a semi-diameter of 3 and a quarter **inches** from **Saturn**. Its revolution occurs in 2 days and 7 hours.

**W.** The fifth lunar circle of **Saturn** [♄], at half-diameter [radius] of 2 **inches** from **Saturn**. Orbits in 45 hours.

**X.** At half-diameter, to the **Sun** 360 **inches**.

**Y.** The distance between **Saturn** and our **Sun** is 2,800 times smaller than that of the **Fixed Stars** from **Saturn**, thus amounting to 1,008,000 **inches**; from which it is to be concluded that no proportional sketch, even at the very smallest scale, may be drawn upon paper, if the **Sun** were given such a size that the other planets and their circles could be proportioned accordingly.

**Z.** The **Fixed Stars**, which are nothing but **suns** and have their own planets around them—even though these cannot be seen by us due to their astonishing height—and are therefore, like our system, entirely worlds. Here one should note that if a ball were to fall 300 **ells** <note>An "ell" (German: *Elle*) was a traditional unit of measurement, roughly the length of a man's arm, though it varied by region.</note> with every heartbeat, it would require 20 days or more for its fall from the **Moon** [☽] down to this **Earth**. From the **Sun** to the **Earth**, however, 25 years. From **Jupiter** [♃] to the **Sun** or **Earth** (whichever were taken as the center point), 125 years. From **Saturn** [♄], however, 250 years.

**§. 38.** Now we establish that all the so-called **Fixed Stars**, and thus all the heavens above **Saturn**, were created before this our present world, and that this our world was then, before the **Fall of Lucifer**, equal to them; but through **Lucifer’s fall**, it was turned into a chaotic formlessness <note>original: *tohu vabhohu*; a Hebrew phrase from Genesis 1:2 meaning "without form and void," describing the primordial state of the world before light was created.</note>, as has already been said several times before.

**§. 39.** Furthermore, it is to be noted that a **Saturnian year** consists of 30 of our solar years; a year of **Jupiter** [♃], 11 of ours, and a bit more, etc. See above, Section 23 of this Chapter. Concerning the days on **Saturn**, no certain observation has yet been made. Regarding the years, everything is likely correct; but because every planet—indeed, every star—has its own rotation around its axis, it would be worth inquiring: How long must a day on **Saturn** be? Now, since **Saturn's** motion and revolution <note>The author uses "revolution" here to refer to the orbital period around the Sun.</note> take nearly 30 solar years, its motion must also be quite slow. On **Jupiter** [♃], a day is 10 of our hours, and so forth.

# The Fourth Chapter.

...of His will, of His infinite glory, and wishing to make something (as it were) outside of Himself a partaker in it, He created—out of the outflowing will of His Majesty, according to His infinite power and glory—everything in, above, and under the heavens; so that all creatures created by Him should not only recognize His power and glory, but also His loving pleasure toward the creature, and should most gratefully acknowledge, boast of, honor, laud, and praise Him for all eternity. Because the outflow of the Divine Will cannot be expressed by any comprehensible sound, nor condensed into a significant word, it is said that God created the world out of nothing. The wise call it <term>Hyle</term> <note>original: "Hyle"; a Greek term (ὕλη) referring to primordial matter or the fundamental substance of the universe</note>. Whoever is able to receive it, let him receive it!

§. 51. That a lifeless body, empty of all rational and other creatures, could not do such a thing <note>i.e., praise God</note> is beyond all doubt for those whose reason is not displaced; for as already mentioned, truly nothing more foolish could be suggested than that the planets and stars <note>represented by the symbol *</note> were created only to illuminate our little point of an **Earth** <note>symbol: ⊕</note>, while otherwise being bodies devoid of all creatures. Suppose it were so, which we do not admit; what use then are those <term>Fixed Stars</term> <note>stars that appear stationary in the sky compared to the planets</note> which, because of their incomprehensible height, no human eye can see, not even through the <term>Telescopes</term> <note>original: "Tubos"; early refracting telescopes</note>? Are these also supposed to shine upon us on the **Earth** <note>symbol: ⊕</note>, when even the visible stars of the first magnitude are unable to do so? Who would philosophize so foolishly? Therefore, it remains established—from the incomprehensible Godhead, which has no measure in length, breadth, or depth, but exists in infinite fullness, as well as from the astonishing height of the stars <note>symbol: *</note> and their terrifying size—that all these visible and invisible stars <note>symbol: *</note> are nothing but **Suns** <note>symbol: ☉</note>. Each of these moves, revolves, and moistens its own world, which worlds are altogether filled with rational and other creatures, according to the properties of their essence, for the recognition as well as the praise, honor, and glory of the Divine Majesty and Splendor.

§. 52. But now the question will be: first, what kind of essence do the aforementioned worlds have, and are they equal to our **Earth-Globe** <note>term: "Erd-Kugel"</note> in density and opacity? (2) What kind of rational and other creatures inhabit them? (3) Have these rational creatures sinned and fallen, like our forefather **Adam**? (4) And if they were fallen, what kind of redemption must they then have had? Regarding the first question, it cannot be resolved quite so simply from the Holy Scriptures. It is known through the more recent <term>Astronomical Observations</term> <note>original: "Observationes Astronomicas"</note> that the planets of our **Solar** <note>symbol: ☉</note> <term>System</term> <note>original: "Systematis"</note> or our world are dense bodies, upon which—through magnificent <term>Telescopes</term> <note>original: "Tubos"</note>—mountains, valleys, rivers, lakes, etc., have been observed; and they are said to have their light, by which we can see and recognize them at night, not from themselves, but from our **Sun** <note>symbol: ☉</note>.

# Of True and Natural Astrology.

Whether, however, their nature is therefore equal to this, our elementary sphere, in essence and properties? We have important reasons to doubt this. Moses speaks in Deuteronomy 6 to Israel: "Hear, O Israel! The Lord our GOTT is one God." <note>original: "Höre Israel! der HErr unser GOTT ist nur ein einiger GOTT." This refers to the Shema, the central prayer of Judaism.</note> This GOTT has proclaimed and revealed His mercy to us only through one Redeemer, His only-begotten Son, Jesus Christ. This one—namely Christ our Redeemer—has also preached to us of only one redemption through His most holy suffering and death, and also of only one (and not many) hells; furthermore, He announced that He would hold the judgment here on this **Earth** <note>symbol: ▽; the alchemical symbol for the element of Earth</note>, as the specific dwelling place of sinful man. Additionally, the Scripture teaches us that this, our **Earth** <note>symbol: ▽</note>, shall be destroyed by **fire** <note>symbol: △; the alchemical symbol for the element of Fire</note>, as a mass light in **fire** <note>symbol: △</note> and disposed toward **fire** <note>symbol: △</note>, concerning which more is to be looked up in Part II regarding **fire** <note>symbol: △</note>. And since all of this is indisputable, we conclude that because the Holy Scripture speaks of such things regarding no other body of our system, but only of our **Earthly** <note>symbol: ▽</note> sphere alone, the same must be of an entirely different substance and nature than all the other planets and stars.

§ 53. Now, if one did not wish to accept what was previously stated, this blasphemy would have to follow: that the only true GOTT had not just one, but many sons, through whom He had redeemed all the aforementioned worlds from their fall and ruin (provided one wanted to claim they were of the same nature as our sphere). Or, Christ the Lord would have had to accomplish countless sufferings, according to the countlessness of these worlds. However, it can in no way be proven that all these worlds floating in the eternal deep should have fallen together and at once through the Fall of Adam; for all the worlds of the **fixed stars** <note>symbol: ✱; stars that do not appear to move relative to each other</note>, as proven above, have not the slightest communion with our **Solar** <note>symbol: ☉</note> system, but have their own suns, light, and motion.

§. 54. Furthermore, if in this, our world, the planetary bodies **Saturn** <note>symbol: ♄</note>, **Jupiter** <note>symbol: ♃</note>, **Mars** <note>symbol: ♂</note>, **Venus** <note>symbol: ♀</note>, **Mercury** <note>symbol: ☿</note>, and the **Moon** <note>symbol: ☾</note> were to be of the same nature as our **Earth** <note>symbol: ▽</note>, then their orbits—in which they complete their course—would also necessarily have to be of one and the same nature as our **Earthly** <note>symbol: ▽</note> heavens up to the orbit of the **Moon** <note>symbol: ☾</note>. From this it would follow that because all these orbits are of the same nature, there would then be nothing that could prevent one planet from entering the region of another; indeed, they would all fall back into confusion. But since no planetary body can in any way deviate or waver from its orbit, it is indeed obvious that they must consist of a difference (opposition); namely, that each of these bodies, for the sake of appearance, is the coarser part of its own fluid or orbit. Since this cannot be contradicted without sophistry, it proves itself that not a single planetary body can have even the slightest commonality in quality with our earthly globe: which is likewise to be understood of all the **fixed stars** <note>symbol: ✱</note>.

# Chapter Four.

§. 55. Since we have now established that the planetary bodies (1) can have no commonality among themselves in **quality** <note>original: "qualitate"</note>, and also (2) in regard to their movement and effect must be of a pure and more subtle essence than our **Earth**-sphere <note>symbol: ▽; the alchemical symbol for the element of Earth</note>, it follows necessarily that the rational and other creatures created in and upon those planetary worlds can have no equality in quality—namely, of one planetary world with another, and much less with us on this **Earth**-sphere <note>symbol: ▽</note>. We wish the same to be understood of all fixed-star worlds; whereby the previously mentioned question: *Whether the planetary and fixed-star worlds were of the same essence in properties and transparency as our **Earth**-sphere <note>symbol: ▽</note>,* will be sufficiently answered.

§. 56. In the resolution of the second question: *What kind of rational and other creatures inhabit the aforementioned worlds?* there is likewise nothing to be shown from Holy Scripture. However, the rational conclusion from the preceding is this: that because we humans on this earth were taken from and out of the same, and must again become this **Earth** <note>symbol: ▽</note>; likewise, the rational and other creatures of the other worlds were created out of their own world-bodies. Therefore, because their worlds are not of one essence with our world- or **Earth**-sphere <note>symbol: ▽</note> (as said before), it follows that their rational and other creatures can have no commonality with us according to their quality, even though all rational creatures, whether they be in the heavens or in all aforementioned worlds, have one and the same image or likeness; as was thoroughly proven in Part II regarding the **Fire** <note>symbol: △; the alchemical symbol for Fire, often used here to represent the divine spark or the Form of God</note>.

§. 57. Thirdly: *Whether these same rational creatures, like our forefather Adam, have sinned and fallen?* Because the upper **star**-worlds <note>symbol: ∗</note> can have no commonality with our **Solar** <note>symbol: ☉; the astronomical/alchemical symbol for the Sun</note> system or world due to inconceivable distance, the sin of Adam—who was created to be a ruler of our **Solar** <note>symbol: ☉</note> system in the place of the fallen Lucifer—could not simultaneously corrupt the upper **star**-worlds <note>symbol: ∗</note>. And although someone might object that just as Holy Scripture has mentioned nothing detailed about the upper worlds, it could also well be that the creatures in other worlds had also sinned and fallen, as it is written: *The heavens are not pure in thy sight* <note>original: "Die Himmel sind nicht rein für dir zc."; a reference to Job 15:15</note>, etc. And since the wisdom and omnipotence of GOD are unthinkably great, He could have presented a means of redemption for them in other ways. But that such an objection is highly absurd can be recognized from the Godhead itself; for it would follow from such a sophisticated supposition that there must be an unfathomable and, consequently, indescribable multiplicity within the Godhead, against which Nature itself strives, even without Holy Scripture. This happens because much more powerful influences radiate down from the upper worlds of the fixed stars and completely alter the otherwise infallible effects of the planetary aspects. Therefore, even when an astrological judgment happens to be correct, such a thing is truly hit upon more by chance than from indisputable principles. For it may have happened that exactly at the moment of birth, the constellations of the upper worlds were in sympathy or in harmony with the constellations of our solar system. ### The 5th Chapter.
# Concerning Religion according to the clear, distinct letter of the Holy Scripture, and the true Mago-Cabbala founded upon the same.

### §. I.

Now we proceed in the name of **GOD** to a matter through which we will, without doubt, fall under the censorship of the Gentlemen of the Orthodoxy <note>The author refers to the strict Lutheran Orthodoxy of the 17th and 18th centuries, which maintained rigid control over doctrinal purity</note>. For because many such learned gentlemen are of the opinion that they alone are entitled and capable to teach and write of theological things, and that the priests cannot err in the Law; they immediately seize upon those who are not of their guild as soon as they even appear to handle such matters. There, everything is pulled through the worst by them—criticized, judged, and condemned—whatever does not allow itself to be measured exactly according to their yardstick. And even if they themselves can find nothing therein which they can declare as erroneous or evil, it is usually enough for them to reject the matter simply because the author is not of their order, and has not learned the art quite as regularly as they have at the universities <term>high schools</term> <note>original: "hohen Schulen," referring to universities</note>, and has not been privileged there to speak and write of **Theology**. However, because both Christ the Lord himself as well as his disciples were not of the order of priests and scribes, and the true teachers and disciples of Jesus Christ must be taught not so much at the high schools of the world as in the school of Christ and his Holy Spirit; so then, no upright, enlightened theologian will approve of the foolish and truly idolatrous imagination of the orthodox heretic-makers. We also expect from such people a judgment that is reasonable and in accordance with Christ's rules; as for the mockery and criticism of the others, it shall concern us little. We proceed, therefore, to our undertaking.

## Chapter V.

### Concerning Religion according to the clear, distinct letter of the Holy Scripture, and the true Mago-Cabbala <note>A term combining "Magia" (divine wisdom in nature) and "Cabbala" (divine wisdom in tradition/scripture), suggesting a mystical understanding of faith.</note> founded upon the same.

->§. 1.<-

**N**ow we proceed in the name of God to a matter through which we will undoubtedly fall under the censure of the Gentlemen of the Orthodoxy. <note>The "Orthodoxy" refers to the established Lutheran church authorities of the 17th and 18th centuries, who often clashed with mystical or "pietist" writers.</note> For because many such learned gentlemen are of the opinion that they alone are authorized and capable of teaching and writing about theological matters, and that the priests could not err in the Law; so they immediately attack those who are not of their guild <note>original: *Zunft*. The author compares the professional clergy to a closed trade union.</note> as soon as they merely show themselves to deal with such things. There, everything is then critically scrutinized, blamed, judged, and condemned by them in the worst way, whatever cannot be measured exactly by their own standard. And even when they themselves can find nothing therein which they can declare as erroneous or evil, it is usually enough for them to reject the matter simply because the author is not of their order, and has not, like them, learned the art in a regular manner at the universities <note>original: *hohen Schulen* (high schools), the standard term for universities at the time.</note> and been privileged to speak and write of Theology there. However, since both Christ the Lord himself as well as his disciples were not from the order of priests and scribes, and the true teachers and disciples of Jesus Christ must be taught not so much at the universities of the world as in the school of Christ and His Holy Spirit; therefore, no righteous, enlightened theologian <note>original: *Theologus*</note> will approve of the foolish and truly idolatrous conceit of the orthodox heresy-hunters. From such enlightened people we expect a reasonable judgment in accordance with Christ's rules; as for the mockery and blame of the others, it shall concern us little. Thus we proceed to our undertaking.

§. 2. Let no one expect, however, in our presentation, a style of writing arranged according to theological scholarship, nor hope that we might perhaps begin with a subtle description of religion according to the ru-

might be? and what He is called? Of this, one finds no actual character in the Book of Nature, but must seek such in the Holy Scripture; there, the first words read thus: In the beginning **God** created the heavens and the earth, etc. He is thus called the Beginner and Creator of all things: **GOD**, in Hebrew **ELOHIM** <note>original: "ELOHIM"</note>. Which the old Cabbalists <note>Followers of Jewish mysticism (Kabbalah), whose methods the author adapts for Christian theology.</note> interpreted as: The mighty Judges. And because this word is spoken in the plural, they have concluded from it—as well as from Genesis 1:26 and Chapter 3:22, where **GOD** is likewise spoken of in the plural (for **God** says in the first place: Let Us, etc., and in the other: Behold, the man has indeed become like one of us)—not without reason, that the mystery of the Godhead—Father, Son, and Holy Spirit—lies hidden therein. Otherwise, **God** has also revealed Himself under the name: The **Lord** Almighty. Genesis 17:1. As He Himself says in Exodus 6:3 to Moses: I appeared to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob under the name of God Almighty, but by my name **LORD** I was not known to them. Now we come to yet another naming, which the Almighty **GOD** gave Himself in Genesis 2:4, where He is called **JEHOVAH ELOHIM** <note>original: "JEHOVA ELOHIM"</note>, which is interpreted as: He who was, He who is, and who will be, that is, independent love and mercy.

§. 5. Thus we have heard from the Scripture that the Almighty Being, by whom all things were created, is and is called **GOD**; but what is His form? Of this, no likeness can be made because of His incomprehensibility: for since everything created is from Him and of Him, it is also entirely impossible that He can or may be grasped by any creature; rather, just as **God** the **Lord** contains this astonishingly great building of the world within Himself and fills everything everywhere, so there is nothing outside and around it but **GOD** everywhere, without any end being found in all eternity in this bottomless depth of the Godhead. Therefore, no likeness of any form can be given to **GOD**, as He strictly forbade such in Exodus 20:4, Deuteronomy 4:15, 23, Isaiah 40:18, 25, and Chapter 46:5.

§. 6. But although **God** the **Lord**, according to His pure Godhead, is entirely without image and incomprehensible, and He has also strictly forbidden that anyone should make any image or likeness of Him, yet the corrupted reason of men has not wanted to be satisfied with how **God** reveals Himself in Holy Scripture, but they have devised all sorts of artful words through which they wish to describe **God**, so that not only one image, but countless idols of contention have been hatched in the schools <note>The author uses "schools" to refer to academic or scholastic theology, which he views as prone to pointless arguments.</note>

### Of Religion and Mago-Cabbala. <note>Mago-Cabbala: A term referring to a blend of "magical" natural philosophy and the "Cabbala" (Jewish mystical tradition), often used by 18th-century esoteric thinkers to explore the hidden workings of God and nature.</note>

...and whoever did not want to accept such rubble-dust of theirs instead of the pure gold from the sanctuary had to be a heretic, though they themselves introduced quite heretical and idolatrous ways of speaking. For where does one read in Holy Scripture the words invented during the decline of the Greek and Latin churches: *Trinity*, *Person*, and the like, from which the idolatrous way of speaking—of three persons in the Godhead—arose? Certainly, whoever would have used the words *Person*, *Trinity*, etc., in the first true Apostolic churches would have unfailingly been cast out from their community as a heretic. And no rational person will deny that as soon as one speaks of three persons in the Godhead in their distinctness—as *God the Father*, *God the Son*, and *God the Holy Spirit*—one immediately presents to the imagination three distinct gods. This then runs contrary to the clear revelation of Divine Majesty, and no human understanding will be found so pure and clear that it does not immediately, through this way of speaking, imagine three gods (or three kinds of gods) according to the number of persons, and thus make for itself a false image of God.

§. 7. *Moses* says in *Deut.* VI. 4: "Hear, *Israel*! The Lord our God is one Lord"; which then *Christ* the Lord himself confirms in *Matth.* XIX. 17; *Mark* X. 18; *Chapter* XII, 29; *Luke* XVIII. 19. And the Apostle *Paul* writes in *Rom.* III. 30: "Since it is one God who justifies," etc. And in 1 *Cor.* VIII. 4, he writes: "So we now know that there is no other God but the one." This he also confirms in *Gal.* III. 20 and elsewhere. Of this one God, *Christ* the Lord says in *Matth.* XXVIII. 19 that He is Father, Son, and Holy Spirit; and *John* writes in his first letter, *Chapter* V. 7: "There are three that bear witness in heaven: the Father, the Word, and the Holy Spirit, and these three are one." <note>This verse, known as the Johannine Comma, was historically used to support the doctrine of the Trinity, though it is absent from the oldest Greek manuscripts.</note> Just as one also finds various places in the Old Testament where this Holy Triad <note>original: "Drey-Zahl"</note> in the one Godhead is mentioned, such as *Gen.* I. 26; *Chapter* III. 22, 23; XI, 7; *Chapter* XVIII; *Joel* III. 21; *Ps.* XXXIII. 6, etc.

§. 8. From what has been said until now, it is truly to be recognized that there is one eternal, infinite God: Father, Son, and Holy Spirit. Of whom *John* writes in 1 *John* IV, 8, 16, that He is Love; and *Christ* the Lord says in *John* IV. 24: "God is a spirit." And therefore, according to the property of a spirit, He is the most simple essence <note>In historical theology, "simplicity" (Einfalt) means God is not composed of different parts or substances, but is a perfect, indivisible unity.</note> and unity; consequently, also in His properties, the highest perfection in holiness, justice, wisdom, omnipotence, love, goodness, and mercy, without the slightest internal conflict. Thus, the will of His omnipotence can consist in nothing other than grace, mercy, patience, great kindness, and faithfulness (according to *Exod.* XXXIV, 6). But when it is...

§. 9. We have previously stated that the One God is Father, Son, and Holy Spirit; however, as to the actual nature of this arrangement—namely, that the One God is Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, and not only in name, but effectively working—we cannot say, because such a mystery is incomprehensible to our reason, and thus also indescribable. We know of nothing in all of nature with which we can give even a small image or likeness of this matter, except the Δ <note>The triangle (or the Greek letter Delta) is used here as a geometric symbol for the Trinity—three distinct sides/angles forming one single shape. In many mystical traditions, it also represents fire.</note>; For just as it is only one essence, and yet has three distinct properties, such as shining, warming, and burning, and none of these properties can be separated from it without completely destroying it. In this way, God is called the Father, the Creator through the Son; the Son, the Redeemer out of the mercy of the Father; and the Holy Spirit, the Light and Enlightenment from the Father and the Son. However, even this is only an imperfect, dead image, by which the essence of the matter we are discussing can be signified very little or not at all. Blessed are those in whom God has revealed Himself as Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, because no one can understand or grasp anything of it outside of such revelation, no matter how clearly one might try to picture or describe it to them.

§. 10. That the Father, or so to speak, God, is God, is denied by no one; and that Jesus Christ, the Only-begotten Son of God, is entirely One with the Father and Holy Spirit, and thus is also the true God and eternal life, is clearly to be proven from very many places in Holy Scripture. For firstly, He Himself says that whoever sees Him sees the Father, because He is in the Father and the Father is in Him, John XIV, 9. 10. 11. and that He and the Father are One, John X, 30. and to Jacob He says, after his nightly wrestling with Him: You have wrestled with God and with men, Genesis XXXII. 28. 30. Secondly, John writes that He, as the Word who became flesh or man, was in the beginning (understanding this as the eternal, essential beginning, which is God Himself, according to Revelation I. 8. III. 14. XXI. 6. XXII. 13) with God and was God Himself, John I. 1. 2. 3. and in his first letter Chapter V. 7. 20. <note>original: "1. Joh. V. 7. 20." — Verse 7 contains the "Johannine Comma," a famous and debated passage explicitly stating the Father, Word, and Holy Ghost are one.</note> he writes that He is One with the Father and Holy Spirit, and that He is the true God and eternal life. Thirdly, the Apostle Paul writes in 1 Timothy III, 16. that God was revealed in the flesh, namely in the humanity of Jesus Christ; that God in Christ was [reconciling] the world with Himself

§. 11. Since this true Triune <term>Triune: The concept of the Trinity, three persons in one divine essence.</term> eternal **GOD**—Father, Son, and Holy Spirit—enjoyed within Himself the greatest and most perfect joy, delight, and blessedness without beginning or end, and desired that there should also be creatures to whom He could communicate Himself in the outflow of His Divine goodness, and who would love and praise Him for it; He then created through Christ the Spirit-world, in which the Son of the Dawn <note>A poetic reference to Lucifer before his rebellion and fall.</note> was the most glorious and excellent, and, as it were, the final point of this Divine diameter or outflow (namely, our solar system). But since he, in his so excellent glory and power, rose up in pride against **God**, he was—in this opposition against the Divine simple perfection—cast out with all his angels from this glory into an incomprehensible darkness, into which all his heavens were simultaneously entangled; and thus from the light became a desolate, dark, formless shape, which was called by the Ancients **Chaos** <note>original: "Chaos"</note>, that is, a mixed heap of all kinds of being.

§. 12. Because the immutable Godhead could not change the will of its Omnipotence, the heavens of Lucifer had to be filled again with other creatures for the praise of Divine glory; therefore **God** created through Christ this world of ours, and within it mankind according to His image, as the Holy Spirit has revealed to us through Moses.

§. 13. However, when Satan saw that out of the dark confusion, such a magnificent world was once again created, and in it the wonder-creature, Man, was formed by GOD, and that Man had been set as the ruler of this world in his stead, his envy and resentment ignited in a rage against this human. He cunningly seduced him through the misuse of his free will to act against God's prohibition and His will. Now the Devil, in his own opinion, had a winning game <note>original: "gewonnen Spiel" — a German idiom meaning he believed he had already won or held the upper hand</note> through the human's disobedience, especially when he saw that Man was cast out of the Garden of Eden and banished into this world. Here, he was to nourish himself in sorrow on the earth—cursed for the sake of his sin—all the days of his life, and eat his bread in the sweat of his brow, etc. Yet, God had mercy on mankind; He cursed the serpent above all the cattle in the field and spoke: The seed of the woman should crush the serpent's head, etc. <note>A reference to Genesis 3:15, the first promise of a future Savior.</note> And He willed that Man (Adam, and in him all his descendants) should once again strive for their first endowed glory and seek the LORD their God, if perhaps they might feel after Him and find Him, since He is not far from any one of us. Acts 17:27.

§. 14. Since the LORD God did not create human beings for wrath, curse, and ruin, but to possess eternal bliss <term>bliss: "Seeligkeit," referring to a state of spiritual salvation and heavenly happiness</term>, and since it was His earnest will that Man should again seek and find God his LORD, and live and be blessed in Him, He let nothing be lacking on His part that might serve their salvation and eternal well-being. He sought them not only through His Holy Spirit from within, but also through the holy Patriarchs <term>Patriarchs: "Altvätter," the early biblical fathers like Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob</term> and Prophets from without—to teach, to correct, and to lead them on the right path in His truth, and to bring them to Himself. Through Moses, He set before the children of Israel His laws and rights, that they should walk and live in them, and He showed them the way of life, as it were, step by step <note>original: "von Fuß zu Fuß" — an idiom for a gradual, careful, or guided progression</note>. He led them out of Egypt into the wilderness, and thereby sought to teach them how they should depart from the world with their hearts and wills, despising it with all its lust and glory, considering themselves here as strangers and pilgrims and seeking again their heavenly fatherland. He allowed them to see many great signs and wonders, seeking thereby to awaken their faith and trust in Him. He allowed them to see many cruel and terrible judgments which befell the disobedient, the ungodly, and the sinners, seeking thereby to awaken in them a truly heartfelt abhorrence of sin and to bring them to His obedience. Through the many and various purifications which He commanded them, He sought to teach them how they [should cleanse] their hearts through faith from all sin and impurity

§ 15. However, as soon as mankind began to multiply in their generation upon the ground cursed by GOD for their sin’s sake, wickedness also increased within them. They broke free from the discipline and punishment of the Holy Spirit, wandered away from GOD again and again, and among a thousand, barely one was found who asked after GOD and sought to walk in His ways. And although the LORD GOD—after they had all corrupted their way before Him—destroyed them all together from the earth by the **Deluge** <note>The "Sündfluth" or Great Flood in the time of Noah.</note> according to His righteous judgment, save for Noah and his people, and thus made an end of the first godless world, yet the descendants of Noah cared little or nothing for it. As soon as they increased again in their generation, wickedness also increased in them again, and they acted not a hair better than their ancestors in the first world had done, but arguably even worse: for instead of seeking the Lord their GOD and serving Him, they chose for themselves all manner of abominations and horrors—yes, even the images of perishable humans, and birds, and four-footed and creeping animals, etc. <note>A reference to the descent into idolatry described in Romans 1:23.</note>—as their gods. §. 16. §. 17. That Christ the Lord was to come into the flesh was prophesied in many places in the **Old Testament**. Thus, it is unnecessary to cite all those things here, especially since this is denied by no one other than an manifest **anti-Christ** <note>original: "Wider-Christen."</note>. -># On the True Religion and Mago-Cabbala.<-

[For] the sake [of the truth], we wish to treat several points even more thoroughly and clearly, and specifically, first of all, concerning the Law.

§. 19. It is well known that among the so-called Christian religions, there has been much quarreling and strife for several hundred years concerning the Law and good works. One party <note>Referring to the Protestant reformers, particularly the Lutheran tradition, which emphasized "Sola Gratia" (Grace Alone).</note> said and taught: that one could not keep the commandments of **God**, and that good works were not necessary for salvation; for one must be saved by grace alone. They sought to prove this teaching of theirs from the letters of the Apostle Paul. And so that this would be firmly planted in all their followers, they asked their schoolchildren the question: Whether we could also fulfill **God’s** commandments and Law with our good works? And they put the answer into their mouths: "Oh no! For our good works are not perfectly good, because we are poor sinners; even when we want to do good, evil clings to us." Romans 7. <note>original: "Römer am siebenden." This refers to Paul's description of the internal struggle between the "flesh" and the "spirit."</note> Because this was, as it were, made part of their nature in their youth—that the fulfillment of **God’s** commandments is impossible, that good works are not necessary for salvation, and that one could indeed be saved by grace even if one sinned greatly every day and deserved only punishment, etc.—they went right on sinning boldly and concerned themselves with nothing less than good works.

Against this, the other party <note>Referring to the Roman Catholic Church and its emphasis on the necessity of merit and works.</note> certainly fought and taught: that good works were necessary for salvation, and that one could and must keep the commandments. However, in practice, they kept them just as little as the others, and thus their strife consisted only of words. What one party criticized and rejected in the other, they themselves always did; for just as one party criticized the other for teaching that the commandments could not be kept (while not keeping them themselves), so the other criticized and rejected the first party’s teaching that good works were necessary for salvation. Yet they said or taught that their church ceremonies were necessary for salvation, and thus they built up again with one hand the very thing they sought to tear down with the other. <note>The author suggests that replacing God's moral Law with "church ceremonies" is just another form of the legalism they claimed to oppose.</note>

### The Sixth Chapter.

Since we wish to avoid all further verbosity in this chapter; in the second part concerning Fire <note>original symbol: $\Delta$, the alchemical sign for Fire</note>, we have described the general judgment based on Revelation 20:11, 15. Translations: *The sons of God seeing that the daughters of men were beautiful* <note>original French: "Les fils de Dieu voyant que les filles des hommes étoient belles"</note>, *when the sons of God saw that the daughters of men were beautiful.* The remaining European versions all have the words: *The sons of God looked upon the daughters of men*, etc.

§. 2. Regarding this memorable passage, it is now rightly asked: (1) Whether by "the sons of God," one understands angels, spirits, or natural human beings? (2) Whether spirits or angels mingle with humans, and (3) Whether the same, because they have no seed, can actually procreate?

§. 3. Concerning the first question, most of the holy Fathers among the Greeks held that the holy angels were meant by "the sons of God," such as: **Justin Martyr, Clement of Alexandria, Eusebius, Tatian, Athenagoras, Proclus**, etc. These men—because they used the Greek translation of the Old Testament <note>The Septuagint</note> rather than the Hebrew text, which has "the angels" instead of the words "sons of God"—fell into the opinion that those who mingled with the daughters of men were indeed angels. However, they were not just any angels without distinction, but those angels who were called <term>Watcher angels, presiding or guardian angels</term> <note>original Latin: "Angeli vigiles Angeli praesides vel tutelares"</note>, (**Guardian Angels**); and **Josephus** was also partial to this opinion, whose words from the German edition read as follows: *Many angels of God mingled with women and fathered headstrong children who relied on their own strength, caring neither for God nor for the world, and behaved almost like the giants of old.*

§. 4. **Philo** follows this view and says expressly in the first book *On the Giants*: *But when the angels of God saw the daughters of men,* etc. He says "the angels of God," not "the sons of God," from which it is to be concluded that **Philo** himself believed that the angels of God mingled with the daughters of men. And this opinion of the Greeks was maintained among the Latin Fathers by **Tertullian** and **Lactantius**, who established that the spiritual substances of angels, which exist without any matter, could carry out such a mingling, and thus could impregnate and consequently procreate.

§. 5. However, since such an affirmation is not to be embraced but rather entirely rejected, **Chrysostom** already in his time considered those who agreed with this opinion to be blasphemers. His words in **Homily 22 on Genesis 6** <note>original: "Homil. 22. über Gen. VI."</note> read as follows: 
> "Here we must present the true understanding of Scripture to your Beloved <note>A respectful address to the audience, "Eure Liebe"</note>, so that you may not easily give a hearing to those blasphemers; for they say that this was spoken not of men, but of angels, because these were called sons of God. But they do not show where the angels are ever called sons of God? For they can by no means demonstrate this. Human beings, however, are indeed called sons of God..."

### Concerning the invisible creatures in the elements.

...called, but the angels never. In which words it is indeed true, and remains so, that in this place angels cannot be understood; however, the proof used by the good Fathers <note>The "Fathers" refers to the early Church Fathers, the influential theologians of the first several centuries of Christianity.</note> is, in our opinion, far too weak; for **Chrysostom** <note>Saint John Chrysostom (c. 347–407), an early Church Father known for his eloquent preaching.</note> concludes in the following manner: If in no place of Holy Scripture are the angels called Sons of God, then it follows that in this place no angels can be understood; now it is certain that in Holy Scripture the angels are nowhere called Sons of God, but rather *messengers* <note>original Hebrew: "Malachim"</note>; *therefore, etc.* But the conclusion is incorrect, especially since in **Job 1:6** and **Chapter 2:1**, exactly that which Chrysostom denies is clearly found, where "Sons of God" are understood to mean angels—not according to our opinion, but according to most *commentators*, and even in the opinion of **Cocceius** <note>Johannes Cocceius (1603–1669), a prominent Dutch theologian.</note>. Yet, although so many excellent men in both former and current times have believed and established this, we nevertheless reject this simple and poorly-founded opinion entirely, and this for important reasons taken partly from Scripture and partly from reason. For that the angels do not mingle with the daughters of men, nor can they mingle, Christ himself testifies most clearly in **Matthew 22:30**, where he says: *For in the resurrection they will neither marry nor be given in marriage, but they are like the angels of God in heaven.* In which place Christ, through the words "to marry" and "be given in marriage," has expressed the act of marriage in the most honorable way, following the style of Scripture, which he flatly denies of the angels.

§. 6. Secondly, sound reason teaches that since the holy angels are of a purely spiritual and immaterial essence and have no natural seed, it is impossible for them to procreate; especially since, in the event that they could procreate, they would have to perform the *act of generation* <note>original Latin: "Actum generandi"</note> either as immaterial beings, or in their own substance, or through an assumed body composed of the elements.

§. 7. That the first cannot be so is clear as day: for how can a purely spiritual essence *perform a venereal act* <note>original Latin: "rem veneream præstiren," referring to sexual intercourse</note>, or procreate without seed, especially since the sense of touch (which the most prominent philosophers of the earth attribute [to physical life], and without which no generation can occur) is lacking in angelic spirits and immaterial entities? From this we therefore conclude: That substance which has no earthly solidity, no feeling or matter, can neither perceive through sensation nor *perform venereal acts* <note>original Latin: "res venereas exerciren"</note>; the angels have no earthly solidity and have no sensation; *therefore*.

§. 8. To which is added that if the angels were to have sensation, they would also have to be destructible. Particularly since everything endowed with this sense is entirely subject to decay and fragility, because its alternating properties are those of heat and cold.

# The Eighth Chapter.

§. 9. What is now objected against this opinion is the following:
That, namely, according to this assumption, the Holy Spirit also could not have cooperated in the procreation of the **Body of Christ**; however, this is sufficiently answered by stating that the operation of the Holy Spirit is entirely miraculous and divine, and is not bound to any auxiliary means, secondary causes, or external physicality. Instead, whenever it wills, it can act without any natural means through divine omnipotence, which divine power is not given to the angels, nor can it be given, because it is nothing other than the omnipotence of God and God Himself.

§. 10. Furthermore, the angels cannot procreate in their own bodies because they are the most minimal and simplest beings and operations, which possess no matter or heavy bodily essence, as Christ Himself testifies in **Luke 24:39**: *Spirits have not flesh and bone.* <note>original Latin: "Spiritus carnem & ossa non habet"</note>

§. 11. But that the angels should steal human seed from elsewhere and subsequently use it is a miserable fantasy and vain fiction, especially since the procreative power of the seed evaporates instantly outside the seminal vessels of the human body and is made useless. Those in the element of Fire <term>$\triangle$</term> consist of the most subtle particles of the fiery sphere and circle and are organized through the power of the universal fire. Because their essence hardly corresponds at all with the human essence, they concern themselves little with human affairs, so that it is difficult and laborious for the sages to maintain their company and to associate with them.

§. 22. Furthermore, they have among themselves a well-ordered polity <note>original: "Policey"; in this period, the term referred to the general administration and organized social order of a community</note>, perform their prayers to the Almighty God, and avoid with all diligence that which is displeasing to Him. Thus the Egyptians, according to the testimony of **DIODORUS SICULUS** <note>A Greek historian of the 1st century BCE.</note>, honored the gods of the earth (whom some call *Gnomones* <note>Gnomes or earth-dwellers.</note>) under the image of a horned goat.
