# Chapter IX.
## Concerning the Greatness, Imagelessness, and Incomprehensibility of **GOD**.

Because we wrote above in Chapter V, Section 5, that **GOD** the **Lord** is entirely imageless and incomprehensible, we wish to seek here to place this quite clearly and distinctly before the eyes of the beloved reader with a figure. Let us suppose, then, in Figure 16, that A. B. is our world-system <note>original: *Systema*</note> with our planets, heavens, and earths; C. the circles of the upper worlds, which are commonly called the fixed stars <note>original: *Fix-Sterne*</note>; D. E. F. G. the systems of the spiritual worlds; H. the heaven above all heavens, which may be grasped by our reason, the throne of the living **GOD**. Now, let someone imagine as if he were standing on this outermost circle of the heaven of all heavens, H., and wished to stretch out his hand there—whether he could do so or not? If he could not stretch it out, then another heaven, J., would have to prevent it, and thus further still, one heaven after another, such as K. L. M. and so forth. Or one would have to assert this most absurd thing <note>original: *Absurdissimum*</note>: that beyond the heaven of all heavens, H., a continuous density or solidity is to be found, in which the Divine Majesty would then undeniably be enclosed. And even if this were so—though it is not proven—what would finally be the end or the cessation of this solidity? Or if one wished to add an infinite fluid <note>original: *Fluidum*</note> there, what kind of quality would one then assign to this fluid? If one further wished to invent infinite heavens upon heavens, one would finally have to reach a point where one is the very last, and outside of it there must then be something which encloses and contains all these invented heavens, ruling them and maintaining them through its living motion. And toward that, beyond the heaven of all heavens, to this Most Holy, True, Infinite Something, our thoughts are directed: namely, to the one true **GOD**, **Father**, **Son**, and **Holy Spirit**, the primal source of all life and being, by whom all things were created and are still maintained in existence; in whose depth, height, and width no ending at all can be devised. A <term>Groundless Void</term> <note>original: *Ungrund*—a term popularized by the mystic Jacob Böhme, referring to the "bottomless" or "groundless" nothingness that precedes all created existence and even the self-revelation of God</note>, before which all reason must be astonished and become dizzy, which only in some...

# Chapter X.

## Explanation of the Words in Proverbs 8:27.

Wisdom speaks in Proverbs 8:27: "When he prepared the heavens, I was there: when he" <note>original: NB (Nota Bene), meaning "note well"</note> "compassed the abyss in a circle, I was there." What the abyss <note>original: *Abgrund*</note> is, we have stated in the previous chapter, at least as far as it is possible to describe it. Almighty God has no beginning and no end. A. A. A. A. in Figure 17 is the incomprehensible depth or the Abyss <term>Ungrund</term> of the Divine Majesty. Many millions of miles still have a conceptual existence in our reason through numbers. However, the all-filling and nowhere-ending Divine Unity can and may be grasped or encompassed by no space, no matter how unfathomably that space might be conceived. This most holy abyss has encompassed itself in a circle, represented as B., and is the first revelation of God out of the abyss; from this revelation B., the heavens C. D. E. F. G. are prepared, of which Wisdom speaks in the mentioned passage. 

Namely: C. D. are the heavens of the spiritual hierarchies; D. E. are the upper worlds, called the fixed stars <term>Fix-Sterne: Stars that appear not to move in relation to each other, as opposed to "wandering stars" or planets.</term> by us humans; E. F. is the distance from the seven <note>Referring to the seven classical planets of the ancient geocentric model.</note> to the aforementioned worlds; F. G. is the system <note>original: *Systema*</note> of our world, along with our planetary heavens—the visible revelation of the Divine Majesty and Glory, the right hand of the power of God where Christ sits and reigns, and from whence He will come again to judge the living and the dead. And this, we believe, is the true understanding of the mentioned words from Proverbs 8:27.

Because we have stated here that Christ the Lord sits at the right hand of the power of God B. C. and will come again from there to judge the living and the dead, someone might ask: Whether such an immeasurable height must be traversed by the beloved Savior in a certain amount of space and time, or whether it would happen like a flash of lightning? To this we answer: That

## Chapter XI.

### Explanation of the Verses in Genesis 1:6, 7, 8, 9 regarding the Waters Above the Firmament and the Waters Below the Firmament.

In Genesis 1:6, 7, 8, 9 we read: And God said: "Let there be a firmament <term>Firmament: Translated from the German 'Veste,' referring to the 'expanse' or 'vault' of heaven which ancient cosmology believed separated the celestial waters from the terrestrial ones.</term> in the midst of the waters; and let it be a division between the waters." So God made the firmament and divided the water under the firmament from the water above the firmament, and it was so. And God called the firmament Heaven. And from evening and morning, the second day came to be. And God said: "Let the water under the heaven be gathered together into special places, so that the dry land may be seen," and it was so. Here it is specifically to be noted and considered that two completely different kinds of water are spoken of, namely the water above and the water below the heaven; this distinction of the waters can be seen in Figure 18. Now that this general separation of the supracelestial waters (marked D.) and the subcelestial waters (marked A, B, B, and the Moon) <note>original: ☾</note> has occurred, the waters of the Sun, Venus, Mercury, Moon, Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn <note>original symbols: ☉, ♀, ☿, ☾, ♂, ♃, ♄</note>—from which the bodies of Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, the Sun, Venus, Mercury, and the Moon <note>original symbols: ♄, ♃, ♂, ☉, ♀, ☿, ☾</note> were first created on the fourth day—have taken their places. For it is truly certain that every sphere of the planets is a certain kind of super-earthly water, as has already been mentioned above in Chapter IV.

## Chapter XII.

### Of the Mercury of the Sages.

->For the explanation of Figure 19.<-

Since an old master-singer’s <note>The "Meistersinger" were members of German guilds for poetry and song in the 14th-16th centuries. The author is adopting their formal, rhymed style.</note> rapture has come upon us; we wish, as the conclusion to this work, to share our thoughts in rhymed verse according to this old master-art for the sake of those who thirst for gold, regarding the magical Figure 19.

Salt, Sulfur, and Mercury, a wonderful spirit <note>original: "Spiritus"</note>,
Whoever has this has enough, yet one should not seek it in the curse,
Which, through man’s heavy fall, throughout this entire system <note>original: "Systema"</note>,
As far as it is elemental, has been permeated and crept through;
For although it is also to be found within, like a thin smoke,
Because no creature of the earth may be sustained without it;
Yet it is so firmly locked away, that it is nothing but child’s play,
The effort one exerts to free it through the glow of earthly fire
From its bonds; for it laughs at this fire.
Rather, one must make it yield from the water through its own kind,
By which one indeed reaches their goal; yet the best way is
That one seeks the first origin, as yet unmixed with the curse,
From which all creatures are begotten, and toward which they also incline.
And walk this path alone, but tread upon no other,
Even though there are seven of them to be found everywhere.
Of these, the first is called Mercury <note>original: "Mercurius"</note>, as is known,
He has fooled more than he has taught, when he escapes right out the chimney,
And leaves the poor gold-cook <term>Gold-cook (Gold-Koch): A derogatory term for "puffers" or false alchemists who focused only on the literal, chemical production of gold through heat, often losing their fortune in the process.</term> sitting there, so that he might sweat from great anxiety,
Because Mercury has so greatly deceived him, and drained him of all strength and sap,
Through fire, poisonous dust, and smoke, as is his constant custom.
Therefore, beware of his path, and do not stray from the right footbridge.
Pass by Saturn <note>original: "Saturnum"; in alchemy, Saturn represents the metal lead and the qualities of heaviness and melancholy.</note> as well, and beware of his outcry;
He is an old, wicked creeper, who makes one poor rather than richer:
Indeed, he has great force and power, for which reason he also despises all his brothers:
He examines all their strength sharply and precisely: do not trust him yourself.

# Chapter Twelve.

Because his greed is far too fierce, he swallows all through his cunning,
And leaves their huts bare, like a poor clod of earth.
His brother **Sol** <note>The Sun, representing Gold.</note> alone has the power to despise his strength.
**Luna** <note>The Moon, representing Silver.</note>, the goddess, likewise, will not be mastered by him.
Instead, her bath cleanses him entirely, so that he appears in the highest radiance,
Whereby **Saturnus** <note>Saturn, representing Lead.</note> becomes nobler when he is resurrected <note>original: "resuscitirt"</note>.
He who can take his sweet **Salt** from him, likewise his **Sulfur** too,
Without the violence of fire and foul smoke, and can bring these,
According to philosophical practice, to take **Mercury** <note>original: "Mercurium"</note> to himself,
He then can live contentedly, and also give something to his neighbor,
So that he can be happy with him, until they find the noble Stone,
Of which the philosophers write, though they practice this art very secretly.
As for **Jupiter** <note>Representing Tin.</note>, his **Sulfur** is greatly praised:
Yet because he is far too poor in **Salt**, and his **Mercury** has little potency <note>original: "Schmalz," literally "lard" or "fat," referring here to the rich, oily essence of the metal.</note>,
So **Saturn** cannot master him at all, unless one seals <note>original: "verkleistern"; in alchemy, this refers to "luting" or sealing a vessel with paste to prevent spirits from escaping.</note> him very well,
So that they both may harmonize and no longer depart from one another.
He who rightly understands this art will suffer no want.
**Mars** <note>Representing Iron.</note> flees and plunders in the manner of war; rarely did anyone become rich from him,
He does not spare his brothers, hence it often happens
That he completely destroys them and utterly overturns their nature.
Yet his **Sulfur** is of a noble kind, and was always compared to **Sol**,
Especially for one who can separate him quite skillfully without any suffering,
And join him with **Venus** <note>original: "Veneri," representing Copper.</note>, he will surely find so much
That he can sit quietly and content, and need not sweat through labor.
From this one can now see that if one wishes to go this way,
Wealth is indeed to be attained; yet I say therewith without fear,
That all this vanity is not equal to true wisdom.
When **Job** <note>original: "Hiob"</note> was blessed again after the **Lord** met him,
And his goods were restored, and seven sons in the same manner
Were begotten by him, yet not according to their rank and order
Rightly named, so one sees what is meant by this:
Namely, that these seven sons of **Job** were by no means as beautiful
As the three daughters whose names the Scripture mentions as a seed
Which alone can be useful and fitting for increase.
Of which the first is called **Jemima**, the second **Kezia**,
The third was named **Keren-Happuch**: whoever has these three has enough.
There are indeed three of these daughters, yet all three are only one thing;
One father from whom they sprang, as they flowed from his womb,
**Spirit, Soul, and Body one must call them: Salt, Sulfur, and Mercury;**

# Of the Mercury of the Sages.

Since it is equally common to all three, therefore all three are but one.
For this reason they are also inseparable; their seed is both feminine and masculine.
If you understand what I have said here, no worry will plague you any further,
And you will recognize clearly and purely what the <term>Philosopher's Stone</term> <note>The legendary "Stone of the Wise" (Lapis Philosophorum) sought by alchemists to transform base metals into gold and achieve spiritual perfection.</note> might be,
For which men strive so diligently, yet which is also despised by many:
This is because folly is too great, and because people are too devoid
Of true wisdom, and love only that through which they can practice malice.
But he who loves the trace of truth finds that <term>Salt</term>, <term>Sulfur</term>, and <term>Mercury</term> <note>Known as the *Tria Prima* (Three Primes), the fundamental components of all matter according to Paracelsian alchemy.</note>,
Are one in their essence, even though they are three by their names.
Through this the conclusion is now made: He who despises Salt, Sulfur, and Mercury,
Does not know his God, even though he names Him so often;
He lies buried in darkness and knows nothing at all of God’s gifts;
But to him who loves the truth, the following is given for consideration:
If he finds from the **Kabbalistic teachings** <note>original: "ex Cabbalisticis"; referring to the tradition of seeking hidden mystical meanings within sacred texts.</note> the key to the **mysteries** <note>original: "Mysticis"</note>,
Which are hidden very deeply herein, he will then, without worry,
Recognize and understand the path of how one should walk toward the truth:
For which we wish luck and salvation, so that everyone may find his share.

### Fig. I.
### En - Soph <note>Hebrew for "The Infinite" or "Without End," representing God before any self-manifestation.</note>

Is the incomprehensible <term>Ungrund</term> <note>A term used in German mysticism to describe the "groundless" or "bottomless" void of the divine that exists before all created things, even before light and dark.</note> of the Divine Majesty, of which there is no concept, neither of any spatiality nor of any times, but rather a perpetual progression of infinity, in a constantly enduring welling up of unimaginable joyfulness in its own light, without any revelation of any name. Therefore, Christ the Son of the living God also says in Matthew 19:17, Mark 10:18, and Luke 18:19: "No one is good but only one, namely GOD." Since now "GOD" [Gott] and "good" [gut] originally have the same meaning in the German language, the Lord JESUS intended to indicate through these words that this "Ungrund" of the incomprehensible Majesty is the infinite goodness or kindness—namely, that it is GOD, which is to say, Good. And so, before anything of this "Good" or GOD was revealed through Creation, there was no other concept or name for this One but "Good," which is the essential goodness, namely GOD, as Christ the LORD said in the words cited above. In the original text <note>The Hebrew Bible</note>, "good" is called <term>Tov</term> <note>original: טוֹב</note>; but by <term>Atbash</term> <note>original: "per Athbatsh"; a Hebrew cipher where the first letter of the alphabet is swapped with the last, the second with the second-to-last, etc.</note> it becomes <term>Nephesh</term> <note>original: נפש</note>, that is, "Soul." ### Fig. 4. Tohu wa-bohu (without form and void) or Lucifer. <note>The Hebrew phrase "Tohu wa-bohu" from Genesis 1:2 is often translated as "waste and void" or "chaos."</note>

This figure would not have been strictly necessary here, since it can already be found in Part I under the section on the Sun ☉ <note>The symbol ☉ represents the Sun in astrology and Gold in alchemy; here it likely refers to a specific chapter or symbolic division of the book.</note>; (see there the magical sketch of the entire world); however, to a lover of God's mysteries, it will not be superfluous. In the preceding pages, it was briefly mentioned how this fallen prince, as well as his fellow fallen angels and all other angels and spirits, were created excellently good and perfect from the very first emanation of the Divine Majesty. But because he exalted himself through the power of his glory, and wished to rule in his own world like the Almighty GOD, his Creator—outside and without GOD, by his own power for himself—he fell completely from the simplicity of the first light-essence and became a ghastly yet indescribable darkness. His origin was a Light-Agent <term>∇</term> <note>original: "Licht-Agens ∇"; the triangle ∇ is the alchemical symbol for Water, but in this context of an "Agent," the author likely uses it to denote an active elemental force.</note>; but his separation from the Divine Light transformed him, along with all his countless millions of angels, into a thick, Salt-Light Water ∇ <note>The symbol for Water.</note>, called Tohu wa-bohu, or a Chaos. Within this Chaos, the "suns" <note>referring to the vital spiritual sparks or essences</note> of all creatures of this earthly circle—those on the surface, those in the womb of the earth, as well as those in the sea and all waters—were contained, hidden, and locked away, formed according to the ideas within the *Fiat* <note>Latin: "Let it be done," referring to God's creative command.</note>. How this world of ours or solar system was separated and created from this thick, muddy, dark water through Divine Mercy, and how all the births of the Archetype <note>original: <term>Archetypi</term></note> conceived in the *Fiat* became manifest through the six days of creation—this we have reported more extensively according to the guidance of the text of Genesis in Part I under the Sun ☉. We have, therefore, only to repeat here that through Lucifer’s fall, the primordial light-essence (from which all creatures in the spirit-world were initially created) is no longer found in its original simplicity in this world. Instead, it has been specified in every creature in and on this sublunary <note>The region below the moon; the physical, changeable earth.</note> world according to its kind and property; and thus, in comparison to a higher principle, it is likewise called Gold ☉, Tin ♃, and Quicksilver ☿. He who can grasp it, let him grasp it! <margin>Matthew 19:12</margin>

If we were not accustomed to letting everyone have their own way, we would have wanted to show clearly and distinctly through this formation of the Tohu wa-bohu that Franciscus Mercurius van Helmont <note>A 17th-century Flemish nobleman and philosopher known for his unconventional kabbalistic and alchemical theories.</note> and Merode, in their thoughts on the first four chapters of Genesis, were exceedingly mistaken. His concepts of the *Adamah* <note>Hebrew for "ground" or "earth."</note>, Adam, Eve, the Garden of Eden, the Tree of Life, and the Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil—as well as his idea of the human body being composed of nothing but worms from the *Adamah*—are nothing but ill-founded whims <note>original: "Würme," literally 'worms,' used here idiomatically to mean 'fancies' or 'cranks.'</note>, and all his concepts in this matter run against the true understanding of the text. Furthermore, his translation of the original text into the languages in which his treatise was printed...

# The Main Key of the Whole Work

...only one essence <note>original: "essentialis substantia"</note>; but its manifestation and revelation are threefold, and in all infinity it is impossible to separate one of these workings from the light or flame, such that it would still remain a light or flame. But enough, and no further!

->Fig. 3. Manifestation of Divine Majesty in Jehovah Elohim. <note>The Hebrew names for God, "Jehovah" and "Elohim," represent the divine name and the creator-god aspects respectively.</note><-

The seeker will already find this figure in part in the *Opus Mago-Cabbalisticum* <note>Referring to Georg von Welling’s *Opus Mago-Cabbalisticum et Theosophicum*, a foundational 18th-century text on alchemy and mysticism</note>; however, giving a perfect explanation of it is not easily done. Almighty GOD is, without beginning or end, the highest and most perfect contentment within Himself, and outside of Him nothing existed that could have added to or increased this contentment. However, so that there might be something to share in and remain part of this glorious joy and most perfect bliss, to the praise and glory of His incomprehensible Majesty, He initially created the Spirit-World, marked here as letter B, which has been discussed extensively enough throughout the entire work as far as was possible. Now, it is said in Scripture that God created the world out of nothing; but "nothing" in its true sense is as incomprehensible and indescribable as the Godhead itself. Such a "nothing" as is taught in the schools <note>A critique of "Scholasticism," the traditional academic philosophy of the time, which the author views as overly logical and spiritually dry</note> is to be found neither in GOD nor outside of GOD. For before the creation, there was nothing but GOD everywhere, and thus nothing else but GOD; therefore, all descriptions of "nothingness" are nothing more than a miserable, pedantic sophistry. 

It follows irrefutably for an enlightened person that all creatures, by whatever name they may be called, proceeded from GOD Himself; and because GOD is the most perfect Good, it could not have been otherwise than that all creatures were, as it were, perfectly good, insofar as a part can participate in the whole. Therefore the text says in Genesis 1:31: *And behold, everything was excellently and perfectly good.* But what was this very first outflow (the so-called "nothing") of the Divine Majesty? Although it has three different names, it has no proper name by which it may be grasped; therefore it is called "Nothing." He was the most powerful prince, and around him were the other hierarchies or angelic worlds. To this, add that the stars must not be allowed to cast their rays therein; human hands must not soil it, nor must it be moved. ## Chapter I.
## Concerning Eternal Wisdom: What and Who She Actually Is.

The wise King Solomon speaks in his Proverbs, Chapter 3, verse 13, etc.: Blessed is the man who finds wisdom, and the man who gains understanding. For it is better to trade with her than for silver; and her gain is better than gold. She is more noble than pearls, and everything you may desire is not to be compared to her. Long life is in her right hand; and in her left are riches and honor. Her ways are pleasant ways, and all her paths are peace. She is a tree of life to all who grasp her; and blessed are those who hold her fast, etc. If we then ask what, or who, this wisdom actually is, of whom Solomon makes such great boast? Before the mountains were settled; before the hills, I was prepared. He had not yet made the earth and what is upon it, nor the mountains of the world. When he prepared the heavens, I was there; when he set a compass <note>original: *Ziel*, referring to the boundary or circle of the horizon</note> upon the face of the deep, when he established the clouds above, when he strengthened the fountains of the deep; when he set the limit for the sea and for the waters,

From which it is then sufficiently proven that Wisdom is indeed Christ, the Son of God, just as he also calls himself Wisdom in Matthew 11:19, Luke 7:35, and Chapter 11:49. And thus Solomon <note>the traditional author of Proverbs and the Book of Wisdom</note> had great cause to say:
> Blessed is the man who finds Wisdom, etc.

Inasmuch as in him alone our <term>salvation</term><note>German: *Heyl*; refers to spiritual health, well-being, and eternal salvation</note>, life, and <term>blessedness</term><note>German: *Seligkeit*; the state of being saved or in heavenly bliss</note> must be sought and found; and oh, woe to the person who does not seek or find Christ, who is Wisdom! For such a person is and remains most unhappy and lost, until he rouses himself and seeks her with his whole heart, and finds in her salvation, life, and blessedness.

### Chapter II.
## Concerning the Lovers of Wisdom: who they are, and how supremely blessed they are.

Having now testified somewhat in the preceding chapter—mostly with verses from Holy Scripture—concerning Wisdom, we wish now to mention in a similar manner something regarding the <term>Philosophis</term> <note>original: "Philosophis," the Latin plural for philosophers; the author defines them here specifically as "Lovers of Wisdom"</note> or Lovers of Wisdom: namely, who they are, how they are constituted, and how supremely blessed they are. And to be brief, we say that a true Philosopher or Lover of Wisdom is such a person who fears **GOD**, avoids sin, and strives with their whole heart to rightly recognize, love, honor, and remain unswervingly attached to the one true **GOD** as the original source of all life and being; to live for and serve Him alone in holiness and righteousness all the days of their life. And herein is founded and revealed all heavenly and earthly wisdom, as much as a creature may recognize and comprehend within and outside of **GOD**; in which recognition the lovers of wisdom can reach great heights through Divine Grace. For the master of the <term>Book of Wisdom</term> <note>A book of the Apocrypha, also called the Wisdom of Solomon, often cited in this period as a bridge between theology and natural science.</note> writes of this in Chapter VII:

> " **GOD** has granted me to speak wisely, 
> " and to think rightly according to such a gift of wisdom. For it is He who 
> " leads the way to wisdom and governs the wise; for in His hand 
> " are both we ourselves and our speech, as well as all prudence and skill 
> " in all manner of business. For He has given me certain knowledge of all 
> " things: so that I know how the world is made, and the power of the 
> " elements; the beginning, end, and middle of time; how the day increases 
> " and decreases; how the seasons of the year change, and how the year 
> " runs its course; how the stars are positioned. 
> " The nature of tame and wild animals; how the wind storms, and 
> " what people have in their minds; the many kinds of plants and the 
> " power of roots. I know all that is secret, for Wisdom, who is the 
> " master of all arts, teaches me."

From these words, it is already clear enough to understand who a true Philosopher is, how they are actually constituted, and how very high they can reach in knowledge. From which also follows, in part, their great blessedness...

Rejoice in the mercy of **GOD**, and be not ashamed of His praise. Do what is commanded you, because you have the time, so He will reward you well in His time.

## Chapter III.
### By what means and ways Wisdom is to be attained.

It might perhaps happen, through the grace of **GOD**, that someone reading the preceding pages would be moved to also strive after Wisdom, and therefore ask: By what means and ways is she most easily acquired? To this we answer with the words of the Apostle James, where he says in Chapter 1, verse 5: *If any of you lacks wisdom, let him ask of God, who gives generously to all and reproaches no one, and it will be given to him.* And this is thus the first and almost the only means which the wise of every age have used to attain Wisdom, according to their own testimonies. For thus writes Sirach <note>The Book of Sirach, also known as Ecclesiasticus, a book of ethical teachings from the Old Testament Apocrypha.</note>: *While I was still young, before I went astray, I sought wisdom openly in my prayer. I lifted up my hands toward heaven, and then my soul was enlightened through wisdom,* etc. And Solomon writes: *Therefore I prayed, and understanding was given to me; I called out, and the spirit of wisdom came to me,* etc.

But it is well to note here that this prayer for wisdom 1) must not be mere lip-service, but must come from the whole heart; for thus Solomon writes in Proverbs 2:3–4 regarding this: *If you call out for it with diligence and pray for it, if you seek it like silver and search for it like hidden treasure; then you will understand the fear of the LORD and find the knowledge of God; For the LORD gives wisdom, and from his mouth comes knowledge and understanding,* etc. And Sirach writes: *I pursued her earnestly, my heart yearned for her,* etc. Chapter 51. And the author of the Book of Wisdom writes: *But when I perceived that I could not otherwise possess her <note>In the original German "züchtig," referring here to the self-control or purity required to house Divine Wisdom.</note> unless God gave her to me, I approached the Lord and prayed to him, and said with all my heart:*

> O **GOD** of my fathers, and **LORD** of all goodness, who have made all things through your word, and have prepared mankind through your wisdom, that he should rule over the creatures made by you, that he should govern the world with holiness and righteousness, and judge with an upright heart. Give me the wisdom that sits by your throne, and do not reject me from among your children. Send her down from your holy heaven, and from the throne of your glory; send her, that she may be with me and work with me, so that I may recognize what is pleasing to you: For she knows all things.

That the word **seeking** means this: that one strives to obtain a thing that one does not have, is known to everyone. The nobler and more precious a thing is, and the more we love it, the greater is the earnestness and diligence we apply in seeking it. And since Wisdom is the most noble, precious, and lovable good—in the absence of which we are most miserable, but in the possession of which we shall be and remain most blessed, in time and in eternity—we must necessarily seek her with the greatest earnestness and diligence.

2) We must love her and her beauty, choose her as our only treasure and portion, and surrender and sacrifice our love and whole heart to her, with the firm resolution to suffer and endure everything for her sake. 
3) We must also, for her sake, truly and in fact renounce not only the world with its lusts, but also our very selves with all that we have and possess; we must deny ourselves and strive only to do her will, and to become right pleasing and well-pleasing to her in all things. From which then 
4) follows quite directly: that we lead a holy, virtuous life, and through **divine grace** arrange our whole conduct and life so that we may come somewhat closer to her, as if in every step and stride we take, until she finally, after she has sufficiently tested us...

Instead of the external word and teacher, they must strive to hear Christ, the living Word, and His Spirit within themselves. # Appendix
## of various rare Chemical Manuscripts.

### I.
### Discourse on the Philosopher’s Stone, which Dr. Hensing at Giessen prefaced to his public chemical demonstrations in the month of November 1722. <note>original: "Discurs von dem Stein der Weisen, welchen D. Hensing zu Giessen, seinen Demonstrationibus chemicis publicis præmittiret hat, Mense Nov. 1722." Dr. Johann Thomas Hensing (1683–1726) was a notable professor of medicine and a pioneer in chemical research at the University of Giessen.</note>

->§. 1.<-

Among those things worthy of contemplation, there are two which, above all others, hold the prize of highest excellence, the fame of greatest importance, and the universal testimony of the most certain utility; and they are therefore well worth being sought with an unwavering earnestness, with a well-ordered understanding and deliberation, and without vain fantasy, and being praised according to their merit.

§. 2. I mean, firstly: That place and state wherein we may be well forever and ever; and then, secondly: the means to live in this world without sickness and want. The first is known to us all under the title of the Kingdom of God and Blessedness; the second has been called at all times the <term>Philosopher’s Stone</term> <note>original: "Lapis philosophorum." In alchemy, this legendary substance was believed to be capable of turning base metals into gold and acting as an elixir of life to cure all diseases.</note>, that is, the Stone of the Wise.

§. 3. However, when something is generally spoken of with the harshest discord, and is sought in the greatest disorder, with blindness, without understanding, and without proper means and ways, experience shows that it is precisely these two praised things.

§. 4. For regarding the first, we need only consider the atheists, idolaters, hypocrites, and religious sects, and the truth of my statement will fall into anyone's hands without effort, and the Gentlemen Theologians will be able to show this more extensively; therefore, I do not wish to dwell on it. Rather, my current contemplation shall be occupied with the <term>Philosopher’s Stone</term> <note>original: "Lap. Ph." / "Lapis Philosophorum."</note>.

<meta>catchword: §. 5.</meta>

<summary>This page introduces an appendix of chemical manuscripts, beginning with a 1722 discourse by Dr. Johann Thomas Hensing. Hensing parallels the search for spiritual salvation with the search for the Philosopher's Stone, framing both as the most vital but often misunderstood pursuits of humanity.</summary>

§. 5. It is true that for time immemorial much has been written regarding this precious stone, as is clearly evident from the writings of the excellently learned and experienced **OLAI BORRICHII** <note>original: "Olai Borrichii." Olaus Borrichius (1626–1690) was a Danish polymath, chemist, and physician who defended the antiquity of alchemy.</note> against **URSINUS**, **KIRCHER**, and **CONRINGIUS** <note>These were prominent scholars who were often skeptical of alchemical claims: Adam Ursinus, Athanasius Kircher, and Hermann Conring.</note>. However, since in this day and age gold and silver—as the primary material of wealth—have been brought to the wrong places through misuse and arrogance, and have consequently begun to vanish from the mints, leading to an outbreak of universal poverty, the blind desire for the <term>Stone</term> <note>original: "Lap." abbreviation for Lapis (Stone).</note> has also sought to become almost universal. Therefore, in just a few years, so many discourses have been produced on the subject that one can read over 8,000 to 10,000 books about it. And if one looks around a little in both the old and the new world, one will find that many emperors, kings, princes, nobles, and common folk—learned and unlearned, even craftspeople, soap-boilers, stocking-knitters, and so forth—have been and still are occupied with the Stone. Indeed, the matter has become so common that even the lowliest charcoal-burners know how to reason about it. On the other hand, there are also many people who regard this Stone as a pure chimera and a worthless work; they not only fight against it with all manner of rational arguments but also consider those people to be fools who merely wish to suggest its possibility. Thus, among others, Cardinal **PERRONIUS** <note>Jacques Davy Duperron (1556–1618), a French cardinal and diplomat.</note> says: *Deplorable are the minds that are occupied with investigating the squaring of the circle, perpetual motion, and the Philosopher’s Stone.* <note>original: "deplorata sunt ingenia, quæ in investiganda quadratura Circuli, perpetuo mobili, & Lapide Philoſophorum occupantur." These were the three great "impossible" quests of the early modern era.</note> These are wretched people who wish to seek the squaring of the circle, perpetual motion, and the Philosopher's Stone.

§. 6. But it is curious that there are not a few who are afraid to openly support the Stone, and therefore disparage the Art and its artists, yet secretly pursue the making of gold. We have a remarkable example of this in the world-renowned and sharp-witted Chancellor of England, **FRANCIS BACON, LORD VERULAM**, who here and there in his writings sharply attacks chemistry, while in the meantime he sought the precious Art with great desire in his own home.

§. 7. Furthermore, it is a certain historical fact that previously in France, alchemy was strictly forbidden; and yet the current Regent <note>Philippe II, Duke of Orléans, who served as Regent of France from 1715 to 1723 and was known for his interest in chemistry and alchemy.</note> has himself encouraged those members of the Royal Society who cultivate chemistry to investigate the renowned Philosopher's Stone. And who does not know that within the Papacy the Art is forbidden under high penalty, and yet nowhere is more fire lit for its sake than in the very monasteries themselves.

§. 8. In such matters, it happens very easily that one falls into two extremes: either one judges the matter too mildly and falls into light-headed credulity, or one blindly despises everything and mocks it against all reason. Now, because such behavior is very unseemly for an intelligent man, I have

I have deemed it appropriate, for this occasion, to say enough concerning the world-famous Philosopher’s Stone so that my highly honored gentlemen may form a correct concept of it and avoid all misfortune.

§. 9. Now, if you consider this matter worthy of your kind attention, I will briefly explain the following points for this occasion: (1.) What is the <term>Philosopher’s Stone</term>? <note>original: "L. P." for Lapis Philosophorum.</note> Is its preparation possible, and are the powers attributed to it believable? (2.) Why do so few people attain it? (3.) The foolish and ill-considered actions that seekers of the <term>Stone</term> <note>original: "Lap." for Lapis.</note> commonly undertake. (4.) Whether it is advisable for anyone to involve themselves in this art?

§. 10. So that we do not reason about color like a blind man, we must first clearly understand what the <term>Philosopher’s Stone</term> actually is, in the true sense.

§. 11. Namely, it is a body which is composed through art from a highly purified, <term>animated Mercury</term> <note>Mercury that has been "quickened" or prepared specifically for alchemical work.</note> and a <term>living Gold</term>, and is so joined together by a long-lasting fire that it can never again be separated. In this form, it can instantly ripen, purify, and <term>fix</term> <note>To "fix" a metal means to make it stable and resistant to fire, a key step in transmutation.</note> the other metals so that they are raised into the nature of the purest gold. So that everything may be rightly understood, I will take the trouble to explain all points of the definition in detail.

§. 12. Firstly, I say the <term>Philosopher’s Stone</term> is a body made by art. It is true that this art is called *Gold-making* <note>original: "Chrysopœia."</note> nowadays, but this is done *improperly* <note>original: "abusive."</note>; for we do not make gold, says **GEBER** <note>Geber refers to Jabir ibn Hayyan, a legendary 8th-century polymath whose writings formed the foundation of medieval alchemy.</note>, but we only serve nature by preparing its own materials so that it can accomplish the final goal of the greatest purity. Others call the art *Alchemy* <note>original: "Alchymiam."</note>, but also *improperly* <note>original: "improprie."</note>, for this is much more occupied with the division of natural bodies and has many subjects and many goals. On the other hand, the basic rules of our art are rightly called *Hermetic Philosophy* <note>original: "Philosophia Hermetica."</note>, the art itself the *Hermetic Art* <note>original: "Ars Hermetica."</note>, and those artists who have actually worked out the <term>Stone</term> are called *Adept Philosophers* <note>original: "Philosophi adepti."</note>, or also simply and preeminently *Philosophers*. And these have no further work than to purify and unite. Nor do they deal with anything other than the <term>Center</term> of <term>Mercury</term> and Gold. The <term>Product</term> is finally a wonderful body, a house of light, the most fixed, incombustible sulfur of nature, easily melted in <term>Fire</term> <note>original: "Δ", the alchemical symbol for fire.</note>, and finally the <term>Seed of Gold</term> <note>original: "☉ Saamen." The symbol ☉ represents the Sun or Gold.</note>, a medicine for humans and metals. Those who claim to have seen this stone, such as **FRIEDERICH GALLUS** <note>Likely referring to the mysterious alchemist Federico Gualdi.</note> in his journey to the wilderness of St. Michael, say that it is a stone or powder that shines brightly by night but is a transparent blood-red by day; others assure us that

For I have said that its *constituent parts* are a highly-purified-animated Mercury <note>represented by the symbol ☿</note> and a living Gold; we must examine these things a little more closely.

§. 13. First, a Mercury <note>original: "☿ii"</note> is considered. Here it is generally known that there is a very old saying: In Mercury is everything that the wise seek. Furthermore, the ancient Geber <note>The Latinized name of Jabir ibn Hayyan, a foundational figure in alchemy.</note> cries out in his *Consideration of things from which the perfection of the Mastery is made, Book M. Chapter VI:* *“Praise be to the blessed God, who created Mercury and gave it a substance and properties of substance which no other thing in nature happens to possess, so that in it this perfection might be found through some artifice, which we find in it as a near potentiality.”* <note>original Latin: "Laudetur Deus benedictus, qui creavit Mercurium, & dedit ei Substantiam & Substantiæ proprietates, quas non contigit ullam ex rebus in natura possidere, ut in illo possit inveniri, hæc perfectio per artificium aliquod, quod in illo invenimus in potentia propinqua."</note> If we now ask *specifically*, what kind of Mercury is this? And where is it to be sought and found most closely? The *Philosophers* in their writings make such strange descriptions and so many detours that one might lose one's wit and reason. But if one searches with untiring diligence for the *concordance* and agreement of the *Philosophers* and follows nature, the following truths are found, which, to avoid long-windedness, I will include in short *Axioms*. (1.) The one purpose and effect of the Philosopher's Stone <note>original: "L. P." for Lapis Philosophorum.</note> is the multiplication and *generation* of gold. (2.) All multiplication and *generation of a species* happens *through a similar species*: That is, like generates its like: Thus a lion generates a lion and not an elephant; a human a human and not a bear; an ox an ox and not an ape or a long-tailed monkey; wheat does not come from barley, nor turnip seeds from grain. (3.) Everything that is to multiply must have its own seed, and every seed requires its own suitable *matrix* <note>A "matrix" refers to a womb or a nurturing environment/vessel.</note>, if the seed is not to be spoiled or produce false *products* against the nature of things. Therefore, no farmer is so foolish as to sow his grain on marble or throw his barley into a swampy puddle; rather, he prepares his field carefully and entrusts the fruits to it. And who would consider a farmer wise who has sown poppy seeds and wants to harvest wheat? (4.) All seed, if it is to become fruitful, must first be whole and uninjured according to its *structure* and *mixture*; then its outer and inner parts must be dissolved and made fluid by proper moisture. Moreover, a proportioned heat must put this *solution* <note>The process of dissolving a solid into a liquid state.</note> into effect; that is: bring it to a perfect deed and move everything. No less must the air be added in the right measure, so that the heat is not smothered and the *solution* and *circulation* of the juices is not prevented. For these reasons, no flour grows: grain does not turn green on a dry granary floor; no barley blooms in winter; and no fruit is to be hoped for under the earth or in an *air pump* <note>original: "Antlia pnevmatica," a scientific instrument used to create a vacuum.</note>. (5.) The moisture which the

For example: a rabbit cannot come from oats; a "beer-tree" cannot grow from the seed of a fox. Just as the vegetable and animal kingdoms each have their own particular seeds, matrices <note>the "womb" or environment where something grows</note>, methods of generation, and life, and nothing exists or originates outside of its own kind: so too is the **mineral kingdom** established for itself, and is as different from the others as the heavens are from the earth. Therefore, when one speaks in this kingdom of seeds, life, death, growth, multiplication, matrix, moisture, warmth, air, and the like, all of this must be understood according to the character and nature of minerals.

§. 14. Now, the <term>Hermetic Philosophers</term> <note>alchemists following the tradition of Hermes Trismegistus</note> seek, as their second aim <note>original: "fine secundo"</note>, the multiplication of gold. Thus they must (1.) have a **golden seed**. (2.) There must be a proper **liquid**. (3.) They must have suitable **matrices** or fields. To recognize these, however, we will follow brief rules. (1.) According to its qualities, gold is the most fire-stable, purest, and heaviest being in the three kingdoms. According to its substance, it is a body so coagulated out of the purest and most fixed <term>Mercury</term>, <term>Sulfur</term> <note>original: "$\text{\sout{S}}$re"</note>, and **SALT** <note>original: "SALE"</note> that these principles—except for the third—cannot be separated from one another by either art or nature.

§. 15. If, therefore, according to the order of nature, the seed must be of the same essence as the fruit (as we have briefly heard), then according to the **opinion of the true Philosophers**, it is true that the seed of gold must not be sought on a thorn-bush or in a dung-beetle—that is, not in combustible, volatile, vegetable, animal, sulfurous, or arsenical things and so forth—but rather in gold itself. (2.) However, gold is **dead** as soon as it is melted out of its ore; that is, it cannot bring about any multiplication on its own, because it only contains as much "fruit" as is necessary for the stability of its own essence, just as we heard concerning grain stored in a loft. (3.) If it is therefore to be made **living** as a seed, its "radical moisture" <note>the fundamental life-fluid of a substance</note> must be opened up and increased with something of its own kind. (4.) Its radical moisture is <term>mercury</term> <note>represented by the symbol ☿</note>, which is coagulated by its sulfur and locked in stony bonds or husks, as is clear from the first rule. (5.) Thus, the <term>Solvent of Gold</term> <note>original: "Solvens Auri"</note> must also be a <term>mercury</term> <note>original: "☿"</note>. (6.) So this <term>mercury</term> <note>original: "☿"</note> must be sought in the mineral kingdom, and with the exclusion of the vegeta-

§. 16. However, so that we do not go astray in such a search, I will once again draw certain **Axioms** <note>fundamental principles or self-evident truths</note> from the true philosophers: (1.) Our **solvent** <note>original: "ſolvens"</note> and our water (they say) is a metallic, heavy, bright-shining **liquid** <note>original: "Liquor"</note> that does not wet the hands. (2.) Furthermore, our water has a close affinity with metals; therefore, it mixes with them precisely and is very reluctant to leave them. (3.) After its preparation, our water either leaves entirely in the fire as a volatile **spirit** <note>original: "spiritus"</note> or remains entirely constant within it. (4) Our water, when united in the proper measure with gold and silver, makes them volatile, and likewise becomes fire-constant with them. When we look around in all of nature, we find no **liquid** <note>original: "Liquorem"</note> which possesses the aforementioned qualities for the most part, even in its raw state, other than (**pay attention, Pamphilus!** <note>original: "arrige aures Pamphile!" - a Latin phrase from the playwright Terence meaning "listen closely!"</note>) the **mercury** <note>original: "Queckſilber" or the symbol ☿</note> known to all people. But now the confusion truly begins; for everyone rejects the common mercury, and thus some want to have a **Mercury of the Bodies** <note>original: "☿ Corporum"</note>, that is, of the **Metals** <note>original: "Metallorum"</note>, made from gold and silver, while others fish for it out of all the elements, upon which many hundreds of thousands [of coins] have been squandered. That is called fetching a thing from India which lies right before our feet. Therefore, so that this confusion may not harm us, I will again select short teachings of the philosophers. (1.) The excellent author of the *Secrets of Hermetic Philosophy* <note>original: "Arcani Philosophiæ Hermeticæ"</note> confirms the opinion of Geber <note>an 8th-century alchemist</note> when he says: Whoever regards common mercury, as it is by nature and in its entire substance, **as the radical solvent of gold** <note>original: "pro ſolvente radicali auri"</note>, deceives himself and others; but whoever, on the contrary, rejects common mercury entirely, acts against the truth. (2.) Whoever can draw from mercury its purest substance and free it from its residue and "dropsy" <note>original: "Waſſerſucht" - referring to watery, non-metallic impurities</note> is on the nearest path to finding our mercury. (3.) Whoever can increase the innate internal sulfur of mercury according to the right weight, then has the true key, the right water and <term>menstruum</term> <note>a solvent used to dissolve solids</note>, to separate the **sulfur** <note>original: symbol △</note> and **mercury** <note>original: symbol ☿</note> of gold from their tightly locked, stony shells and to make them living or active.

§. 17. See, this is the precious water which has been given so many different names by the philosophers to ensnare fools, and which I, without envy and openheartedly, have called a "highly purified animated mercury" in the definition above—as much as I have been able to research from more than 400 books through tireless study and experimentation.

§. 18. Now we will also consider the **living gold**. Common gold is, as already mentioned, entirely passive and as if dead: furthermore, it has partly innate foreign additions, and partly there are additions added to it by the craftsmen...

Therefore, the **philosophers** <note>alchemists often referred to themselves simply as "the philosophers"</note> certainly reject common gold, but not gold itself; rather, they teach how to cleanse and purify it from all additives by means of the "devouring mineral wolf," which is <term>antimony</term> <note>represented by the symbol ♁; it was called the "wolf" because it "devours" or reacts with base metals to leave pure gold behind</note>, or through <term>quartation</term> <note>a process of refining gold by alloying it with silver and then separating them</note>, **solutions** and **precipitations**, **cementations**, and so forth. Then they regard it as the **immediate matter** <note>original: "Materiam proximam"</note>, from which the **Sulphur of the Philosophers** <note>original: "△ Philosophorum"</note> must first be made before the **Stone** <note>original: "Lapis"</note> or true gold-seed is set free.

Specifically, they take one **quintel** <note>a small unit of weight, roughly 4 grams</note> (one does not need pounds of gold as the fraudsters claim) of the purified gold that has been made into a subtle powder, and with three quintels of the **philosophical mercury** <note>original: "☿ii"</note> taught above, they make an exquisite **amalgam**. This is a **mass** which can be handled with the hands like soft butter. They place this into a proportionate glass vial, which is called the "external philosophical egg," and which is and acts in its own way just as the shell of an animal egg does. Then they close the vial tightly at the top so that no more air can enter or leave than is necessary. And then, in a spacious furnace, they provide the proper heat without ceasing, day and night, for nine months. During this time, the gold becomes volatile with the mercury and, according to the **philosophers' way of speaking**, is brought into **prime matter** <note>original: "primam materiam", the formless base of all substance</note>. 

Meanwhile, so many wonderful colors appear—from blackness to whiteness, and from whiteness to redness—and **consequently** so many altered states of the joined mercury and gold, that the philosophers cannot describe them sufficiently: until finally the gold gains the upper hand and binds the mercury to itself in such a way that it can never again be separated by any power of fire, water, or air. Now the first wheel has turned; however, the **Stone** is still far from finished. Instead, the **Sulphur of the Philosophers** <note>original: "△ Philosoph."</note> has first been prepared, which as yet does nothing else but further awaken the "dead" gold, making it rich in blood and seed. Then, when one combines this **Sulphur** with gold, adds the **Philosophical Mercury** to it, and cooks it for seven to nine months just as the first time, one finally obtains the highly praised **Stone of the Wise** in the form of the true seed of gold, which can be multiplied many millions of times over. Thus, let us now look at the "field" in which this seed is planted.

§. 20. Because everything happens in the **fire**, whose actions and operations proceed much faster than those of air and water. In this very same way, a seed can be prepared from silver which brings the aforementioned bodies to its own nature. Finally, it is to be noted regarding this alone: that the way explained thus far is called the **dry path** by the philosophers. They do indeed also have a **wet path**, but it is kept so secret by them that no man can become wise to it from their writings. Therefore, we will not involve ourselves with it. It is enough that my most gracious gentlemen have clearly heard from the preceding discourse not only what the **Philosopher's Stone** is, but also that its preparation is possible and its power is credible.

...master teacher. <note>original: "Lehr-Meister"</note> (2.) A certain amount of time. (3.) A certain disposition of the understanding and the body. (4.) A clever and constant practice. (5.) Proper materials <note>original: "Materialia"</note> and instruments <note>original: "Instrumenta"</note>. (6.) A suitable location. Where one or another of these circumstances is lacking, no art is learned—or at the very least, no perfection is attained. For example, if someone wishes to become a land-surveyor <term>Feld-Messer; a specialist who measures and maps land boundaries</term>, he must have an intelligent, experienced master <note>original: "Maître"</note> who first explains to him the types of fields according to their simple surface, or districts composed of mountain, valley, and plain; and then according to their shape, whether they are triangular, square, five-, six-, or multi-sided. This master then shows him the instruments—the rods, squares, plane tables <note>original: "Mensulas prætorianas"</note>, and the like—and instructs him in their nature for various uses, and finally shows him the practice alongside the theory. (2.) A student of geometry <note>original: "Studiosus Geometriæ"</note> must devote not just a single hour, but sufficient time to the learning of these things. (3.) His mind must be equipped with arithmetic. (4.) He must have good eyes in his head to see, and good feet for walking. (5.) Good instruments are necessary, so that the measuring rod is not crooked, the plane table is finely polished, and the quadrant is accurately <note>original: "accurat"</note> divided; otherwise, all operations are in vain. (6.) But what do you think will become of the apprentice if he is satisfied with the instruction of his teacher <note>original: "Præceptoris"</note> and remains sitting behind the stove? Must he not diligently go out into the field and, in all places thereof, partly see the operations <note>original: "Operationes"</note> himself and partly perform them himself, so that he may be well-practiced?

§. 23. Now let us apply this to our art. If there is an art in the world that requires deep knowledge, or which necessitates hidden, subtle manual techniques, it is certainly the Hermetic Art <term>Ars Hermetica; the art of alchemy, named after Hermes Trismegistus</term>. But where are the skillful and faithful master teachers who might help us lift the heavy stones? There are books enough, but what help are they? Firstly, they are obscure; secondly, I would like to see the preacher, lawyer <note>original: "Advocatum"</note>, mathematician, or physician who becomes wise and skillful in his chosen profession through books alone. What a mess <note>original: "Geschirr"</note> such self-taught people <note>original: "Autodidacti"</note> often make, and why are they held in such low regard? Meanwhile, why is it that no living master teachers—or only very few—are to be found in the Hermetic Art? I will briefly state the cause: If one is an adept philosopher <term>Philosophus adeptus; an alchemist who has successfully discovered the Philosopher's Stone</term> and lets it be known, his freedom and life are immediately lost. People seize him by the head and torment his soul to make gold. You may read of the famous **PHILALETHES’** **Fates** <note>Refers to Eirenaeus Philalethes, a famous 17th-century alchemist, and his work "The Open Entrance to the Closed Palace of the King"</note> in his "Open Palace," and you will marvel at the wickedness of the world. Indeed, what shall I say? If one cannot even practice the innocent, noble chemistry <note>original: "Chymie"</note> with understanding and proper order within one's office, then persecution after persecution follows. The Devil rages at once; gold-maker, chemist, murderer, poison, poison, sharp and unsafe medicines—these will be...

(1.) Because they do not bring the necessary understanding with them. For a **disciple of Hermes** <term>Discipulus Hermetis; a student of the Hermetic arts or alchemy, named after the legendary sage Hermes Trismegistus</term> must first and foremost be a good **theologian** <note>original: "Theologus"</note>, so that he knows how to conduct himself toward God and neighbor in such a way that misfortune and curses do not pursue him. Furthermore, he must be an exquisite **moralist** <note>original: "Moralist"</note>, so that he can especially keep his **passions** <note>original: "Affecten"</note> in check, lest he fall into blind greed. Finally, he must be a complete **physicist** <note>original: "Physicus"</note> according to all branches of natural science, knowing the content, nature, and power of all bodies, so that he does not, like a will-o'-the-wisp, fall into work now upon gold and now upon filth. And then he must have a complete understanding and **practice** <note>original: "praxin"</note> in the entirety of common chemistry, so that he does not try to accomplish with it what must be achieved through the secret arts. See what kind of man the **adept philosopher** <term>Philosophus adeptus; a master who has successfully attained the secret of the philosopher's stone</term> must be, and whether a tailor's apprentice could suddenly become such a one, even if he involves himself with **chemistry**: but enough of that!

§. 24. Moreover, the **disciples** <note>original: "Discipuli"</note> of the so-called "Gold-Art" usually do not devote the proper time to it. For when they have read through one or two **authors** <note>original: "Autores"</note> once, they think they are skilled enough, and imagine that as quickly as they have learned the art, just as hastily can gold be made, from which one **absurdity** <note>original: "Absurdum"</note> after another is born. And such people measure their understanding with far too large a yardstick, flattering themselves that they can pick out the single truth from the dark riddles and **contradictions** <note>original: "Contradictionibus"</note> of the **philosophers**, even though one has enough to do when trying to reach one's goal using clearly written books. Regarding the lack of knowledge of the right **matter** <note>original: "Materia"</note>, the true **regimen** <note>original: "Regiminis"; the method of governing the alchemical fire or process</note>, as well as a suitable location, I will say nothing for now, but only consider that the main cause is the will of God, whom it has pleased to create gold and silver without **decay** <note>original: "Corruption"</note> and indeed in such **quantity** <note>original: "Quantität"</note> that all people, even if ten times more were living, would have enough until the end of the world; if only greed did not soon rake everything into one place, wastefulness soon scatter everything, and finally pride consume many millions and turn them into nothing.

When I consider this carefully, I come to the thought that a true **spirit of dizziness** <note>or "delusional spirit"</note> has been sent out among those **seeking gold**, which persuades them today to choose **Gold** <term>☉; the sun/gold</term>, tomorrow **Silver** <term>☽; the moon/silver</term>, and the day after that something else as the **matter of the Stone** <note>original: "materia Lapidis," the raw material needed to create the Philosopher's Stone</note>. Thus, in their searching, they always remain hopeful, but when they hope most confidently, they are most dangerously deceived in, by, and through that very hope. But this is the third proposition, which must now be explained: Those who practice the **Hermetic Art** against the teachings of the **true philosophers** were once called **Sophists**, but nowadays they are called **Alchemists**.

§. 25. Among these, several have noticed that **Mercury** <term>☿; quicksilver</term> is no ordinary water, but that something great must be hidden within it; therefore, they have taken it into their hands. Various men have tried to **fix** <note>original: "figiren," meaning to turn a volatile substance into a solid that can withstand fire</note> it just as it is, wanting to turn it quickly into gold and silver. However, the **Mockingbird** <note>The author personifies Mercury as a "Spottvogel" because of its tendency to "fly away" as vapor, mocking the chemist's efforts</note> not only shattered their glasses but even strong iron spheres; it flew up in smoke and left behind an empty nest. Yet, when it was handled somewhat more modestly, it did indeed leave its fluid form and, after a long time, became a powder. However, at the first opportunity, it took up its wings again and remained **Mercury** as before.

Others indeed believed the word of the **philosophers** that **Mercury** in its **crudity and impurity** was worth nothing; therefore, they sought to purify it with **Salt** <term>🜔</term>, vinegar, lye, and the like. They mixed it with **Salt** <term>🜔</term>, **Vitriol** <term>🜕</term>, **Sal ammoniac** <term>🜹</term>, and **Fire** <term>🜂</term>; afterward, they **sublimated** <note>the process of heating a substance until it vapors and then collects again as a solid</note> it ten, twenty, or many more times. But when they brought it back to life <note>returned it to its liquid, metallic state</note>, it was and remained **leprous** <note>original: "aussäßig"; a technical alchemical term for metals contaminated with base impurities</note>, and for all that heavy labor, **all was for naught** <note>original: "Hopfen und Malz verlohren," literally "hops and malt are lost," a German idiom for a wasted effort</note>.

§. 26. Afterward, it happened that some were even more sharp-sighted, recognizing that the **salts** did not strike at the heart of metallic things and thus could not purify the **Mercury** **to its core** <note>original: "centraliter"</note>, much less replace the still-missing **Fire** <term>🜂</term>. Therefore, they fell upon the metals; they mixed the **Mercury** with them, **amalgamated**, **distilled**, **sublimated**, boiled, and roasted them, but the end result was a zero. When the **Mercury** had been **vexed** <note>tormented or agitated</note>, so to speak, with good and bad words to no benefit, they abandoned it and turned to the metals. And indeed, for a long time, a **salt-like essence** and even a running **Mercury** were sought from **Gold** <term>☉</term>, **Silver** <term>☽</term>, **Lead** <term>♄</term>, **Tin** <term>♃</term>, and **Iron** <term>♂</term>; but partly in vain, and partly without use.

§. 27. After that, the **Soul** <note>original: "Anima"</note> or the **Fire** <term>🜂</term> of Gold and the other metals was supposed to have done the work. Then began a process of **cementing**, **calcining**, **dissolving** in **Royal Fountains** <note>original: "Fontibus Regalibus," likely referring to Aqua Regia, a mixture of acids that can dissolve gold</note>, **oil of Lead** <term>♄</term>, **volatilizing** with **acidic spirits** <unclear>$\ddagger$dis</unclear>, **urinous spirits**, **extracting** with **radical vinegars**, and the like. They tormented themselves with the so-called **Purple Mantle** of **BASILIUS VALENTINUS** <note>A famous 15th-century legendary alchemist; the "Purple Mantle" refers to the final red stage of the alchemical process</note>, so that many thousands were...

...wasted, and blown into the air, even wedded with ash and filth; in short: gold and silver were expected to allow themselves to be separated from that in which their very essence consists, and the other metals were expected to give up what they themselves do not possess. §. 28. However, when they obtain an **arsenical sublimate**, or a **sulfuric water**, or even a **saline powder** through many dangerous labors, they are already richer in hope than **Croesus** <note>A king of Lydia legendary for his wealth</note>, but in reality poorer than **Irus** <note>The stereotypical beggar from Homer's Odyssey</note>. Now the cry is: "We see clearly that the **metals** and metallic ores are locked too tightly; we must go to the **intermediate minerals** and to the **salts**, for there the **Sulfur** <term>△; the active, combustible principle</term> and **Mercury** <term>☿; the fluid, volatile principle</term> of **gold** <note>original: "auri"</note> lie open and can be extracted quite easily." 

Then, my highly esteemed gentlemen, you would see with amazement how the **arsenic** eats the clothes off the laborers' bodies, and even their beards and skin. How the **mercury** <term>☿</term> rewards the sophists with catarrhs, consumption, suffocations, and strokes, instead of gold. How the **mercury** <term>☿</term> gnaws at their very bones. If lime, bismuth, zinc, cobalt, or cinnabar could speak, they could not tell enough wonders of how they are treated now kindly, now cruelly, and how they secretly enter the bodies of the alchemists—just as the Devil once entered the swine of the Gadarenes <note>A reference to the biblical miracle where demons were cast into a herd of pigs</note>—so that they run in heaps into the sea, by which I mean, into the kingdom of the dead. 

But what shall I say of the **Salts**? Because common kitchen salt is said to have the benefit of an excellent **balsam of life** in the human body, it must also be suitable for the **Philosopher's Stone** <note>original: "L. P." for Lapis Philosophorum</note>; because **Saltpeter** <term>⊖</term> shows great power in sulfuric things, especially in gunpowder, it must also be able to open the hard-bolted lock of nature. Because **Alum** <term>⊖</term> is very useful for dyeing cloth, does it follow <note>original: "ergo"</note> that it is abundantly filled with the **Sulfur** <term>△</term> and **Mercury** <term>☿</term> of the **Sun** <note>original: "Solis," referring to gold</note>? **What things, of what kind, and how great—could you keep from laughing, friends?** <note>original Latin: "Quæ, qualis quanta Risum teneatis amici." A quote from Horace's Art of Poetry</note>. Yet these things are treated with all seriousness and zeal.

§. 29. The follies already recounted are foolish enough, but they are not all of them, for there are even more **absurd ones**. Just listen: When a certain King in Egypt, called **Khalid** <note>original: "Calid," referring to the historical/legendary Khalid ibn Yazid</note>, was discussing the **Stone** with the **philosopher Morienus**, and asked too precisely about the secret preparation of **mercury** <term>☿</term>, the latter answered the King out of craftiness—and because he did not dare to flatly refuse the King a direct answer: "**This thing is extracted from you.**" <note>original: "Hæc res ex Te extrahitur."</note> Thereupon, the clever sophists reasoned in all haste: "There we have the...

# Appendix.

...the nest where the golden eggs lie; why have we been so foolish for so long? Is man not a *microcosm* <note>original: "microcosmus"; the idea that the human body is a "little world" that mirrors the laws and composition of the entire universe</note>? Is he not, like the great world, composed of the four elements? Do we not see daily that stones grow within him <note>a reference to kidney or bladder stones</note>? Did it not once happen in Silesia that a golden tooth was found in a head? Well then, why should the primary essence of gold not be found within him? O blessed Morienus! <note>A legendary 7th-century alchemist said to have taught the secrets of the Stone to King Khalid ibn Yazid</note> You have rescued us from all error. But no sooner did these good gentlemen delight in this excellent discovery than new *doubts* <note>original: "Dubia"</note> arose. But where (they ask) is the place in man where the *ore* <note>original: "Minera"</note> of such great treasure lies? In such doubt, blood, hair, *urine, excrement*, bones, marrow, and yet other things were taken from the human; but the saying of **ARNOLD OF VILLANOVA** <note>A famous 13th-century physician and alchemist</note> always proved true: *He who seeks in dung will find dung.* <note>original: "Qui in merdis quærit, merdam inveniet"</note>

§. 30. Then came **HELWIGH**, who wanted to be the cleverest of all; at least he was not as filthy as the others, for he flattered himself and wanted to persuade the whole world that he had found the right *ore* in the mouth. At first, he did not proceed very clearly, but the password was *Visaliena Tessæ*, which was shortly understood to mean the *Essence of Saliva* <note>original: "Essentia Salivæ"; Helwigh used an anagram to hide his "secret" ingredient</note>; with that, the whole of philosophy came to an end. Finally, it became known that **Aristotle** had said that *species* <note>distinct types of matter</note> could not be *transmuted* unless they were first changed back into *primary matter* <note>original: "erste Materie" or "primam Materiam"; the formless, raw substance from which all things are made</note>. The philosophical saying also became known: that gold must first be brought into *primary matter* before it can perform the wonders attributed to it. Now pay attention, for we are about to catch the right hare by the ear. If something—so the eager artists now reason—is to be *reduced into primary matter*, it must lose all its *specific form* and become like an undetermined substance. If this is to happen, we must look for a powerful-acting spiritual essence which, while having no material form itself, possesses all the forms of the world in its power: and thus can not only rob bodies of their innate form but also introduce the *form of transmutation* according to the artist's wish and disposition. As whimsical as this philosophy is in theory, it turns out just as foolish in *practice*. Some stay safely on the ground so they do not fall from a height and say: the earth is the *womb and uterus that receives the influences of the heavens.* <note>original: "matrix, & uterus recipiens influentias Cæli"</note> Therefore, *that universal spirit, or the archeus <note>vital life force</note> of the world soul* <note>original: "Spiritus ille universalis, sive mundi anima archæus"</note> is *solidified* <note>original: "coagulatur"</note> in the earth and found there in a *solid state*. For this reason, they dig and seek out "bolar" <note>clay-like</note> fatty earths from soil that has never been plowed, exposing it to the rays of the sun, moon, and stars for several months. Finally, they leach the earth or distill it; in the end, they obtain either a <term>gold</term> <note>symbolized by the sun ☉ in the original</note> or German saltpeter, or a similar water, which they could have bought in *abundance*, cheaper and better, at the apothecary.

<meta>This page continues the author's skepticism regarding the methods of alchemy. On the previous page, he mocked those seeking the Philosopher's Stone in human biological materials. # Appendix.

§. 31. Others fish such precious things out of the air with heavily calcined salts <note>A chemical process of heating a substance to high temperatures to remove volatile components or cause oxidation</note>, and so that nothing remains unburdened, they must press dew, hail, snow, frost, March rain-water, and sun-rays into service to yield the Spirit of the World <note>original: "Spiritum mundi"; in alchemy, this was believed to be a universal life-force or substance permeating the atmosphere</note>. They may resist as much as they like, but it does no good; the artist makes oil, salt, water, and earth out of these things—separating, composing, distilling, calcining, and digesting them—and when he finally stops, he is just as clever as he was before, and must laugh at his own "wisdom."

§. 32. It is fortunate for the sun that the gentlemen astronomers have revealed its immense distance; for I believe there would still be fools who would have ventured into it, especially if they had heard that the sun is nothing but pure flowing gold, as a certain physicist once claimed. These are the greater follies <note>original: "Ineptiæ majores"</note>; I could also report on many lesser trifles <note>original: "Nugis minoribus"</note>, where people wander about, wanting to pull profit—sometimes Gold <term>☉</term> and Silver <term>☽</term>—out of pebbles, or trying to make poor ores rich, or attempting to ripen the "unripe" without fire or any mercy; extracting the "fixed grain" <note>original: "Granum fixum"; a term for the stable, non-volatile essence of a metal</note> most expeditiously <note>original: "compendiosissime"</note> and promising great profit thereby. But enough of this <note>original: "Sed manum de Tabula"; literally "hand off the tablet," a phrase meaning to stop work or cease speaking</note>. A word to the wise is sufficient <note>original: "Sapienti sat"</note>.

§. 33. Now there are 3 questions left to discuss. (1.) Whether one can advise anyone to actually get involved with the Hermetic Art <term>Arte Hermetica</term> <note>Another name for alchemy, attributed to the mythical figure Hermes Trismegistus</note>? (2.) What qualities must a person have if they wish to become a successful disciple of this art? (3.) How should one recognize someone who claims to know the art, or who wants to teach it to us, to see if he is a true possessor of the art?

§. 34. To the first question, I answer roundly <note>original: "rotundé"</note> with No. For although we are certainly assured that the true beginnings of the Philosopher's Stone <term>L. P.</term> <note>original: "Lapis Philosophorum"</note> lie in Mercury <term>☿</term> and Gold <term>☉</term>, there are still very many locks to be opened. At the very least, the philosophers assure us that the true preparation of Mercury <term>☿</term> has been touched upon by no one specifically <note>original: "in specie"</note> or openly; indeed, they assure us that this preparation, under penalty of the cruelest curse, must not be disclosed in any writings. If someone were to come to this knowledge, it must happen either through direct divine inspiration <note>original: "immediatam inspirationem divinam"</note>, or by means of oral revelation and manual demonstration <note>original: "mediante orali revelatione & manuali demonstratione"</note> from an Adept under the seal of the most secret silence <note>original: "sub Sigillo secretissimi silentii"</note>. And even if one has this Philosophical Mercury <term>☿</term>, so many difficulties remain in the subsequent work regarding the external furnace, the vessel, the composition, and the fixed and volatile weight <note>original: "ratione furni externi, Vasis, Compositionis, ponderis fixi & volatilis"</note> of the Gold <term>☉</term> that most fall into despair. Only very rarely can one or another err in patience 200 times like Pontanus <note>Johannes Pontanus, an alchemist who famously claimed to have erred hundreds of times before finding the "Philosophical Fire"</note>; and very few live long enough to reach it in extreme old age like the Count of Trevisano <note>Bernard Trevisan (1406–1490), a famous alchemist who reportedly spent his entire life and fortune seeking the Stone, only finding success at age 82</note>.

§. 35. But if anyone, despite all this, had so much self-confidence that he wished to find the treasure through clever investigation and untiring industry: let him consider, as an answer to the 2nd question, what **AURELIUS AUGURELLUS** <note>Giovanni Aurelio Augurello (c. 1441–1524), an Italian humanist and poet who wrote "Chrysopoeia," a poem on making gold</note> says there:
