# Appendix.

Come now! You mortals! Follow this bright light,
That seems to have broken forth from the darkness;
Do not tread henceforth upon those crooked paths,
On which the rabble wanders, firmly and surely believing
To know the whole secret of this art,
Upon which many thousands have already labored in vain.

->❦ ❦ ❦ ❦ ❦ ❦<-

He who is greedy or lazy, and a deceiver,
A citizen, craftsman, or a merchant who has to do
With wares; he who otherwise squanders his goods and property,
A poor peasant who must often drive to the field,
Likewise he who wishes to capture the Stone <note>The Philosopher's Stone, the legendary substance capable of turning base metals into gold</note> out of avarice—
All of these will achieve nothing in this art.

->❦ ❦ ❦ ❦ ❦ ❦<-

On the other hand, he who yields himself entirely to the discipline of Wisdom,
Honoring nothing in the world higher than his Creator,
Loving Him more than gold, yes, even more than heaven itself,
And turning to Him completely with heart, mind, and soul—
He can trustfully venture into this work;
Wisdom, whom he serves, will deny him no good fortune.

With which that which the incomparable author of the *Secrets of Hermetic Philosophy* <note>original: "Arcani Hermeticæ Philosophiæ"</note> says in sections 2, 4, and 5 agrees, and is well worth reading. Finally, **GEBER** <note>Latinized name of Jabir ibn Hayyan, a 13th-century corpus of alchemical writings was attributed to him</note> speaks: one can indeed reach the completion of the Mastery <note>original: "Magisterii"; the completion of the alchemical Great Work</note> with little expense, if only one possesses the principles of the art; however, the poor are unsuited for the task, as they are too easily forced to stop <note>Because they lack the capital to sustain long experiments</note>.

§. 36. Should someone finally present himself as a possessor of the art, then ask him: Whether he can prepare the whole Mastery from <term>♁</term> <note>The symbol for Antimony</note> alone, or if he uses gold, whether he requires more than a *Quintlein* <note>A small weight, roughly 4 grams</note> or at the very most a *Loth* <note>A weight roughly equal to 15-17 grams</note>? (2.) Whether he can, with one furnace in a sealed glass—without opening or moving it—perform calcination, putrefaction, sublimation, precipitation, solution, and coagulation? <note>These are the various stages of chemical transformation in the alchemical process</note> Whether the matter in the glass first becomes black or white? And what it means when they say: one must first make silver before one can make gold? If he can perform <note>original: "præstiren"</note> and explain all of this, then believe him; if not, he is a deceiver. But suppose someone has learned to recite this from books; then pay attention: if he asks for even a single penny's <note>original: "Hellers"</note> worth of payment, he is no Adept <note>A "Master" of alchemy who has successfully created the Stone</note>, but wishes either to practice at the risk of your own purse, or will certainly swindle you before you even notice.

->Let he who is wise take warning.<-

### 1. What is alchemy?

It is an art that Alchimus <note>A legendary figure often cited in early modern texts as the inventor and namesake of alchemy, though modern etymology traces the word to the Arabic "al-kīmiyā."</note> invented, and which received its name from the Greek word *Archimo* <note>original: "Archimo"; likely a corruption of the Greek "chymeia," meaning to pour or smelt</note>, which in Latin is called *massa* <note>original: "massa"; meaning a lump of raw material or dough</note>.

### 2. What kind of art is it, and what does it teach?

This art teaches how to separate the essence of things from the waste products <note>original: "Excrementen"; referring to the "dross" or impurities that hide the pure essence</note>, and through it, metals are brought to perfection, whereas they were previously corrupted and imperfect in the mines. Therefore, it is to be noted that metals are distinguished from one another only by their accidental form, and not by their essential form <note>This follows Aristotelian logic: the "essence" of all metals is the same, while "accidents" like color or melting point are temporary qualities that can be changed</note>; for which reason it is also possible to separate all accidental things which have nothing of the metallic essence. For at whatever time, at whatever place, and with whatever heat all imperfect metals are deprived of the corrupting <term>Sulfur</term> <note>original: "As"; the author uses the stylized symbol of a triangle over a cross, indicating the "corrupting" or "combustible" principle that prevents base metals from being gold</note>, they are immediately made into gold. Thus, true alchemy is an art [that teaches] the principles <note>original: "Principia"</note>, causes, properties, and suf-

<summary>This page introduces a formal series of alchemical questions and answers, defining alchemy as the art of purifying metals by stripping away their "accidental" impurities to reveal their shared "essential" form as gold.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the "Alchemical Questions" from the previous page, finishing the answer to Question 2 regarding the fundamental nature of metals before moving into the specific mechanics of the "Great Work"—the creation of the Philosopher's Stone through fire, digestion, and the refinement of Mercury.</meta>

<header>Appendix.</header>

...properties of all metals from their foundation, through which art the imperfect, mixed, and corrupted are transformed into true gold <note>symbol: $\odot$</note>.

### 3. How are the metals brought to perfection through this art?

To achieve this, one must above all things procure such an *agent* <note>An active substance or "acting being."</note> or acting essence, in which is found both the separating and the fixing power <note>The "fixing" power refers to the ability to make a substance stable and resistant to the heat of fire.</note>, so that when it is applied to imperfect metals, it has the strength to keep them in the fire <note>symbol: $\Delta$</note> until all accidental things <note>In Aristotelian terms, "accidents" are non-essential qualities like color or impurities that can be stripped away.</note> are partly separated and partly consumed by the strength of the internal (not external) fire <note>symbol: $\Delta$</note>—since it does not allow itself to be easily separated by external fire—and finally nothing remains but the essence of gold <note>symbol: $\odot$</note> or silver <note>symbol: $\text{\☾}$</note>.

### 4. What else is understood by this acting thing?

->The Philosopher’s Stone.<-

### 5. What is the Philosopher’s Stone?

A universal tincture <note>A substance capable of "staining" or transforming the very nature of base metals.</note>, or artificial gold <note>symbol: $\odot$</note>, which is produced through the imitation of nature from the Mercury <note>symbol: $\text{\☿}$</note> of the Sages, made "super-perfect," and boiled and digested to the highest degree.

### 6. What kind of boiling or digestion is this?

By this is understood only a slow decoction <note>The process of heating or boiling a substance in a liquid to extract its essence.</note>, by means of which the Mercury <note>symbol: $\text{\☿}$</note> of the Sages is first resolved into an elixir or reddish juice (meaning drinkable gold <note>original: "$\odot$ potabile"; a legendary medicinal liquid sought by alchemists</note>), and thereafter coagulated into a powder through the degrees of fire <note>symbol: $\Delta$</note>; and indeed, after the black color has passed away, it turns first into white, then into yellowish, and finally into the red "blood-color," which last indicates the completion of the digestion.

### 7. What does this digestion accomplish?

When it is completed, the Mercury <note>symbol: $\text{\☿}$</note> of the Sages has been transformed into the Stone. If one dissolves and coagulates this anew, its tinting power <note>The ability of the Stone to transform a specific volume of base metal into gold.</note> will continually increase and be raised unto infinity.

### 1. What is alchemy?
It is an art invented by Alchimus <note>A legendary figure often cited in early modern texts as the founder of alchemy, though the name is likely a back-formation from the word "alchemy" itself.</note>, which received its name from the Greek word *Archimo* <note>original: "Archimo"; likely a reference to *chemeia* (pouring/infusing)</note>, which in Latin is called *masia* <note>original: "masia"; this may be a corruption of *magia* (magic) or *massa* (matter/substance).</note>.

### 2. What kind of art is it, and what does it teach?
This art teaches how to separate the essence of things from the dross <note>original: "Excrementen," referring here to impurities or waste matter.</note>, and through it, metals are brought to perfection, whereas they were previously corrupted and imperfect in the mines. Therefore, it should be noted that metals are distinguished from one another only by their accidental forms, but not by their essential forms <note>In the Aristotelian philosophy used by alchemists, the "essential form" is the core nature of a thing (which all metals share), while "accidental forms" are surface qualities like color or hardness that can be changed.</note>. For this reason, it is also possible to separate all accidental things which possess nothing of the metallic essence. For at whatever time, in whatever place, and with whatever heat all imperfect metals are deprived of the corrupting <term>fire (symbol: $\triangle$)</term>, by those means they are immediately turned into gold. Thus, true alchemy is an art [that teaches] the principles, causes, properties, and conditions <note>original: "Leiden," likely referring to the "affections" or ways a substance is acted upon.</note>

-> ### 3. How are metals brought to perfection through this art? <-

To achieve this, one must first and foremost prepare such an **agent** or active being in which both the separating and the **fixing** <note>In alchemy, "fixing" or "fixation" refers to the process of making a volatile, spiritual substance stable so it can withstand the heat of fire without evaporating.</note> power are found simultaneously. Thus, when it is applied to imperfect metals, it has the power to maintain them in the <term>fire</term> <note>original symbol: Δ</note> until all accidental things are partly separated and partly consumed through the strength of the **internal** (not external) <term>fire</term> <note>original symbol: Δ; Alchemists often distinguished between the "vulgar" fire of a furnace and the "secret" or "philosophical" fire inherent within the matter itself.</note>—seeing as they cannot be so easily separated by external means—until finally nothing remains but the essence of <term>gold</term> <note>original symbol: ☉</note> or <term>silver</term> <note>original symbol: ☾</note>.

-> ### 4. What else is understood by this active thing? <-

**The Philosopher’s Stone.**

-> ### 5. What is the Philosopher’s Stone? <-

A universal tincture, or artificial <term>gold</term> <note>original symbol: ☉</note>, which is generated through the imitation of nature from the <term>mercury</term> <note>original symbol: ☿</note> of the wise, made over-perfect, and cooked and **digested** <note>Digestion refers to the application of gentle, steady heat over a long period, similar to how a biological stomach processes food.</note> to the highest degree.

-> ### 6. What kind of cooking or digestion is that? <-

By this is meant only a slow **decoction** <note>The process of boiling down or concentrating a substance.</note>, by means of which the <term>mercury</term> <note>original symbol: ☿</note> of the wise is first **resolved** <note>dissolved or reduced to its liquid state</note> into an elixir or reddish juice (understood as <term>potable gold</term> <note>original: "Gold potabile"; a legendary alchemical medicine consisting of gold dissolved in a liquid, believed to grant longevity.</note>), and thereafter coagulated into a powder through the degree of heat. Specifically, after the black color has passed, it turns first to white, then to yellowish, and finally into the red blood-color, which last stage indicates the completed digestion.

-> ### 7. What does this digestion effect? <-

When it is completed, the <term>mercury</term> <note>original symbol: ☿</note> of the wise has been transformed into the **Stone**. If one dissolves and coagulates this again, its tinting power will continue to increase and be heightened unto infinity.

### 8. Does the Stone, besides its power of transformation, possess other powers?

According to the testimony of the Sages, among other remarkable things, it also makes glass malleable, so that it may be hammered <note>The legend of *vitrum flexile* (flexible glass) was a common trope in alchemy, suggesting that the Stone could change the very nature of brittle materials.</note>.

### 9. Is it not also a universal medicine, which demonstrates its effect in all diseases, even those deemed incurable?

Because it is not only the most powerful and indestructible substance, but also encompasses all the powers of the firmament, it is certainly the greatest, most universal, and most noble medicine under the **lunar globe** <note>original: "lunarischen Globo"; this refers to the "sublunary" world, or the earthly realm below the orbit of the moon where things are subject to decay.</note>, which heals all incurable diseases.

### 10. Why was it stated above only that the Stone must be made purely from <term>mercury</term> <note>original symbol: ☿</note>, and no mention was made of a ferment?

One must know that **fermentation** <note>In alchemy, fermentation is the final stage where a "leaven"—often gold or silver—is added to the Stone to "fix" it and give it the specific quality of the metal one wishes to produce.</note> is not found to be essential within the <term>mercury</term> <note>original symbol: ☿</note> of the Sages, but only occurs by chance. This is not only because it already contains within itself everything necessary for the Art, but also because the operation using pure <term>mercury</term> <note>original symbol: ☿</note> is, among all others, the most perfect and the shortest. Therefore, it was sufficient in that place to mention only the most noble operation, which is the most perfect and depends on no other.

### 11. How many ways are there by which it acts, and in which action is the fermentation found?

The Sages, in order to successfully complete their operations, have found two ways: one which they call the **dry** way, and the other which they call the **wet** way. By the **wet** way, they mean nothing other than that the operation is to be conducted solely with the <term>mercury</term> <note>original symbol: ☿</note> of the Sages, without the addition of any other thing or ferment. In the **dry** way, however, they have deemed a ferment necessary to make the work shorter, because the dry way (in which the <term>philosophical mercury</term> <note>original symbol: ☿ phil.</note> is not prepared as quickly as in the wet way) would otherwise require far too long a time.

### 12. What is the ferment?

The ferment of the <term>philosophical mercury</term> <note>original symbol: ☿ phil.</note> in the dry way is of two kinds. The first and simplest is <term>gold</term> <note>original symbol: ☉</note>, which has been purified by <term>copper</term> <note>original symbol: ♀ (Venus)</note> and reduced to the most subtle **calx** <note>A "calx" is a fine powder produced by heating a metal to the point of oxidation; it was considered the "ash" or "body" of the metal.</note>. The other, far more noble because it has a much greater power for the **projection** <note>Projection is the final step of the Great Work, where a small amount of the Stone is cast upon a molten base metal to transform it into gold.</note> of the Stone, is any fixed and **fiery fire** <note>original symbol: △ischer △; "fiery fire" refers to the concentrated essential heat or "sulfur" of the metal.</note> that is extracted from common <term>gold</term> <note>original symbol: ☉</note> itself or from other metals; although some wish to deny that such a fixed <term>fire</term> <note>original symbol: △</note> exists within metals.

### 13. What is the nature of this golden <term>sulfur</term> <note>original symbol: 🜍</note>, which is found in other metals besides common <term>gold</term> <note>original symbol: ☉</note>? And what are those metals?

Here one must first establish, based on Geber <note>Referring to the 8th-century alchemist Jabir ibn Hayyan, whose Latinized works were foundational to European alchemy.</note>, that metallic bodies consist of two <term>sulfurs</term>: one accidental and fixed, and another that lies locked within the <term>mercury</term>. The first, which is the only one under discussion here, is found—following its sufficient <term>solar</term> <note>original: "☉arischen"; meaning perfected to the state of gold.</note> elevation—only in certain metals: namely, besides common <term>gold</term> <note>original symbol: ☉</note>, in <term>iron</term> <note>original symbol: ♂; Mars</note> and <term>copper</term> <note>original symbol: ♀; Venus</note>. Thus, from each of these, this golden <term>sulfur</term> <note>original symbol: 🜍</note> can be drawn and, when it is united with the <term>Mercury</term> <note>original symbol: ☿</note> of the Sages, can be made into the Philosopher's Stone. Furthermore, the fixed sulfurs of other metals are not to be used at all as a <term>ferment</term> <note>A "leaven" or catalyst added to the work to direct the transmutation toward a specific metal.</note> for the Mercury of the Sages, because they have not reached the same solar degree of elevation.

### 14. What is the <term>Mercury</term> <note>original symbol: ☿</note> of the Sages?

This is that same important question, upon whose thorough explanation the entire truth of this science depends. For in the various interpretations of this name, so many and so great contradictions occur that anyone, at first glance, is forced to doubt this true Art. However, when the matter is considered a little more closely, one soon finds that all such various meanings, expressed with different words, aim only at a single thing. Therefore, for the sake of better understanding, the <term>Mercury</term> <note>original symbol: ☿</note> of the Sages can and must be considered in this threefold sense:

Firstly, as it is the **remote matter**; (2.) as it is the **nearer matter**; and (3.) as it is the **next matter** <note>Also called "proximate matter."</note> of the Stone.

As the **remote matter**, it is nothing other than the mere celestial impression sent to us indirectly from the stars into the air, poured out everywhere through the same, but finally received by the earth, where it is made physically tangible and visible.

When these effects of nature are accomplished, the matter has indeed already taken on a physical form; but it is still imperfect, and has progressed from the "remote" to the **nearer matter**.

If this is now further brought through various operations and alterations to such a perfect form and nature that it requires no further preparation, but can immediately be placed into the **philosophical egg** <note>The *ovum philosophicum*, a hermetically sealed glass vessel used for the final stages of the Great Work.</note>, then it is called the **next matter**.

But because the discussion concerns the innermost dissolution of <term>gold</term> <note>original symbol: ☉</note> or the fixed <term>sulfur</term> <note>original symbol: 🜍</note> that one wishes to use as a ferment—specifically by the **dry path** and not the **wet path**—the <term>Mercury</term> <note>original symbol: ☿</note> of the Sages must also...

...which is taken as the primary matter, is obtained in one path under a different form than in the other.

### 15. Under what form is the Philosophical Mercury obtained in the Dry Path?

Necessarily in the form of a living, running, and non-wetting <term>mercury</term> <note>original symbol: ☿ii</note>; however, it is brought to this form from the matter not by nature, but through <term>art</term> <note>The alchemist's skill in manipulating natural processes.</note>.

### 16. But why in the form of a running and non-wetting mercury?

Because in it alone common <term>gold</term> <note>original symbol: ☉</note>, along with all fixed and golden <term>sulfurs</term> <note>original symbol: 🜍eln; the active, "combustible" principle within metals</note>, are thoroughly and inseparably dissolved, like ice in <term>water</term> <note>original symbol: 🜄</note>, which no other <term>menstruum</term> <note>a solvent</note> can do. For the dissolver and the dissolved must be of exactly the same nature, like ice and water, and the only difference consists in this: just as ice, compared to dissolved water, is a frozen or congealed <term>water</term> <note>original symbol: 🜄</note>; so it is with the <term>Mercury</term> <note>original symbol: ☿</note> of the Sages in relation to <term>gold</term> <note>original symbol: ☉</note> and the fixed <term>sulfur</term> <note>original symbol: 🜍</note>, which are and can be nothing other than a congealed and decocted, dissolved and, to a certain extent, raw mercury. Just as we see that ice immediately dissolves into water and into another liquid because it was formed directly from it; so too can <term>gold</term> <note>original symbol: ☉</note> and the fixed solar <term>sulfur</term> <note>original symbol: 🜍</note> be immediately dissolved by and into that which they were before, and from which they were directly formed. <term>Philaletha</term> <note>Eirenaeus Philalethes, a famous 17th-century alchemist, likely being quoted from his work "Open Entrance to the Closed Palace of the King."</note> says:

> *From <term>mercury</term> <note>original symbol: ☿</note>, before it became mercury, something else could have been formed other than a metal or mineral; but after it has become mercury, or a running <term>water</term> <note>original symbol: 🜄</note> that does not wet the hands, it is now destined to take on a metallic or mineral form.*

From this it is evident that <term>mercury</term> <note>original symbol: ☿</note> (because it is in fact a running and non-wetting <term>water</term> <note>original symbol: 🜄</note>) is the primary matter of all metals; and consequently, all metals must be directly <term>resolved</term> <note>broken down into their constituent parts</note> through and into it alone, because nature makes no leaps in its workings, and therefore Art must also make none when it follows nature.

### 17. What is the Mercury of the Sages as the primary matter in the Wet Path?

A double saline substance of <term>water</term> <note>original symbol: 🜄</note>, and the Mercury of the Sages, which was made in the Dry Path from the other matter, namely through various preparations and changes that will be described further below.

### 18. Is common <term>mercury</term> <note>original symbol: ☿</note> likely to be the Mercury of the Sages in the dry path, since it is a running and non-wetting <term>water</term> <note>original symbol: 🜄</note>?

Because it has already been brought by nature into the form of a quicksilver, and is found—partly due to an excess and partly due to a deficiency—not to be of the same nature as <term>gold</term> <note>original symbol: ☉</note>, it is rightly rejected by all the Sages.

### 19. Is it then the <term>mercury</term> <note>original symbol: ☿</note> of the bodies?

Although the mercury of the bodies <note>Mercury extracted from solid metals like gold or silver.</note> does not have as much of the aforementioned superfluous essence as common mercury, and is not contrary to the nature of <term>gold</term> <note>original symbol: ☉</note>, its <term>sulfur</term> <note>original symbol: 🜍</note> has meanwhile been altered in its nature. Because it has thereby lost its raw form and penetrating power, it is also given no regard in the Work, just like common mercury.

### 20. What is understood by the "crudity" or raw form of the <term>sulfur</term> <note>original symbol: 🜍</note>?

A non-fixed sulfur that remains in the depths of the <term>mercury</term> <note>original symbol: ☿</note> and is called <term>Arsenicum</term> <note>Arsenic; in alchemy, this often refers to a volatile, soul-like principle rather than the modern chemical element.</note> by <term>Geber</term> <note>original: "Gebro"; referring to the famous 8th-century Arabic alchemist Jabir ibn Hayyan.</note>. In this (non-fixed sulfur), the sole foundation of the [alchemical] operation entirely rests. For if it were fixed, there would be no action in our Work, because it is the true innermost (<term>radical</term> <note>Latin: "radicalis", meaning "at the root".</note>) heat, or, as <term>Philalethes</term> <note>Eirenaeus Philalethes, a famous 17th-century alchemical author.</note> says, the sulfurous power for burning.

-> 21. The <term>mercury</term> <note>original symbol: ☿</note> of the bodies, especially the metallic ones, is attached to common <term>gold</term> <note>original symbol: ☉</note> <-
-> and <term>silver</term> <note>original symbol: ☽</note>, and can thus be inseparably fixed with them, <-
-> which is one of the properties of the Mercury of the Sages. <-
-> Therefore, etc. <-

Although the mercury of the metals is fixed with <term>gold</term> <note>original symbol: ☉</note> and <term>silver</term> <note>original symbol: ☾</note>, one gains nothing more through this than an increase in the weight of the gold and silver; such properties, however, are not sufficient to recognize the Philosophical Mercury. For the latter first dissolves the aforementioned metals thoroughly before it is transformed with them—through a more secret <term>fixation</term> <note>The process of making a volatile substance stable under heat.</note>—not into common gold and silver as before, but into the <term>Philosopher's Stone</term>.

### 22. Philosophical Mercury is called "Mercury of the Metals" by the Sages; will it then be the mercury of the bodies?

One must know that these words, "Bodies" and "Metals," are distinguished by the Sages such that Philosophical Mercury may indeed be called the Mercury of Metals, but it cannot be confused with the "corporeal" [mercury]. This must be understood in terms of its metallic origin: for since Philosophical Mercury is not found at all in the form of a quicksilver (to which nature has brought the common mercury of metals), it is sought in such a form in vain.

### 23. If the <term>Philosophical Mercury</term> <note>original: "☿ Phil."</note> does not exist in nature, where then should one seek it?

Although it does not exist in nature in the form of a quicksilver, it is nonetheless present in another form, and through the <term>Art</term> <note>The practice of alchemy.</note> it can finally be transformed into a true mercury—that is, into a running, non-wetting <term>water</term> <note>original symbol: ▽</note>—which possesses such virtues that common mercury can never attain through nature alone.

### 24. How, then, should the Art, by imitating Nature, be able to produce a mercury that is better than the common one from a matter that is a pure vapor?

For a better understanding of this question, it was shown above that the <term>Mercury of the Sages</term> <note>original: "☿ der Weisen"</note> is to be considered in three ways: first, as the <term>most remote matter</term> <note>original: "Materia remotissima"</note>; further, as the <term>remote matter</term> <note>original: "remota"</note>; and finally, as the <term>proximate matter</term> <note>original: "proxima"</note>. When one has previously grasped and considered this well, it must be known that such an imitation of Nature by the Art is by no means to be understood as if it could happen in that same <term>most remote matter</term> or the mere vapor that is still in the <term>water</term> <note>original symbol: ▽</note>, much less that it should be started therein. Rather, all these preceding works, which prepare the way, as it were, in the most distant matter, belong to and are possible for Nature alone; consequently, they are to be left to her alone. 

Therefore, when the Sages advised the artist to imitate Nature, they did not mean this regarding the most remote matter (*remotissima*), but rather the <term>remote matter</term> (*remota*), as it has already been brought into a corporeal being but left imperfect. For then, and not before, it is placed by Nature into the desired state in which it is also handed over to the Art, in order to complete it upon the <term>water</term> <note>original symbol: ▽</note> into a true <term>mercury</term> <note>original symbol: ☿</note> that is better than everything natural. And because the operations of Nature are not sufficient to produce mercury—much less the <term>Philosophers' Stone</term>—from the <term>remote matter</term> in the earth, whether by the dry or wet path, but only produce a common mercury and the common metals; thus one can truly say that the Art may not only help Nature, but may also complete and surpass her.

### 25. Under what form is the <term>remote matter</term> <note>original: "Materia remota"</note> handed over by Nature directly to the Art for its completion? And what else is it called by the Sages?

When the remote matter first comes into the artist's hand, it is a white corporeal substance that allows itself to be dissolved in water and becomes crystals, like any other <term>salt</term> <note>original symbol: ⊖</note> or alum; and it has the following two special properties:

### 26. It was said above that all metals are brought forth by Nature from the <term>remote matter</term> <note>original: "Materia remota"; the substance in its early, undeveloped state.</note>, which is a <term>salt</term> <note>original symbol: ⊖</note>: but <term>Hermes</term> <note>Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary founder of alchemy.</note> says that Heaven is the father of metals and the <term>water</term> <note>original symbol: ▽</note> their mother; likewise, that the wind carried them in its belly; how then can this be applied to the <term>salt</term>?

The **Central Salt** of the metals is indeed the true and right seed, from which—according to nature—not only <term>quicksilver</term> <note>Common mercury.</note> is produced in the bowels of the <term>water</term> <note>original symbol: ▽</note> itself, and from this, all metals and minerals; but also, above the <term>water</term>, the <term>Mercury</term> <note>original symbol: ☿</note> of the Sages and the <term>Stone</term> <note>The Philosopher's Stone.</note> have their origin. Because this <term>salt</term> in its first origin was begotten by the stars, then carried into the air or the "belly" [of the wind], and finally received by the <term>water</term>, made bodily within it, and transformed into perfect metals; therefore Hermes said: Heaven was the father of the metals and the earth their mother, and the wind carried them in its belly.

### 27. <term>Sulphur</term> <note>original symbol: △</note> and <term>Mercury</term> <note>original symbol: ☿</note> are, according to <term>Geber</term> <note>original: "Gebro"; Jabir ibn Hayyan, a famous 8th-century alchemist.</note>, the matter of all minerals and metals; therefore, can it not be the aforementioned <term>salt</term>?

<term>Bacon</term> <note>original: "Baco"; likely Roger Bacon, the 13th-century philosopher and alchemist.</note> solves the question best and most beautifully when he says: a certain thing is found in nature which, through the union and proportioned mixture of a pure living <term>mercury</term> with a similar <term>sulphur</term>, is congealed into a solid mass; which is more clearly revealed by others and is nothing other than the mentioned <term>salt</term>; for in the metallic <term>salt</term>, the <term>sulphur</term> and <term>mercury</term> are found. The **Little Peasant** <note>original: "Der Kleine Bauer"; a pseudonym for the alchemist Johann Grasshoff.</note> says: although it is often written in the Sages' scripts that all metals were created from <term>sulphur</term> and <term>mercury</term>, one should never understand this as a <term>mercury</term> or <term>sulphur</term> *outside* of the seed of the metals; for the principles of the metals are in the seed, which is their perfect and uncorrupted <term>salt</term>; and when they have brought the same into a double <term>dual substance</term> <note>original: "Gial-Substanz". In this context, it likely refers to a binary or "yellowed" (from Italian *giallo*) state of the matter being prepared.</note>, they call one part of this doubled being <term>sulphur</term>, and the other <term>mercury</term>; yet they understand nothing else by it than the <term>salt</term>, which has been brought into such a double substance.

### 28. The Sages say that all metals which flow in any fire are from the Earth and the Water; consequently not from <term>sulphur</term> and <term>mercury</term>?

The Sages also understand the aforementioned <term>salt</term> by the earth and the <term>water</term> <note>original symbol: ▽</note>. When

When they now say that the metallic <term>Salt</term> <note>original symbol: 🜔</note> is their **Vitriol**, they mean a substance that is composed of <term>Sulphur</term> <note>original symbol: 🜍; the principle of combustion and soul.</note> and <term>Water</term> <note>original symbol: 🜄; the principle of fluidity.</note> which have been digested and cooked together. In this cooking process, the subtle earthly essence becomes oily and turns into a <term>Sulphur</term> <note>original symbol: 🜍</note>; the watery part, however, becomes "gluey" or viscous when combined with the subtle <term>Salt</term> <note>original symbol: 🜔</note>, becoming a primary source of **Quicksilver**. In this manner, Nature continues to produce all metals within the earth: she works with a constant alteration, using only the heat found within the mineral mountains. By means of this heat, these substances are finally united. From these united substances—depending on whether they are pure or impure—either "perfect" metals <note>such as Gold or Silver</note> or "imperfect" metals <note>such as Lead or Iron</note> are generated.

### 29. Modern philosophers say that there are three beginnings (principles) of metals; but can these not be the <term>Salt</term> <note>original symbol: 🜔</note> and the "doubled essence"?

One must certainly recognize that when the **Three Principles of Nature** <note>Sulphur, Mercury, and Salt, famously popularized by Paracelsus.</note> are mentioned, they are likewise contained within the Salt and originate from the Salt. This "doubled essence" <note>the combination of Sulphur and Mercury</note> cannot be obtained from the Salt unless the Salt is first dissolved into the three original parts from which it was immediately formed.

### 30. How can one prove concisely from true authors that the aforementioned <term>Salt</term> <note>original symbol: 🜔</note> is the true and sole matter of both the <term>Mercury</term> <note>original symbol: ☿</note> of the Philosophers and the Stone?

To cite only a few of the most famous authors: first, **Hermes** says: "The metallic Salt is the **Philosopher's Stone**." Here, the word "Stone" is used to refer to the <term>remote matter</term> <note>original: "materiam remotam"; the raw, unrefined starting material.</note>, which is the <term>Salt</term> <note>original symbol: 🜔</note>. **Raymond Lull** and **Arnold** <note>Arnold of Villanova, a 13th-century physician and alchemist.</note> also call it by the name "the Stone." They say to dissolve it into its elements or principles, and claim that when these are purified of all their impurities and reunited into one essence, the "dead body" becomes living again—clear, white, and shining like **Mercury**. Thus, these two authors intend to create both the <term>Mercury</term> <note>original symbol: ☿</note> and the Philosopher's Stone from the simple <term>Salt</term> <note>original symbol: 🜔</note>.

**Geber** <note>The Latinized name of Jabir ibn Hayyan, the father of chemistry.</note> says: "The natural principles of metals are <term>Sulphur</term> <note>original symbol: 🜍</note> and <term>Mercury</term> <note>original symbol: ☿</note>." However, it was proven above that these are nothing other than a <term>Salt</term> <note>original symbol: 🜔</note> that has been brought into a doubled essence. **B. Filius** <note>Likely "Boni Filius" or "The Son of the Good," a pseudonymous alchemical author.</note> states: "Whoever cannot prepare the metallic <term>Salt</term> <note>original symbol: 🜔</note> cannot make the Mercury of the Wise." **Trevisan** <note>Bernard Trevisan, a 15th-century Italian alchemist.</note> claims: "One must turn the doubled saline essence—which, as **Basilius** <note>Basilius Valentinus, the legendary Benedictine monk and alchemist.</note> says elsewhere, is in the Salt—into Quicksilver." This is also evident from the text ***The Little Farmer*** <note>original: "der kleine Bauer"; an influential 17th-century alchemical work by Johann Grasshoff.</note>: (The white and red lilies, or the white woman and the red man—likewise <term>Sulphur</term> <note>original symbol: 🜍</note> and <term>Mercury</term> <note>original symbol: ☿</note>—in which the <term>Salt</term> <note>original symbol: 🜔</note> lies hidden). For as he himself confesses, this is found entirely within the metallic Salt. The following authors also agree with this: *The Assembly of the Philosophers* <note>original: "Turb. The <note>original: "Historicus Chimicus"</note> **Chemical Historian** says: From the salt becomes water, and from the water comes Mercury. **Arnoldus** says: Quicksilver comes from a non-burning <term>Fire</term> <note>original symbol: △; the alchemical principle of heat and soul</note>: and where he explains these words elsewhere, he writes: the <term>Salt</term> <note>original symbol: ⊖</note> of the metals is the "non-burning fire" of the Wise <note>literally "the White ones," referring to the alchemists who have reached the "white" stage of the work</note>. **Richardus Anglus** confirms this with the following: Quicksilver comes from a white, bright earth and clear water. This is again mentioned in various places. **Basil Valentine** is clear when he says: the aforementioned <term>Mercury</term> <note>original symbol: ☿</note> also has its spirit within itself, which is called a "clear water" by Richardus Anglus, Arnoldus, and Raymond Lully. But the "Earth of the Wise" is the metal <term>Gold</term> <note>original symbol: ☉</note>, which contains much <term>Fire</term> <note>original symbol: △</note> within it. **Anaxagoras** says our gold is red and of a fiery nature, mixed with the soul and nature of the <term>Moon</term> <note>original symbol: ☾; Silver</note> by means of the spirit, since the entire <note>original: "Compositum"</note> **compound** is nothing other than the Mercury of the Philosophers. **Morienus** states: Unless Sun and Moon are brought into one body, it is impossible to reach this art. These two pieces are explained by others thus: The <term>Salt</term> <note>original symbol: ⊖</note> of the metals is the Moon or the "Silver of the Wise," which holds within its depths the red and white vapor; the former is a non-fixed <term>Fire</term> <note>original symbol: △</note>, Arsenic, Gold, and Sun, while the other is called **Hermes’ Bird**, the **Eagle**, the **Dragon’s Tail**, clear water, spirit, and <term>Mercury</term> <note>original symbol: ☿</note>. These three parts together, as the whole compound, are again indicated under the names of the <term>Salt</term> <note>original symbol: ⊖</note>, <term>Fire</term> <note>original symbol: △</note>, and <term>Mercury</term> <note>original symbol: ☿</note> of the Wise.

¶ 1. **From which metals must one then extract this <term>Salt</term> <note>original symbol: ⊖</note>?**

Because no small difficulty arises in the choosing of minerals and metals, one should note the following essential requirements: First, it shall be extracted from such metals in which its essential parts—among which two are volatile—have not yet entered into a fixed coagulation. Secondly, it shall be sufficiently "cooked" <note>digested by natural heat</note> and able to withstand a separation, through which it is decomposed into its three original parts; this division or "dissection" only serves to sweep out the internal impurities. Thirdly, it shall be obtained without the loss of the spirits. By the first requirement, common gold is excluded, because in it alone all spirits have passed into the hardest and most fixed coagulation. By the second, according to Basil Valentine and others, it is restricted only to certain metals and one mineral, namely **iron, copper, and vitriol**. By the third, all minerals and metals that have been melted in fire are excluded.

32. **Can the Stone then not be made from melted metals?**

One must know that a metal which is still in its <note>original: "Minera"</note> **ore**, and is perfect and unspoiled according to its "seed-substance," is different from those that have passed through the <term>Fire</term> <note>original symbol: △</note>...

...[distinguished from common] metals, as in these the two parts of the seed-substance—Spirit and non-fixed <term>Fire</term> <note>original symbol: △</note>—have vanished, being weakened and destroyed to such an extent that the <term>Philosophers' Mercury</term> <note>original symbol: ☿ Phil.</note> and the Stone can no longer be made from them. And although these metals melted through <term>Fire</term> <note>original symbol: △</note> still contain their <term>Salt</term> <note>original symbol: ⊖</note>, <term>Fire</term> <note>original symbol: △</note>, and <term>Mercury</term> <note>original symbol: ☿</note>, these are not the *Principles* which the Sages seek. Rather, they are to a certain extent "bodies" generated by the metals themselves, which directly make up the mineral <term>Body</term> <note>original: "Corpus"</note> and the metal itself. 

For the Sages did not mean the whole metal, but only the intermediate substance, when they said: The *Principles* of the metals are in the seed, which is their perfect and uncorrupted <term>Salt</term> <note>original symbol: ⊖</note>, taken not from melted metals, but from their ores <note>original: "Minern"</note>. For this reason, it is called the "Full Moon" by **Arnoldus** <note>Arnold of Villanova, a 13th-century physician and alchemist</note>, and it is recovered without the loss of the <term>Spirits</term> <note>original: "Spirituum"</note>. This is one of the great secrets to achieving the true goal. From this it follows that in metals not yet diminished by the smelting-fire, a fixed <term>Fire</term> <note>original symbol: △</note>, a spiritual <term>Mercury</term> <note>original symbol: ☿</note>, and a non-fixed <term>Fire</term> <note>original symbol: △</note> may be found, which lie hidden in the bare <term>Salt</term> <note>original symbol: ⊖</note> and, together with it, constitute the complete seed. For these two spirits, in which alone the life of the metals is contained, flee from the metals during smelting and leave behind the dead body, which can no longer demonstrate its powers <term>universally</term> <note>original: "universaliter"</note> but only <term>specifically</term> <note>original: "particulariter"</note>.

33. How does one obtain this <term>Salt</term> <note>original symbol: ⊖</note> from the metals?

Only and alone through <term>extraction</term> <note>the process of drawing out a specific substance using a solvent</note> with vinegar (its dissolution is "in the barrel," as **Basil** and others testify), by a preceding <term>suitable calcination</term> <note>original: "conveniente Calcination"; heating a metal until it oxidizes into a powder</note>, through which the metal is turned into an ash that cannot be brought back: **Note:** For **Basilius** <note>Basil Valentine</note> says: he who has not the ash, has not the <term>Salt</term> <note>original symbol: ⊖</note>; and he who cannot make the metallic <term>Gold</term> <note>original symbol: ☉</note> also cannot make the <term>Philosophers' Mercury</term> <note>original symbol: ☿ Phil.</note>. **Similarly** others say: Thus the sharpness of the vinegar, acting within the <term>calcined</term> body, draws the <term>Salt</term>-substance to itself, and with it simultaneously the subtle <term>Fire</term> (called the <term>intrinsic sulfur</term> <note>original: "Sulphur intrinsecum"</note>) that lies hidden in the salt. In both of these—the <term>Salt</term> and the <term>Fire</term>—all the metals of the Wise are to be found.

34. What properties does this <term>Salt</term> <note>original symbol: ⊖</note> have, by which one can recognize the infallible truth?

When it is dissolved in <term>Water</term> <note>original symbol: ▽</note>, it is green; but when <term>coagulated</term> <note>solidified from a liquid state</note> it is white, crystalline, sweet, and flows easily on a metal plate like wax, and contains its life-giving spirit and soul within itself. Furthermore, in this <term>Salt</term>, as mentioned above, there is a lunar glow; therefore the Sages say that one should take such a <term>Salt</term> that leaves behind a "lunar essence" in the bodies. This is to be understood as follows: when this <term>Salt</term> is placed on a glowing copper plate, it

35. How does one then proceed further with this obtained <term>Salt</term> <note>original symbol: ⊖</note>, so that finally the <term>Philosophers' Mercury</term> <note>original symbol: ☿ Phil.</note> and the Stone may be made from it?

One must not only change it from its natural <term>Salt-form</term> <note>original symbol: ⊖-Form</note> into other shapes, but also dissolve it into its original parts. This is because one cannot reach one extreme from another except through a middle point; thus, one can only come from the <term>remote matter</term> <note>original: "Materia remota"</note>—that is, from the <term>Salt</term> <note>original symbol: ⊖</note>—to the <term>proximate matter</term> <note>original: "Materia proxima"</note>, or the double <term>Salt-Substance</term>, through a medium. This is achieved through various intervening <term>degrees</term> <note>original: "Gradus"</note> of <term>preparation</term> <note>original: "Præparation"</note> and <term>alteration</term> <note>original: "Alteration"</note>, each of which necessarily requires the one before it.

36. Which and how many are these degrees?

The Sages have diligently avoided treating these in their proper order, so that this great secret—which consists solely in the said order of preparation and transformation—should always remain hidden in their books. Here, however, these degrees are described in clear words.

The **1st Degree** of alteration is called by **Isaac Hollandus** <note>A 15th-century Dutch alchemist known for his works on mineral and vegetable stones</note> the "Reddening of the <term>Salt</term>" <note>original symbol: ⊖</note>, and he teaches it to be performed thus: One should place this <term>Salt</term> <note>original symbol: ⊖</note> in a hermetically sealed glass and apply such a gentle warmth beneath it that it cannot melt, until it first acquires a yellow color and finally a red color. This happens because the Green is then transformed into Redness, and henceforth remains constantly red and non-fixed; thus, the greatest essential requirement is fulfilled by this degree.

The **2nd, 3rd, and 4th Degrees** are sufficiently contained in **Basilius** <note>Basilius Valentinus, a legendary 15th-century alchemist</note> and the **Little Peasant** <note>original: "kleiner Bauer," referring to Johann Grasshoff’s "Der Kleine Baur," a popular 17th-century alchemical text</note>. Through the second degree, this reddened <term>Salt</term> <note>original symbol: ⊖</note> is distilled into an oil, which Basilius calls the <term>Spirit of Mercury</term> <note>original: "Spiritum ☿"</note>. It is made in such a way that from this reddened <term>Salt</term> <note>original symbol: ⊖</note>, its spirits—which are twofold, namely a dry and a moist vapor—are both extracted through <term>degrees of Fire</term> <note>original symbol: △-Grad</note> together in the form of an oil. One must repeatedly pour this oil back onto the matter remaining in the glass and distill it off again until it has entirely drawn its "body"—which is the fixed <term>Salt</term> <note>original symbol: ⊖</note>—into itself, and the entire substance of the red <term>Salt</term> <note>original symbol: ⊖</note> has been brought into the form of an oil through repeated distillation.

The **3rd Degree** of transformation consists solely in the <term>putrefaction</term> <note>original: "Fäulung"</note> of this oil through the heat of <term>digestion</term> <note>A process of slow, gentle heating in a sealed vessel</note>, by which the red color is cast down, and a white juice (the red <term>precipitated matter</term>) remains floating on top, which...

...first, a <term>Spirit</term> <note>A volatile substance released during heating</note> and <term>Mercury</term> <note>original symbol: ☿; here referring to the "philosophical" mercury, not common quicksilver</note> must be separated from the matter by distillation; the remaining matter, however, must be <term>calcined</term> <note>reduced to powder through heat</note> with a slow <term>Fire</term> <note>original symbol: $\triangle$</note>, and the aforementioned Spirit must be poured back over it, so that the <term>Subject</term> <note>original symbol: $\infty$; in this context, the "Magnesia" or the physical matter being worked upon</note> may draw out its own soul (which is otherwise also called <term>Salt</term> <note>original symbol: ⊖</note>, <term>Gold</term> <note>original symbol: $\odot$</note>, and <term>Arsenicum</term> <note>Not common arsenic, but a volatile "fiery" principle</note>), and draw the Spirit off from its soul again, until an oil remains that shines like a glowing coal; after that, calcine the remaining matter even longer until it becomes ash, in which the treasure of the wise lies hidden: namely, the <term>fixed Salt</term>, without which the Art cannot be completed. This must finally be extracted from its <term>Subject</term> <note>original symbol: $\infty$</note> by that very same Spirit in which it still lay wrapped after the calcination. This third degree is called the <term>Anatomy of Salt</term> <note>original: "Anatomia ⊖"; the analytical separation of the salt into its components</note>, and through it, the salt is purified of both external and internal <term>dregs</term> <note>original: "Fæcibus"; the impure waste matter</note>.

The 4th degree contains nothing else but that the aforementioned <term>Salt</term> <note>original symbol: ⊖</note>, which has been divided into its three natural <term>Principles</term> <note>Salt, Sulfur, and Mercury</note> through the <term>Anatomy</term>, is transformed into a double vial-substance; its Spirit, united with the <term>Salt</term> <note>original symbol: ⊖</note>, constitutes one part, and the Soul—the <term>Fire</term> <note>original symbol: $\triangle$</note> or <term>Arsenicum</term> (as <term>Geber</term> <note>Referring to Jabir ibn Hayyan, the legendary 8th-century father of alchemy</note> calls it)—makes up the other by itself. Here one should note in particular, as if in passing, what the <term>Small Peasant</term> <note>original: "kleine Bauer"; a pseudonym for the alchemist Johannes Grasshoff</note> reminds us regarding this part: namely, that this Spirit united with its <term>Salt</term> <note>original symbol: ⊖</note> is immediately transformed into a certain substance, and indeed in such a way that, if one takes a little more of the <term>Subject</term> <note>original symbol: $\infty$</note> than the proportion allows, the matter becomes thick, like butter; and if someone could have this matter over the <term>Water</term> <note>original symbol: 🜄</note> (from which all metals have come in the bowels of the earth), then the Art would not fail him.

The 5th degree of change can finally be learned from the clear words of <term>TREVISANI</term> <note>Bernard of Trevisan, a famous 15th-century alchemist who sought the Stone for 80 years</note>, where he says: every man must transform the double vial-substance into Mercury. Here the Mercury has, so to speak, attained its perfect nature. In the <term>dry path</term> <note>A method of alchemy using high heat and crucibles rather than liquid solvents</note>, however, it is not necessary that this double vial-substance be transformed into <term>Mercury</term> <note>original symbol: ☿</note>; rather, there the Spirit united with its body is directly <term>coagulated</term> <note>thickened or solidified</note> into the <term>Stone to the white</term> <note>original: "Stein ad album"; the stage of the work that transmutes metals into silver</note>, which the Sages confirm, saying: the work to the white is completed with three elements—<term>Fire</term> <note>original symbol: $\triangle$</note>, <term>Water</term> <note>original symbol: 🜄</note>, and <term>Earth</term> <note>original symbol: 🜃</note>—but the <term>Fire</term> <note>original symbol: $\triangle$</note> is omitted, which is thereafter <term>imbibed</term> <note>soaked or saturated</note> with its Soul and coagulated into the <term>Stone to the red</term> <note>original: "Stein ad rubrum"; the final stage for transmuting metals into gold</note>. This operation can happen in the <term>wet path</term> without the aforementioned <term>ferments</term> <note>substances added to "ripen" the work</note>, namely from this <term>Salt</term> <note>original symbol: ⊖</note> or <term>Mercury</term> <note>original symbol: ☿</note> alone; because it was already shown above that for the Sages, <term>Salt</term> <note>original symbol: ⊖</note>, the Stone, and the <term>Subject</term> <note>original symbol: $\infty$</note> are one and the same. In the dry path, however, according to the report of <term>TREVISANI</term> and others, one must make from the double vial-substance a mercury—or a flowing and non-wetting <term>Water</term> <note>original symbol: 🜄</note>—and ferment it with one of the above <term>ferments</term> and prepare it according to the Art. **37. By what various names is this Salt specifically called by the Sages, when it is taken according to one degree or another?**

To ensure that no further difficulty remains regarding the many names of the <term>Salt</term> <note>original symbol: 🜔</note>, as the <term>Remote Matter</term> <note>original: "Materiæ remotæ"; the raw, unprocessed starting material</note>, the following names—all of which presuppose a certain degree of progress—are listed in order. Firstly, those which concern the perfect and unaltered Remote Matter; in this state, it is called by the Sages: <term>Our Secondary Chaos</term> <note>original: "Secundævum Chaos nostrum"; a reference to the primordial state of the Work, paralleling the creation of the world</note>. For just as our elements or <term>Principles</term> <note>The tria prima: Salt, Sulphur, and Mercury</note> emerge from the mixed properties in our Secondary Chaos (in which the four elements are mixed and transformed into our water), so it is otherwise called the Stone, <term>Salt</term> <note>original symbol: 🜔</note>, <term>Mercury</term> <note>original symbol: ☿</note>, and the <term>Ore</term> <note>original: "Minera"</note> in which Nature has begun its work: <term>Ore of Silver</term> <note>original symbol: Minera ☽</note>, <term>Ore of Gold</term> <note>original symbol: Minera ☉</note>, the Ore of all metals, <term>Magnesia</term> <note>A term for the "mother" or "womb" of metals, not modern magnesium</note>, <term>Salt</term> <note>original symbol: 🜔</note>, green ore, the <term>Green Lion</term> <note>A metaphor for the raw mineral or a strong acid capable of dissolving gold</note>, <term>Celandine</term> <note>original: "Chelidonia"; a plant name used here to describe a specific stage or color</note>, <term>coagulated Mercury</term> <note>original symbol: ☿ coagulatus</note>, <term>dry and non-flowing Water</term> <note>original symbol: 🜄</note>, <term>Water</term> <note>original symbol: 🜄</note> coagulated by the dryness of <term>Fire</term> <note>original symbol: 🜂</note>, the full moon, <term>Urine-Salt</term> and <term>Saltpeter</term> <note>original: "Sal petræ"</note>, etc. However, that it is also called a <term>vegetable and animal Salt</term> occurs because of its green color, and because it consists of spirit, soul, and body. 

Following this are the names which concern the first and second <term>Degrees of Alteration</term>. In the first, because of its preparation and the redness it has attained, it is called the common prepared <term>Salt</term> <note>original symbol: 🜔</note>, <term>precipitated Mercury</term> <note>original symbol: ☿ præcipitatus</note>, the red penny, Mars, <term>Colcothar</term> <note>original: "Colchotar"; red iron oxide residue</note>, the red servant, and Cinnabar. In the second degree, because it is an oil or an oily and simultaneously red liquid, it is called a <term>Mercury</term> <note>original symbol: ☿</note> that wets the hands, <term>Spirit of Mercury</term> <note>original symbol: Spiritus ☿</note>, and according to <term>Basil</term> <note>Referring to the alchemist Basil Valentine</note>, the <term>liquid Gold</term> <note>original symbol: ☉</note>, or the <term>Lead of the Sages</term> because of its weight—since it is so difficult to drive upward through distillation that barely a drop passes over in an hour. Likewise, it is also called the <term>incombustible oil</term>, <term>water of life</term> and not of the vine <note>i.e., not ethanol/alcohol</note>, <term>Water</term> <note>original symbol: 🜄</note> of the metal, <term>Ses</term> <note>Possibly a contraction or variation of 'Aes', meaning copper or bronze</note>, the <term>blood of the red man</term>, and the <term>Mercury of Mercuries</term> <note>original: "☿ Mercuriorum"</note>. In this latter name, the title of Mercury is used incompletely through the word <term>pious</term> <note>original: "piorum"; likely a wordplay or a reference to those "holy" parts of the matter</note> and is taken particularly for each part, for the parts themselves, or the three <term>Principles of Nature</term>, to which this name <term>Mercury</term> <note>original symbol: ☿</note> is assigned to all together without distinction. From the third degree, the following names have come:

->namely, a white and a red one, in his hands etc.<-

The names belonging to the fourth degree are as follows: According to <term>Geber</term> <note>referring to Geber/Jabir ibn Hayyan, the foundational 8th-century alchemist</note>, <term>Arsenic</term> and <term>Quicksilver</term>; for the <term>Sun</term> <note>original symbol: ☉, representing Gold</note> is, as <term>Bracescus</term> <note>Giovanni Bracesco, a 16th-century alchemist</note> explains it, called <term>Living Silver</term> <note>original: "Argentum vivum"</note>, and the <term>Fire</term> <note>original symbol: △, representing Sulphur or the active principle</note> united with <term>Mercury</term> <note>original symbol: ☿</note> is called <term>Arsenic</term>; for he says one must separate the Arsenic from the <term>Vessel-Water</term> <note>original: "Phial-▽"</note>; but the Vessel-Water, and the <term>Mercury</term> <note>original symbol: ☿</note>, <term>Antimony</term> <note>original symbol: ♁</note> or <term>Water</term> <note>original symbol: ▽</note>, are called the same thing. In this degree, it is also designated by other names: such as the **double Vessel-substance**, the **doubled Mercury**, the **golden and silver nature**, **Man and Wife**, **Fire and Mercury**, the **white and red lily of the Little Peasant** <note>referring to Johannes de Monte-Snyder, an alchemist known as the "Little Peasant"</note>; because it is also explicitly stated in this that the <term>Antimony</term> <note>original symbol: ♁</note> united with the <term>Sun</term> <note>original symbol: ☉</note> is transformed into a white, sweetish matter, like milk, it is also called by the Sages the **Virgin’s Milk**: but because, as he further speaks, if more of its <term>Antimony</term> <note>original symbol: ♁</note> were added to this <term>Sun</term> <note>original symbol: ☉</note> than the proportion allows, the mass would become thick, like butter, so it is also called the **gluey matter**, **Butter of Antimony** <note>original: "butyrum Antimonii"</note> and **Mountain of Swabia** <note>original: "Mons Sueviæ"</note>: Likewise, the other Vessel-substance, because it shines like a glowing coal, has even more names, namely **Carbuncle**, **Sun**, **Light of the World**, **Splendor of the Sun** etc.

In the fifth and last degree, through which this double substance is brought into the previous perfect, simple, and fully changed state, it has received only the true name of a **Mercury**, since it is at last indeed a running, and non-wetting water, prepared from one, two, and three parts; from which it is clearly to be concluded that, although the <term>Mercury of the Sages</term> is at one time called a water that wets the hands, and at another time, a water that does not wet the hands; again, at one time the dry, and at another time, the oily; now the simple, double, and triple; now the red, the white, now the green etc. matter, one should not imagine anything different, but rather a **single Subject** or **Matter**, which is given to us directly by Nature for further elaboration; for the same is transformed in its preparation now into two, now into three, now back into one substance; and can moreover be changed, both inside and outside the <term>Egg</term> <note>The "Philosophical Egg," the sealed glass vessel used to contain the work</note>, according to various circumstances of time, into many kinds of colors and forms, before it attains the full nature of Mercury and of the <term>Stone</term> <note>original: "Lap.", short for Lapis Philosophorum or Philosopher's Stone</note>, according to which diversity of preparation, time, and many kinds of colors, so many names have been devised by the Sages.

<header>Appendix.</header>

### 38. Are there then, besides this Universal, also Particulars?

Yes; and indeed as many as every molten metal still has bodily parts within itself: Now every metal, although already molten, consists—as bodily dissection <note>referring to alchemical "anatomy," or the separation of a substance into its components</note> teaches—of bodily <term>Mercury</term> <note>original symbol: ☿</note>, fixed <term>Sulphur</term> <note>original symbol: 🜍</note>, and fixed <term>Salt</term> <note>original symbol: 🜔</note>; there are thus just as many <term>Particulars</term> <note>alchemical procedures or substances that work on specific metals or "particular" cases, rather than the "Universal" medicine that transforms all things</note>, each of which can specifically have its effect with benefit.

### 39. What then are the effects of the Particulars—firstly, of Mercury, and then also of Salt and Sulphur?

The first effect of the **bodily Mercury** is this: that when united and fixed with <term>Gold-Calx</term> <note>original: ☉ Kalk; Gold reduced to a fine powder</note>, it provides an **increase** <note>original: "Augmentum"</note>. The second: that when it is dissolved by <term>Strong Water</term> <note>original symbol: 🜄 fort., referring to Aqua Fortis or Nitric Acid</note>, thereafter [rectified] <note>the original symbol indicates a process like rectification or coagulation</note>, and through calcination, putrefaction, and distillation turned into an oil, it is immediately ready for **Particular-Tinctures**. The third: that with the oil, the **Sulphur of Gold** <note>original symbol: 🜍 ☉</note> can also be extracted.

The first effect of the **fixed Salt** <note>original symbol: 🜔</note> is: that when it is drawn from a metal, whichever it may be, it transforms common mercury into **Silver** <note>original symbol: ☽</note>, regardless of the fact that it lost its spirits through melting in the **fire** <note>original symbol: 🜂</note>, as was mentioned in the Universal; for this is not to be understood absolutely, but only regarding the most noble parts (namely, in so far as it has become unfit for the <term>Mercury of the Sages</term> and the **Stone** to be made from it). Therefore, one must know that the metallic Salt cannot be so destroyed by the power of Sulphur that it does not still have sufficient spirit to penetrate. The second effect is that, after it has become red (as shown in the Universal), it can be distilled into an oil for the reason mentioned; and then—according to the testimony of **Hollandus** <note>Isaac Hollandus, a 15th-century Dutch alchemist often cited for his practical laboratory instructions</note>—it not only fixes the Mercury but also tinges the metals to a red color at a tenfold higher degree.

Finally, the effect of **fixed Sulphur** is threefold. The first is that it colors silver yellow (citrinates); the second is that it fixes common mercury; and thirdly, it is the foundation of the **Particular-Tinctures**, as **Basilius** <note>Basil Valentine, the legendary Benedictine alchemist</note> says.

# Addition.
## To Make One out of Three.

->or<-

->A clear process on how to prepare the Philosopher's Stone, both for the White and the Red, from the 3 previously mentioned Principles in the wet way, as the shorter path.<-

When you have obtained one *loth* <note>A unit of weight, approximately 14.6 grams or half an ounce.</note> of the astral or Central **Gold** <term>original symbol: ☉; representing the Solar or metallic principle of Sulphur</term>, 3 *loth* of the **Soul** or the shining **Antimony** <term>original symbol: ♁; often representing the "Earthly" or "Salt" principle in this context</term>, and 8 *loth* of the **Spirit**, as the **Mercury** <term>original symbol: ☿</term>; then take 4 and a half *loth* of your Mercury or Spirit; unite these with your Gold weighing 1 *loth*; put them together into a hermetically sealed vial, and you will see how the matter in the glass or vial, over the gentle heat of a *Balneum* <note>A water bath (balneum Mariae), used for steady, gentle heating.</note>, constantly rises and falls, and becomes quite black again, and finally, in 34 days, turns completely into a black, dry powder that remains at the bottom. 

When this is seen, one must strengthen the **Fire** <term>original symbol: 🜂</term> and maintain it at that same degree until the matter becomes like white snow and as shiny as a sheet of silver. If this has occurred and the matter has not yet become fixed <note>In alchemy, "fixation" is the process by which a volatile substance is made stable and resistant to heat.</note>, one must increase the Fire anew, and then the matter will again begin to rise and fall; it will also remain hanging in the height or the middle of the glass and not touch the bottom for 38 natural days. During this time, for nearly 30 days, so many various colors will show themselves that it is impossible to describe. Finally, the matter sinks to the bottom, and then it is fixed; and one grain of it, according to Jodocus <note>Likely referring to Jodocus von Rehe, a 17th-century alchemical writer.</note>, tinged two and a half *loth* of **Mercury** into **Silver** <term>original symbol: ☾</term>. Thus, according to Jodocus, Basilius <note>Basilius Valentinus, a legendary 15th-century alchemist/monk whose writings were highly influential.</note>, and others, is the true Philosopher’s Stone prepared in the wet way for the White <note>The "White Stone" or "Little Work" was believed to transmute base metals into silver.</note>.

After this preparation, take the Soul or the **Antimony**, weighing 3 *loth*: Unite it with the remaining 3 ½ *loth* of Mercury, and distill them often through an *alembic* <note>The top part of a still, used for distillation.</note> until they have been well united through the distillation. Afterward, divide it into 7 parts and <gloss>imbibe</gloss> <note>The process of "imbibition" involves adding a liquid to a dry substance until it is saturated.</note> the Stone with one part after the other, through sevenfold imbibing and coagulating. Then the Stone, in the first <gloss>imbibition</gloss> <note>The OCR reads "Inhibition," likely a variant or typo for Imbibition.</note> and coagulation, tinges Mercury and **Lead** <term>original symbol: ♄</term> into Silver; and in the Silver, after separation, about 2 grains of Gold were found. In the 4th imbibition, however, one part tinges 4 parts of Copper into Gold; in the 5th, one part already falls upon 100 parts; in the 6th, upon 1,000; in the 7th, upon 10,000. And so the Stone is also prepared for the Red <note>The "Red Stone" or "Great Work" was the final goal, capable of transmuting base metals into gold and acting as a universal medicine.</note>.

->To GOD alone the glory.<-

### III.
# Extract
### From the Latin Manuscript:
## MANNA COELESTE, called the HEAVENLY MANNA.
### .

### The Preparation of the Stone.

Take in the name of God the best **Lead** <term>original symbol: ♄; understood here as the Philosophical Lead-Ore</term> or Earth; sieve and cleanse it of all impurity, roots, stones, or any other foreign matter that Nature has begun to form. Place this "tree" into an **alembic** <note>A distillation vessel consisting of a gourd-like container and a cap with a beak.</note>, cover it well with a blind cap <note>A cap without a spout, used for digestion rather than distillation.</note>, and set it for 40 days in **horse dung** <note>Decaying horse manure was a standard laboratory tool used to provide a gentle, steady, and natural heat through fermentation.</note>. After that, distill its **Water** <term>original symbol: 🜔</term> from it three times, so that the last shall then be the true philosophical and mineral **Water**. Save half of this for the "unification," and with the other half proceed further to **putrefaction** <note>The stage of decomposition where the matter turns black, seen as a necessary death before rebirth.</note> in horse dung for 40 days. Next, draw out your two multiplying **Spirits** <term>original symbol: 🜓os</term> and keep them, each separately, in two glasses until the time of multiplication. Then, take the **Water of Nature** <term>original symbol: 🜔 naturæ</term> which remained at the bottom of the alembic, and add twice its weight of the first saved **Water**. Seal it in an egg-shaped vial and let it stand in horse dung until the **White Work** <note>Also known as the *Albedo*, the stage where the matter becomes a white stone capable of transmuting metals into silver.</note> is completed, which will happen within 7 months, during which time it will turn white. Subsequently, take it out and multiply it with your white **Mercury** <term>original symbol: ☿</term>; thus the Stone will be multiplied in a short time and driven to a transparent redness.

### The Multiplication.

Take your **White Stone**, dissolve it in your white **Mercury** which you have kept for this purpose; place it in the furnace for one month, as you have been taught in the practice, during which time your Stone will become red. Thereafter, take your red **Mercury**, or Oil, and dissolve the **Red Stone** within it; let it stand again for one month, and your medicine will be increased from 10 parts to 100. You may repeat this four times, but beware of the fifth repetition, lest you find your glass broken, as I have found through my own unfortunate experience. Had I been led by the hand and taught in this way, I would not have failed. You may multiply four times, but no more. Then the Stone is good: 1. For health. 2. For multiplication. 3. For the preparation of precious pearls. 4. For the transformation of all metals into **running Mercury** <term>original symbol: ☿ curr.; quicksilver</term>. And 5. For the performance of various magical things.

# The First Use for Health.

Many among the wise, who did not know the proper use of the Stone, have taken some 1/4 <term>grain</term> <note>A tiny unit of weight, approximately 65 milligrams.</note>, others more or less, and found death instead of health. For it requires more care than one might imagine. The only and safest way to drive away all diseases in all people with it is as follows:

<term>Recipe</term> <note>original: "℞." - the traditional symbol for a medical prescription.</note> 4 <term>grains</term> of the Stone, by <term>goldsmith's weight</term> <note>A precise measurement system, also known as Troy weight, used for precious metals and medicines.</note>, and dissolve them in a <term>pint</term> <note>A unit of liquid volume, roughly half a liter.</note> of Rhine or French wine; but not in strong <term>liquors</term> <note>original: "Liquoribus."</note>, such as Spanish or Canary Muscat wine, a <term>water of life</term> <note>original: "Aqua vitæ"; referring here to brandy or distilled spirits.</note>, and similar such heating wines. Place it in a large glass that is clean and strong, and the wine will quickly turn red, almost like the medicine itself—namely, quite a deep red. Let the glass stand for four days, covered and free from dust, because it is an oily substance that you cannot dissolve sooner. Afterward, pour another <term>pint</term> of wine into it, stir it with a clean little wooden stick or <term>ivory</term>, and keep adding more wine until it takes on a beautiful gold color and you see that no more redness is present within. For this redness, if any were still there, would be a sign to you that the <term>tincture</term> has not yet been sufficiently diluted <note>original: "ausgedehnet," meaning expanded or extended in volume.</note>, and would therefore inflame the body and drive out the spirit <note>A warning that the undiluted Stone is so energetic it causes death.</note>.

Whether the wine is yellow enough can be seen at the top of the glass, namely when a subtle and white <term>circle</term> <note>original: "Circul."</note> appears like a pearl, which usually happens after four hours of movement. As soon as you see such a sign, then filter the wine; thus this white matter will remain hanging on the <term>filter</term> <note>original: "Filtro."</note> like a pearl, but the wine will become yellow, like <term>gold</term> <note>original symbol: "☉" - the alchemical symbol for the Sun and Gold.</note> itself.

These are the certain signs by which you shall do yourself no harm, and without which the wine will become so strong that it inflames the body, or where it is too weak, it brings no benefit. Know, therefore, that this is a great secret. In all internal diseases, give a spoonful of this <term>liquid</term> <note>original: "Liquore."</note> every morning, and it will soon drive the illness out through a gentle sweat; for it does not purge the body, nor does it provoke vomiting, nor does it drive such a heavy sweat that one becomes weak from it, but rather it strengthens the person. And if the disease has lasted many years, then use this medicine for 12 days continuously; but all other diseases it cures within 24 hours. In external injuries, such as: ulcers, <term>scabs</term> <note>original: "Gräze"; likely scabies or itchy skin eruptions.</note>, <term>fistulas</term>, <term>touch-me-not</term> <note>original: "noli me tangere"; a historical term for corrosive skin ulcers or skin cancer.</note>, etc., smear the damaged place with the Stone itself, which is an oil that was not dissolved in the wine, and do this for 9 days in a row. Furthermore, whoever carries the Stone upon themselves cannot be attacked by any evil spirit, nor will any join them. If the Stone is used on a possessed person, the evil spirit can no longer remain with them,
