## The Second Use is for Multiplication.

Many have made the white and red stone, who have not known its multiplication. For the white stone becomes red when one persists with the external fire <note>original: "$\triangle$"</note>; however, neither the red nor the white gives a higher <term>projection</term> <note>The final stage of alchemy where the Stone is cast upon base metal to transmute it.</note> than one part to 10. But if you do not take great care and guard yourself, the smell alone will be able to kill you. Now, if you want to increase the stone infinitely, so that it is no longer congealed into a dust, but must remain in the form of an oil, then proceed as follows: After the **philosophical mercury** <note>original: "$\mercury$ Phil." - a purified alchemical substance, not common quicksilver.</note> is prepared (which can happen within 40 days), you must bring it back to putrefaction in the same way you made it; and this can be well accomplished in a short time in a urine-glass or a <term>small cucurbit</term> <note>original: "Cucurbitula" - a gourd-shaped chemical vessel.</note> with a <term>blind head</term> <note>original: "blinden Hut" - a still-head without a spout, used to force vapors back down to the bottom (reflux).</note>. In the same vessel, put no more than 12 ounces of the matter; seal it or close it with a <term>lute</term> <note>original: "Luto" - a specialized airtight sealing paste.</note>, which I will teach you hereafter; (but in a <term>vial</term> it will not work.) When your matter now becomes like melted or flowing pitch, take the glass out and place it in the furnace with common ash; and when it has cooled in 24 hours, take the blind head from the cucurbit, place another one on top, and set a wide <term>receiver</term> <note>original: "Recipienten" - the vessel that collects the distilled liquid.</note> before it. But watch yourself well here, that the vapor does you no harm. Furthermore, seal the <term>joints</term> <note>original: "Junckturen"</note> of the head and the receiver diligently with the following lute: Take <note>original: "℞."</note> 1 ounce of eggshells <term>calcined</term> <note>Burnt to a white powder.</note> for 24 hours; 2 ounces of <term>amausa</term> <note>A type of glass-like flux or enamel.</note> pulverized more finely than flour; and mix them together; moisten it with egg whites beaten together, and make a dough out of it; with this, smear a softened pig’s or ox’s bladder, then place it threefold around the joints and bind it well. Let it dry there for 24 hours, and place the glass so deep in the ash that it rises 6 fingers high above the putrefied matter; the <term>cap</term> <note>original: "Capitellum" - the top part of the distillation apparatus.</note> should be very cold. Make a gentle fire until you see a snow-white vapor rising; and continue with it until no more white smoke or vapor rises; thereafter let it cool for 24 hours, so the aforementioned white vapor will become an oil, or a thick, slimy, and <term>viscous juice</term>, which is the **white mercury** <note>original: "$\mercury$"</note>, for the multiplication of the white stone: Then remove the receiver from it, set another before it, and seal it as before; fill the furnace...

For **projection** <note>the act of casting the Stone upon base metals</note> with the white stone, take a tenth part of silver and throw nine parts of the stone upon it; keep it in flux for twenty-four hours: this is the **fermentation**. # The Fifth Use is for Certain Magical Effects;

## The first of which represents and depicts

### The Creation of the World.

<term>Take <note>original: "℞," the symbol for "recipe," used here to introduce an alchemical process.</note></term> Rainwater, about 80 pounds; preserve it in well-sealed glasses for 40 days, and it will become foul-smelling and the dregs will settle to the bottom. Gently pour the clear part into a wide, round wooden vessel so that the vessel is one-third full. Place it in a secret spot in the sun at noon. Let a single drop of the blessed stone <note>The Philosopher's Stone</note> fall into this water, and you will soon see a thick and black smoke on its surface, just as it was during the Creation. After that, pour two more little drops into it, and you will recognize the separation of the light from the darkness; and so, little by little, every half-quarter of an hour <note>Approximately 7.5 minutes</note>, add 3, then 4, then 5, and finally 6 drops, but after that nothing more. Then you will see upon the water, one after another, everything that God created in six days, as well as the manner of the Creation and inexpressible mysteries. Let it stand thus, and in half a quarter-hour, everything will disappear.

Appendix. 555

## On Good Company and Acquaintance with the Sages.

When you carry the Stone before you in full light above our horizon, and walk alone in the garden, take a portion of the first prepared rainwater; pour as much of the **white stone** into it as you previously poured of the **red stone**; then vapors will soon rise up to the <term>Moon <note>original: "☽," the astrological and alchemical symbol for the Moon or silver.</note></term>. If you observe this every month at the proper time, there shall be no <term>Sage <note>A master alchemist who has successfully completed the "Great Work."</note></term> living upon the same horizon as you, who is also a possessor of the Stone, who shall not become known to you. For at that same time, he also goes out and looks toward the East, South, West, and North to see if he might perceive such an effect, performed by an <term>Artist <note>A common historical term for a practitioner of alchemy or the "Hermetic Arts."</note></term> who wishes to make his acquaintance; and he will immediately answer your operation in the same aforementioned manner. In this way, you shall learn to recognize the possessors of the Stone. The fourth [use] helps toward

## A Good Gathering.

If you desire a meeting with the Sages and their companions, then anoint the temples of your head with the **white stone** at that same nightly hour, and pray earnestly that you may learn what kind of person it is. Place 3 freshly plucked **laurel leaves** under your pillow, and fix your <term>imagination <note>In alchemical practice, "imagination" was considered a literal creative force of the mind, capable of perceiving or manifesting spiritual truths.</note></term> upon recognizing him. Thus fall asleep, and when you wake, remember the face of the person, his name, and the place where he resides; and if you do not go to him, he will come to you, thinking that perhaps the secret has not yet been fully revealed to you. The cause of this effect is the **universal spirit of vitality** <note>original: "allgemeine Lust-Geist." This refers to the *spiritus mundi*, a subtle substance believed to permeate the universe and transmit information or influence across distances.</note> which, being locked within the Stone, accomplishes such things. The Sages, with whom you can thus become acquainted everywhere, reveal themselves more often in a poor form than a rich one. Before you undertake these operations, however, you must use the Stone for nine consecutive days, as I have taught you before.

### Chapter I. On the Brevity and Blessedness of the Hermetic Science.

In learning a mechanical or other art, one finds that "art is long and life is short" <note>A reference to the famous Hippocratic aphorism "Ars longa, vita brevis."</note>: But when one possesses the **Hermetic Science** <note>The study of alchemy and secret wisdom attributed to Hermes Trismegistus.</note>, a short art and a long life are required: For our work is so easy that one would not believe it if it were told in plain words, and our **Medicine** is so full of life that the Wise reach an extraordinarily high age through it.

### Chapter II. Why the Science is difficult, and why it is easy?

The difficulty of the same consists, as <term>Trevisanus <note>Bernard Trevisan (1406–1490), a famous Italian alchemist known for his search for the Philosopher's Stone.</note></term> says, in our words and the sense of them: The ease comes from the understanding of the words according to their spirit, not according to their literal sound, because understanding according to the letter is nothing but ignorance.

### Chapter III. To recognize the Matter is difficult, but to handle it correctly is far more difficult.

The knowledge of the **true Matter**, upon which both Nature and Art work, is quite difficult to attain, because the "envious" Wise <note>Alchemists often described themselves as "envious," meaning they were jealous guardians of their secrets, hiding the truth from the unworthy.</note> have hidden it under the names of all things; but more than difficult—

### Chapter IV. How the Matter of the Wise is constituted?

The first matter of the Wise is the last of Nature: Art begins where Nature ends; but Art helps Nature as a **midwife** <note>A common alchemical metaphor suggesting the alchemist does not create, but only assists the natural "birth" of the Stone.</note>, when she remains inactive, either due to the fault of the unsuitable "birthing-mother" <note>Referring to the vessel or the base substance in which the transformation occurs.</note> or a coincidental abundance of foreign things.

### Chapter V. The division of Matter.

Matter is of two kinds: One is called the "First," the other the "Second," and it is the latter which is found in all places, and is sold publicly for the lowest price; which one can also have in one's own house for free. The "First" is not found on earth nor under the earth, for it is our Water—that is, our <term>mineral Mercury <note>original: "☿"</note></term>—which has been drawn out of the "Second Matter" through the skillful work of the Wise. This second matter is coarse and base, and is held in very low regard by the ignorant, but is considered quite precious by the Wise.

### Chapter VI. The description of the Second Matter.

This well-known Matter is found in all places, in all people, and in every single thing. It is base, and is very often thrown into the streets by the maids, and likewise, children play with it in the alleys. It is spread daily in abundance over the entire surface of the earth. It is the same matter which Adam took with him into his grave; which the builders of Solomon's Temple rejected <note>A reference to the "Stone which the builders rejected" from Psalm 118, often used alchemically to describe the common starting material.</note>, and without which no one can live: with which all things are nourished: which we have constantly before our eyes day and night, and whose **coagulated spirit** is better than the whole world.

### Chapter VII. What the proximate Matter is?

It consists of two parts, namely two **mercurial beings**, which are opposed to one another: For when one is warm, the other is cold; if one is volatile, the other is constant; if one is soft, the other is hard; if one is oily, the other is salty. Yet these contrary beings are inseparably united, and can only be separated by a Wise person—without the destruction of the whole—from the superfluous oily being that was mixed among them by chance.

### Chapter IX. What body does this congealed air, which SENDIVOGIUS calls the first matter of metals, take on?

## Chapter X. Explanation of the Saying of MORIENUS.

### Chapter XII. That the Stone is made from nothing but fire, and that **Fire** <note>original symbol: Δ</note> is but one single thing, both in heaven and on earth.

The essence of the Stone is nothing other than a pure **Fire** <note>original symbol: Δ</note>; and the same fire that burns in kitchens, shines in light, and glows in the heavens, and which gives life, is the true essence of our Stone. Also, the Stone is not distinguished from Fire, except only in this: that the Philosopher’s Stone is a fixed fire, while elementary fire is a volatile fire. Know then, student eager for learning! that the volatility or great movement of the essence of fire when it burns causes the combustion and alteration in all combustible materials. For fire penetrates all things, except for gold, down to their smallest particles, and raises them up because of its uncommonly swift volatility, and separates or divides them from one another in the process of lifting them, thus carrying the whole away with it. When, as in gold and the Stone, something fixed and earthy remains, it does not hinder or resist the strong union; for because the entire essence of this same fire is the most subtle, volatile, and penetrating **Alkali**, which has been attracted by the most subtle earthly **Volatile** light, it is gradually moved and driven about by the power of the unceasing light. This light, in seeking to unite with the most subtle essence of the **Alkali**, moves it powerfully and violently, even if we cannot clearly or properly see it. From this it follows that if that same most subtle essence were fixed, it could not burn, because it would not possess that same movement which moves nature and from which combustion arises. This most subtle alkaline fixed essence is found only in metals, in which cold is united. Indeed, the true pure metallic essence is nothing other than the nature of fire itself—namely, the congealed fire itself. The artist, however, must dissolve the congealed and fix the dissolved when he wishes to make the Stone, and this can be made from nothing other than the nature of fire.

There are two elements, Earth and **Water** <note>original symbol: ∇</note>; indeed, only one true one, namely **Water**, is found. The mixed essences of fire and air are of a different nature, with which light is always united. Light, however, can enter no body or element more easily than the essence of fire, and the essence of fire itself cannot act without light. Since, therefore, the Stone is only a fixed fire, this essence of fire itself must be considered the Matter; and since it is the radical moisture <term>radical moisture <note>original: "Wurzel-Feuchtigkeit"; the vital fluid or "innate heat" believed to sustain life in living beings.</note></term> in animals and all things—

### Chapter XIII. Knowledge of the Matter is Useless Without the Art.

Knowledge of the second matter is the door which opens a free entrance to the closed palace of the King. Afterward, the knowledge of our <term>fire <note>symbol: Δ</note></term>—which is called the proximate <term>matter <note>original: "Materia"; the physical substance used in the work</note></term> of the Stone—is such a hidden secret that it is found only through the secret art of the easiest practice, which is nonetheless very difficult to obtain. Indeed, it is a wonder of the Art; for he who understands the work understands the whole of science, and he who does not understand it loses time, effort, and expense in the handling of the matter. This is because the philosophical operation in the preparation can only be learned through a great gift of God, by means of long-term diligence, or through the instruction of an experienced master. Hence it happens that many who know the matter do not know how to use it.

### Chapter XIV. Why many who know the matter do not know how to use it?

The cause of this ignorance in the artistic work is simply the variety of preparations among both the modern and ancient <term>authors <note>original: "Auctoribus"</note></term>, who have come to the work through various paths. Some have attained it with great labor and a long time, others with lighter effort and shorter manual operations. The ancients push heavily for <term>dissolution <note>original: "Auflösung"; the process of turning a solid into a liquid state</note></term>, the moderns for **calcination** <note>the reduction of a substance to powder or ash through heat</note>. *Artefius* places the whole art in the fire; with whom *Pontanus* and *Trevisan* agree. *Lullius* places it in the weights; *Sendivogius* in the extraction of his <term>sal ammoniac <note>original: "salis ammoniaci"; a salt used as a flux or to clean metals</note></term>, and *Paracelsus* swears that the whole work consists in the <term>composition <note>original: "Composition"</note></term> of his <term>mineral electrum <note>original: "Electri Mineralis"; a specific alchemical alloy or mixture of metals</note></term>. Therefore, the students of the Art go astray because they do not find the very same things in one author that they note in another, and they do not consider that every author has his own process. Therefore, it is clumsy to rebuke now this one, now another, as if they were not in agreement; for they have obtained one goal in a single matter through different means, according to the Italian proverb: ->*Our ancestors have all arrived at one result through diverse paths.* <note>original Italian: "J nostri Antiochi [Antichi] per diverse vie sono tutti arrivati ad un' efferto."</note><- (Long before us, the wise ancients attained one goal through many paths.)

<summary>This page explains that knowing the correct "matter" (fire) is insufficient without the practical "Art" of the work. It accounts for the confusing contradictions between famous alchemists like Paracelsus and Lullius by explaining that they simply used different methods to reach the same goal.</summary>

### Chapter XV. What is the Proximate Matter?

The proximate matter is our volatile <term>water <note>symbol: ▽</note></term>, which is drawn from no single vegetable, mineral, or animal thing; not from dew, nor rain, nor honey, wax, or chalk; not from salts or metals, but solely from the <insert>previously described</insert> second matter. This second matter rises from the earth to heaven, and from heaven to the earth, through the power of the rays of the <term>Sun <note>symbol: ☉</note></term> and <term>Moon <note>symbol: ☽</note></term>. From this second matter alone is our <term>water <note>symbol: ▽</note></term> extracted, which is the proximate and first matter of the blessed Stone.

### Chapter XVI. What is our Water?

Our water is the fountain in which the King and Queen bathe, and the true <term>Mary’s Bath <note>original: "B. M." or "Balneum Mariae"; a gentle heating method using water, like a double boiler</note></term> of the Wise. It is wet and dries; dry and moistens. Aside from this <term>water <note>symbol: ▽</note></term>, the chemists should seek nothing else: no furnace, no vessel, no fire. This <term>water <note>symbol: ▽</note></term> encompasses everything that is necessary within itself. It is the <term>fire <note>symbol: △</note></term>, the vessel, the furnace, and everything.

### Chapter XVII. Division of the Water.

Our <term>water <note>symbol: ▽</note></term> is divided into the first and the second: the first is called Eva; the immaculate virgin; the volatile part; the spiritually impregnated <term>Beja <note>a traditional alchemical name for the feminine principle or Mercury</note></term>; the <term>universal Mercury <note>symbol: ☿</note></term>. The other is called the <term>Sun of Nature <note>symbol: ☉</note></term>; Virgin's Milk; permanent moisture; <term>Foliated Earth <note>original: "Terra Foliata"; a stage where the matter appears in leaf-like layers</note></term>; the <term>Mercury of the Wise <note>symbol: ☿</note></term>, which encompasses everything that the Wise seek.

### Chapter XVIII. Of the Philosophical Fountain, Vessel, and Furnace.

Our fountain, vessel, and furnace are in our <term>water <note>symbol: ▽</note></term>. That is the furnace, vessel, fountain, and <term>enclosure <note>original: "Clausura"</note></term>. In it, as a clear, bright, flowing, warm, and living <term>water <note>symbol: ▽</note></term>, our King comes to life again and kills all his enemies. The <term>fire <note>symbol: △</note></term> which is within it digests the <term>fire <note>symbol: △</note></term> and warms the bath. The moisture, which is a smoke within it, holds the enclosure and the bond within itself; and thus this water—which is an exceedingly bright fountain drawn from the sea, clear, crystalline, and not yet brought back into its <term>saline <note>original: "sialische"; likely referring to the nature of salts or fluids</note></term> nature through our art—is fire, smoke, bath, lock, and bond; in short, it is everything. In it, with it, and through it all is, all becomes, and all consists. And everything is nothing else but our <term>water <note>symbol: ▽</note></term>; indeed, without it, all is vanity of vanities, and everything is entirely vain in the chemical work.

### Chapter XIX. Why the philosophical Water <note>symbol: ▽</note> is called a "strong Water" <note>original: "▽ fortis" or "aqua fortis"</note>?

Our first water is called a <term>parting-water <note>original: "Scheid-Wasser"; a strong acid, like nitric acid, used to separate silver from gold</note></term> because it is a sea-water <note>symbol: ▽</note>, sharp and corrosive. Therefore SALMANAZAR <note>a name often attributed to a legendary alchemical authority</note> says: Our water <note>symbol: ▽</note> is a corrosive fire <note>symbol: △</note>, and it cannot be otherwise, because our water <note>symbol: ▽</note> is a pure spirit which, without its body, is always corrosive. It is also called a strong water <note>original: "▽ fort."</note> because it wets and <term>calcines <note>reduces to a powder through heat or corrosion</note></term> everything, except for the metallic radical moisture. And if it did not wet, no dissolution would be achieved. A dissolution, as <term>Geber <note>Abu Musa Jabir ibn Hayyan, an influential 8th-century chemist and alchemist</note></term> teaches, cannot happen through acidic spirits alone which possess "ponticities" <note>original: "Ponticitates"; a term for sharpness, astringency, or the power to penetrate</note>; and the acidic spirit exists in the water <note>symbol: ▽</note> without its body with the un-elemental moistening. Although this same water is fluid, clear, pure, and crystalline, it does not wet, except in a certain way, until the non-wetting metallic and immortal water <note>symbol: ▽</note> has been united with its body—not with corrosivity, but rather with a great sweetness.

### Chapter XX. Concerning the Philosophical Fires.

We have three fires <note>symbol: △</note> without which the <term>hermetic work <note>the process of creating the Philosopher's Stone</note></term> cannot be performed. The natural fire comes from the Sun and Moon and is the innate warmth, the fire of nature <note>symbol: △</note>, which is <term>congealed <note>frozen or solidified</note></term> in its innermost womb. The Unnatural fire is that which is stirred up by art, and is transformed by the <term>Philosopher</term> from a dry thing into a moist thing, because in this fire <note>symbol: △</note>—which is called a bath, that is, a water <note>symbol: ▽</note>—the putrefaction of our <term>body <note>original: "Cörpers"</note></term> or our "Adam" <note>a term for the raw material or the "first man" of the work</note> takes place. The Counter-natural fire <note>symbol: △</note> is our first water <note>symbol: ▽</note>, which destroys, <term>calcines</term>, grinds down, and annihilates everything; for it dissolves the form of the stone or its specific <term>figure <note>original: "specificam"</note></term>, not into clouds, but into a philosophical water <note>symbol: ▽</note>.

### Chapter XXI. The Contrary Effects of the Fires.

The Counter-natural fire <note>symbol: △</note> destroys the <term>composite <note>original: "Compositum"; the mixture of ingredients</note></term> and brings it to putrefaction; but the natural fire <note>symbol: △</note>, which is added to it, conversely <term>congeals</term> the spirit of the solid body that was dissolved by the Counter-natural fire into a philosophical (and not a cloud-like) water <note>symbol: ▽</note>. However, in the cloud-water, the natural fire <note>symbol: △</note>—the volatile spirit—is never seen without its body.

### Chapter XXII. The Division of Fires according to ARTEFIUS.

<term>ARTEFIUS <note>a celebrated alchemist, often cited as a master of the "secret fire"</note></term> divides them into the ash-fire <note>symbol: △</note>, the lamp-fire <note>symbol: △</note>, and the fire <note>symbol: △</note> of our water. Our water <note>symbol: ▽</note> is a fire that we need throughout the entire work: in the beginning, in the middle, and at the end. The other two we do not need except occasionally. But if we wish to speak freely, all fires are comprised within our water <note>symbol: ▽</note>. Within it is Air <note>symbol: 🜁</note>, which indeed does not rule, yet [rules] the bath of the

### Chap. XXIII. On Common and Chemical Calcination.

Common calcination is the separation of the moist and the dry, and a destruction of the composite; indeed, a corruption of the volatile and fixed radical moisture <note>original: "Humidi radicalis"; the essential life-force or "sap" of a substance</note>, so that a body remains behind which has been transformed into an ash that cannot be melted. Therefore, without moisture, it yields no flow <note>cannot be cast or poured</note>, but rather turns to glass. Philosophical calcination is a spiritual and invisible evaporation of our volatile essence from our body, and a drying of the same body, with the preservation—indeed, with the increase—of the fixed radical moisture, so that it easily drinks back in its volatile part, which is separated from the fixed part by a wonderful art. Common calcination happens with a powerful melting fire <note>symbol: Δ</note> and strong water <note>original: "∇ forti"; likely aqua fortis or a strong acid</note>; but ours happens with the very gentlest fire <note>symbol: Δ</note>, without great violence of the flame, so that our matter retains its sweetness or porosity during the extraction of the volatile <term>As <note>likely referring to the "Aes" or the essential metallic body</note></term>.

### Chap. XXIV. On Common and Chemical Distillation.

Common distillation is an extraction of all moistures from the solid matter, with the alteration of the composite and the destruction of its particular form; by the Spagyrists <note>original: "Spagyricis"; alchemists who follow the Paracelsian method of "separating and recombining"</note> it is also called a circulation of the vapor, which becomes water at the bottom of the receiver <note>original: "Recipienten"; the vessel that catches the condensed liquid</note>. Philosophical distillation is a raising of the water <note>symbol: ∇</note> from the earth <note>symbol: 🜃</note>, indeed a dissolution of our volatile essence into a water <note>symbol: ∇</note>, which is no common water <note>symbol: ∇</note>, but rather a spirit that sits upon a water of its own kind; and this extraction is the secret of the art, because it happens in a very wonderful way, due to its lightness, without any method of distilling common to the alchemists.

### Chap. XXV. On Common and Chemical Sublimation.

Common sublimation is a lifting of the matter toward the sides of the vessel, and into the head of the aludel <note>original: "in capite Aludelis"; the top part of a pear-shaped sublimation pot</note>. But philosophical sublimation is a sweeping out of the impurity from the matter, through which our "one thing" is made volatile, noble, and pure; and yet nothing foreign is added, nor is anything taken from its essence. Rather, one only sublimates it and removes the superfluous and foreign elements—not through a common sublimation, which does not transform everything that is superfluous, impure, and dreggy into the right matter, as the philosophical sublimation does by means of our fire <note>symbol: Δ</note>.

### Chap. XXVI. That Sublimation, Distillation, Calcination, Dissolution, Putrefaction, and Union are performed through Cooking.

One does not calcine without distilling; one does not distill without sublimating; and one does not sublimate without dissolving <note>original: "solviren"</note>; one does not dissolve unless the matter is brought to putrefaction; one does not unite them unless they have been separated. And as many labors as there are, when one possesses our philosophical <term>fire <note>symbol: Δ</note></term>, they are but one, namely: Cooking. Cook, and do not let the cooking vex you, because in natural cooking alone so many works are performed; and gold, through mere cooking in our water, when it is digested to the highest degree, is brought back and becomes a Stone that <term>tinges <note>from Latin "tingere"; to transform or "dye" the nature of a base metal into a noble one</note></term> all common metals into gold.

### Chap. XXVII. Whether the Gold that the Stone requires be common <term>gold <note>symbol: ☉</note></term>?

Common <term>gold <note>symbol: ☉</note></term> is entirely and utterly a dead <term>gold <note>symbol: ☉</note></term>, and no longer possesses the fertilizing spirit of life, but has lost it in the melting-<term>fire <note>symbol: Δ</note></term>. That same mineral spirit, which fled from the melted common <term>gold <note>symbol: ☉</note></term>, is the gold which the Sages require. However, moved by compassion for the blindness of an inexperienced student, I will reveal how far one is distinguished from the other in every part through the following comparison.

### Chap. XXVIII. Inequality of common and philosophical Gold.

Our gold is pure spirit; the common is pure body. Our spirit is the bodily form of the <term>gold <note>symbol: ☉</note></term>; the common is the matter shaped by this spirit. As far as matter is from form, so far is common gold distinguished from philosophical <term>gold <note>symbol: ☉</note></term>. Nature makes the common kind merely through <term>coagulation <note>the process of a liquid becoming solid</note></term>, because she has no hands to dissolve <note>original: "solviren"</note> and coagulate the matter through repeated dissolution. Philosophical <term>gold <note>symbol: ☉</note></term> does not stop at the first coagulation of nature, but is brought higher through our Art, and raised into a tinging spiritual body through repeated dissolving and coagulating. The common is thick and dense, a material part that is robbed of our spiritual essence, which it allowed to depart in the most violent torture of the fire <note>the author refers to the intense heat of the smelting furnace as a "martyrdom" or torture that kills the metal's spirit</note>. Our <term>gold <note>symbol: ☉</note></term> is that same spiritual substance itself, which flees from the <term>fire <note>symbol: Δ</note></term>. Finally, common <term>gold <note>symbol: ☉</note></term> is only a dead and a single body; but ours is a living and a double one. Of this, one part is fixed, cooked, and purified; the other is raw and not fully <term>digested <note>matured or refined by heat</note></term>. Thus and in such a manner, where inactive nature has ceased, Art begins; and after the superfluous essence is set aside and the separation of the fixed part from the volatile is accomplished, Art assists nature anew, until from the two bodies of our <term>gold <note>symbol: ☉</note></term>, one penetrating, immortal, and tinging body is made.

### Chap. XXIX. Whether common mercury <term>mercury <note>symbol: ☿</note></term> is used for the preparation of the Stone?

Common mercury <note>symbol: ☿</note> does not enter into our work, nor can the Stone be made with it or from it; neither can the Mercury of the Sages be drawn from it. It is entirely distinct from common, physical mercury, which one may rightly call a "deceiver of alchemists." Our Mercury is a true spirit, from which all metals originate as if from a seed. Even the common mercury or quicksilver sold in apothecaries is a true body that has remained material because nature has not provided it with its own "worker" <note>the internal "agent" or "formative fire" required for growth</note>, despite the fact that within common mercury, that same universal spirit we seek is frequently hidden. Yet, at the very moment it enters the physical matter of the quicksilver, it becomes "specified" <note>limited to a specific form</note> and useless for our work, which deals solely with living, spiritual metals, and not with physical ones that are internally united with our universal matter.

### Chap. XXX. Objection against the Matter.

If every thing brings forth its own kind, and <term>gold <note>symbol: ☉</note></term> cooked to the highest degree becomes a <term>tinging <note>transformative</note></term> Stone, then one must surely seek the gold-making seed within gold <note>symbol: ☉</note>, and cannot find it in such a lowly and common thing as Chapter VI claims. Rather, it must be found in its own body, which is gold <note>symbol: ☉</note>. For the seed of wheat is wheat, the seed of a dog is in a dog, and of a human in a human. Furthermore, the saying of Sendivogius <note>original: "SENDIVOGII"; referring to Michael Sendivogius, a famous 17th-century alchemist</note> is not contrary to this—namely, that common gold <note>symbol: ☉</note> has lost its spirit in the melting-<term>fire <note>symbol: △</note></term> and is therefore dead. For if that were so, common gold <note>symbol: ☉</note> could never be made living again; since a dead body cannot return to life without a miracle of Divine Omnipotence. Therefore, a spirit cannot return into a soulless metallic body. However, gold <note>symbol: ☉</note> *can* be revitalized and raised to the essence of the Stone; therefore, the Stone must be sought in gold <note>symbol: ☉</note>, and our mercury <note>symbol: ☿</note> must be taken from no other thing than gold <note>symbol: ☉</note>.

### Chap. XXXI. Refutation of the above objection.

"In gold <note>symbol: ☉</note> is the seed of gold, and from metals must metals come." So cry the inexperienced chemical bunglers confidently, those who do not raise the eyes of their mind above the horizon of their physical sight. But metals and minerals, while they still hang in their <term>matrix <note>the "womb" of the earth where minerals grow</note></term>, do possess their seed within them, contrary to this opinion; however, outside of the mines and matrices, they are without seed. They are like severed bodies or limbs that have been cut off and separated from animals and plants, which then have no seed—indeed, from the very moment that the life-sap, the rising life-

### Chap. XXVI. That Sublimation, Distillation, Calcination, Dissolution, Putrefaction, and Union are all performed through Boiling.

One does not calcinate without distilling; one does not distill without sublimating; and one does not sublimate without dissolving; one does not dissolve if the matter is not brought to putrefaction; one does not unite them if they have not first been separated. And as many types of work as there are, when one possesses our **philosophical fire** <note>original symbol: $\Delta$, representing the internal heat of the vessel</note>, they are but one: namely, **boiling**. Boil, and do not let the boiling weary you, because in natural boiling alone are so many works performed. Through mere boiling in our **water**, when it is digested to the highest degree, gold is brought back and becomes a **Stone** that <term>tinges <note>transforms the color and essential nature</note></term> all common metals into gold.

### Chap. XXVII. Whether the gold required for the Stone is common gold <note>original symbol: $\odot$</note>?

Common gold <note>original symbol: $\odot$</note> is entirely a dead thing and no longer possesses the fructifying spirit of life; rather, it has lost it in the **melting-fire** <note>original: Schmelz-$\Delta$</note>. That same mineral spirit which fled from the melted common gold is the "gold" that the Sages require. However, moved by compassion for the blindness of an inexperienced student, I shall reveal how far one is distinguished from the other in every respect through the following comparison.

### Chap. XXVIII. The Inequality between Common and Philosophical Gold.

Our gold is pure spirit; the common is pure body. Our spirit is the bodily **form** <note>the organizing principle or "soul" of the metal</note> of gold; the common is the matter shaped by this spirit. As far as matter is from form, so far is common gold distinguished from the philosophical. Nature produces common gold merely through **coagulation** <note>solidification</note> because she has no hands to dissolve and coagulate the matter again through repeated dissolution. Philosophical gold does not stop at Nature's first coagulation; rather, it is brought higher through our **Art** <note>the practice of Alchemy</note> and raised into a tinging spiritual body through repeated dissolving and coagulating. 

Common gold is thick and dense, a material portion deprived of our spiritual essence, which it allowed to escape during the violent martyrdom of the fire. Our gold is that very same spiritual substance itself which flees from the fire. Finally, common gold is but a dead and single body; ours, however, is a living and double one. Of these two, one is fixed, boiled, and purified; the other is raw and not fully <term>digested <note>matured or ripened by heat</note></term>. Thus, where inactive Nature has stopped, the Art begins; after the superfluous essence is set aside and the separation of the fixed part from the volatile is accomplished, the Art assists Nature anew until, from the two bodies of our gold, one penetrating, immortal, and tinging body is formed.

### Chap. XXIX. Whether common Mercury is used for the preparation of the Stone?

Common mercury <note>original symbol: ☿</note> does not enter into our work; the Stone can neither be made with it nor from it, nor can the **Mercury of the Sages** be drawn from it. This Mercury of the Sages is entirely distinct from the common, physical metal, which one may rightly call a "deceiver of the alchemists." Our Mercury is a true spirit, from which all metals originate, as if from a seed. Even the common mercury or quicksilver sold in apothecaries is a true "body" that has remained in a material state because Nature did not provide it with its own internal **agent** <note>German: "Würker," meaning an active force or catalyst</note>. This is despite the fact that the same universal spirit we seek is frequently hidden within common mercury; however, at the very moment it enters the physical matter of the quicksilver, it becomes <term>specified <note>localized or fixed into a particular form</note></term> and useless for our work. Our work deals solely with living, spiritual metals, and not with physical ones, which are internally united with our universal matter.

### Chap. XXX. Objection against the Matter.

If every thing brings forth its own kind, and gold <note>original symbol: ☉</note> boiled to the highest degree becomes a <term>tinging <note>transformative</note></term> stone, then one must surely seek the gold-making seed within gold itself. One cannot find it in such a lowly and common thing as Chapter VI suggests, but only in its own body, which is gold. For the seed of wheat is wheat; the seed of a dog is in the dog; the seed of man is in man. And the saying of **Sendivogius** <note>Michael Sendivogius (1566–1636), a famous Polish alchemist</note> is not contrary to this—that common gold lost its spirit in the **melting-fire** <note>original symbol: △</note> and is therefore dead. For if that were so, common gold could not be made alive again; since a dead body cannot return to life without a miracle of Divine Omnipotence, so too the spirit cannot return to a soulless metallic body. Yet, gold can indeed be revitalized and raised to the essence of the Stone. Therefore, the Stone must be sought in gold, and our Mercury taken from no other thing than gold.

### Chap. XXXI. Refutation of the above objection.

"In gold is the seed of gold, and from metals must metals come." So cry the inexperienced chemical **bunglers** <note>German: "Stümpler," referring to unskilled amateurs</note> with confidence, for they cannot raise the eye of their mind above the horizon of their physical sight. But metals and minerals, while they still hang in their <term>matrix <note>the natural geological environment or "womb" where minerals grow</note></term>, do indeed possess their seed within them, contrary to this opinion. However, once removed from the mines and matrices, they are without seed, like severed bodies or limbs cut off and separated from animals and plants. These possess no seed; indeed, from the very moment that the life-sap—the rising spirit of life—

Once the spirit has departed from gold and other metals, they are no longer fit to bring forth metals as a seed would. This is because that seed can be brought to no higher perfection by art than that which nature itself has already <term>specified <note>A term meaning nature has already assigned the substance a final, fixed identity, leaving no room for further transformation</note></term>. Art cannot take it any further, nor can it reunite the part that has flown away with its body according to even the slightest **homogeneities** <note>The quality of being uniform in kind or nature</note>; for in the specified body that lacks spirit, there is no seed. Thus, the spirit has evaporated, and the form has been destroyed. Therefore, wheat cannot be compared with gold in this state, because common, dense, and melted gold—having been torn from its **matrix** <note>The "womb" or natural environment where minerals grow</note>—remains sterile, just like a grain of wheat that has been ground and baked into bread. Just as bread no longer brings forth any wheat even when it is cast into the earth <note>The OCR shows "f.", but context suggests "Erde" (earth/soil)</note>; so too is melted gold sterile and without seed. Therefore, I conclude that the gold-seed, from which the **Universal Medicine** <note>Another name for the Philosopher's Stone, capable of curing both metals and human bodies</note> is prepared, is to be obtained not from common metals or minerals, but alone from that body which is entirely a metallic seed, from which both metals and plants have originated.

## Chapter XXXII. The Stone is made neither from animal nor vegetable matter.

It is impossible to make the Stone from anything that is close to animal nature—as for example, from blood, flesh, bones, or seed—unless they are first brought to **putrefaction** <note>The process of rot or decomposition, which alchemists believed released the inner essence of a substance</note>, and after putrefaction are reduced to the mineral nature of <term>Fire/Sulfur</term> and <term>Gold/Sun</term>. But when animal nature casts off something from its immediate matter as being foreign and superfluous to the animal nature, then that which is cast off and superfluous (because it is not an animal part) must certainly be either a vegetable or a mineral. It cannot be a vegetable, because it has been too much altered and subtilized by nature to be of a vegetable nature; for its composition would have to float on <term>Water</term> if it were a vegetable, woody, or herbal substance. Furthermore, if it were a seed or had the nature of a seed, it would sprout forth in the earth. Moreover, it would be absurd of nature if she were to produce a seed out of a thing that was distinct from the nature of that seed; for every thing begets its own kind. Furthermore, this same foreign essence cast off by the animal nature is cast off either within the nourishment, before the nourishment, or after it. If it is cast off within or before the nourishment, it will be a coarser part of the food, from which comes the nourishment and simple purging of the food; but if it is cast off after the nourishment, it has only then been transformed into the closest nature of an animal being.

### Chapter XXXIII. The Stone is made only from a metallic matter.

If the **Philosopher’s Stone** is a Gold-Tincture, which tinctures all metals and makes them into <term>☉</term><note>Alchemical symbol for Gold</note>, then the Stone can come from nothing other than a metallic genus; because only an **agent** <note>An active substance or force that produces a specific effect</note> that is of a metallic kind acts upon the nature of metal. This same agent or acting thing, from which alone metals are made, is the spirit of metallic nature, by which minerals are also nourished and maintained; indeed, because it is in no way different from the general **World-Spirit** <note>The 'Anima Mundi,' a vital breath or soul believed to permeate all nature</note>, by which all things are nourished, it is also said to be in all things; but from which thing is it to be extracted by the **Philosopher** <note>The term used for an alchemist who has attained true knowledge</note>? You have already understood this from what was said before, if you are no dullard, for I have clearly described the matter.

### Chapter XXXIV. What is the Dew of Heaven and the Fatness of the Water [$\nabla$]? <note>The symbol $\nabla$ represents the element of Water</note>

The coagulated dew of heaven and the fatness of the Water [$\nabla$] are two different, separate beings, but from one root. One is the Salt [$\ominus$] <note>The symbol $\ominus$ represents Salt, one of the three Alchemical Principles</note> of Fire [$\triangle$], the other the fatness of the Water [$\nabla$]; both come from the Fire [$\triangle$], where their roots flourish. Both come from the dissolution of bodies and mixed things, which are dissolved in Fire [$\triangle$], and because of the constant generations and nourishments, they are made bodily anew and corrupted again, while they ceaselessly ascend and descend. One is opposed to the other, for the greatest enmity exists between them; but if you can reconcile them and ignite the metallic Fire [$\triangle$] through their active spirit, then you will be happy, and no one but GOD alone will be able to hinder you from attaining health and wealth.

### Chapter XXXV. Of the Fatness of the Earth?

The fatness of the earth is called, to speak sincerely, by a different name in each of the three kingdoms. In the animal kingdom, it is called thick <note>original Latin: "craſſum"</note>, and its source material <term>minera; the raw ore or natural state of a substance</term> is an animal, indeed even man himself. In the vegetable kingdom, it is called a resin <note>original Latin: "reſina"</note> and oil; and the source material of this fat is every plant. In the mineral kingdom, it is called Fire [$\triangle$], and its source materials are all metals. This fatness consists of two extremes: an earthly solid and a volatile heavenly one; but between these extremes, many levels of properties are perceived, although in every degree the fatness always remains the same, which Fire [$\triangle$] alone draws onto the Water [$\nabla$] like a magnet; for without this fatness, which has a magnetic power toward it, this would never remain before our eyes upon the Water [$\nabla$]. I proceed further and say: The fatness is actually called Water [$\nabla$], and its name is Fire [$\triangle$]; it is called water and its name is resin; it is called Fire [$\triangle$] and its name is air <note>original Latin: "æra"</note>. Nevertheless, in the vegetable and animal as well as in the mineral kingdom, the fatness is the foundation of all things, and in it all elements, all principles, and all seeds are contained. Therefore, one must know that there is no alkali <note>a soluble salt obtained from the ashes of plants, vital in alchemical processes</note> except from the ash of burnt fatness. If, therefore, in a burnt alkali that same Fire [$\triangle$] is found which the Sage seeks for the preparation of the Stone, it necessarily follows that an alkali is hidden in the fat, and in the alkali a Water [$\nabla$], which is cooked by the Sage and raised to the Stone. ## Chapter XXXVI. Two separate materials are required before the preparation.

If you do not have an incapable head, you will have already grasped that one must have two materials of different beings at hand, which however in the beginning sprouted from one root; and that these materials must be distinct, and yet have only one nature. For if one is male and the other female, then a generation <note>the creation of a new substance</note> occurs. Therefore, if they were not separated from each other, they could not be united. 

But when the union of these materials has occurred, it becomes that single matter to which nothing is added and nothing is taken away, according to the testimony of Zacharia <note>Denis Zachaire (1510–1556), a famous French alchemist</note>, who says that after the union, no work is easier than ours, as one needs no other labor than the <term>decoction (the long-term heating or "cooking" of a substance)</term> of such already united materials. However, so that you may grasp this truth, I will open it sincerely and extensively in the chapters following now.

## Chapter XXXVII. Whether our Stone, because it is only one, is drawn out from a single body?

Therefore everything happens—whatever it may be—through Fire [🜂], once the Mercury [☿] of the Sages has been prepared beforehand. 

But before our Mercury [☿] is made, one must have two bodies in the first preparation: two mercuries and two fires [🜂], from which the heat of the Suns [☉] and the moisture (the "saliva") of the Moon [☽] <note>Moon symbol for Silver</note> must be taken. **SENDIVOGIUS** <note>Michael Sendivogius (1566–1636), a famous Polish alchemist and advisor to emperors.</note> is right: Here I return to my purpose, and I tell you the truth, my son! One is not created from one, because this belongs to **GOD** alone; let it suffice you that you can bring forth from two a thing that is useful to you. **GEBER’S** <note>Geber is the Latinized name of Jabir ibn Hayyan, the foundational figure of Arabic alchemy.</note> saying is not contrary to this; he added nothing nor took anything away, but rather taught that the superfluous is merely separated during the preparation. For he understands this regarding the immediate matter of the Stone, which is found neither below nor above the earth: This same thing is the single thing of which **PONTANUS** <note>Johann Pontanus, an alchemist famous for a widely circulated letter claiming he traveled the world only to find the secret of the "philosophical fire" in a single word.</note> swears that all dreggy, all impure, and superfluous essence is transformed into the true matter by means of our fire [$\Delta$] <note>The triangle symbol here represents Fire, specifically the "Philosophical Fire" which Pontanus claimed was the secret to the entire art.</note>. 

But **PONTANUS’S** fire [$\Delta$] cannot be taken from a single matter; as he himself speaks: The fire [$\Delta$] is taken from elsewhere, not from the matter; it is also not transformed with the matter, because it is not of it. Therefore, one must conclude that certain bodies are found in which Sulfur [🜍] and Mercury [☿] are properly united with each other, and from which they are separated by the wonderful art of the Philosopher when he brings those same bodies back into the first matter of the Stone. Thus, one should not take Sulfur [🜍] alone, nor Mercury [☿] alone; for the former only blackens and spoils the work without mastery, but with it—that is, with the Mercury [☿]—he completes the work. 

**GEBER** confirms this when he says the medicine cannot be taken from Mercury [☿] alone, because it is not made perfect by itself, but only with an addition, which is Sulfur [🜍]. Without this, the mastery is prolonged to the point of despair <note>original: "ad desperationem protelatur"</note>. Therefore, one adds well-digested Sulfur [🜍] to the Mercury [☿] to shorten the work. Even though this Sulfur [🜍] could be found in the very same subject from which the Mercury [☿] is taken, it would then require far too long an operation, and the artist's life would not be sufficient for its completion. When **GEBER** also speaks: "He who can make it from Mercury alone will be a happy seeker," he was not speaking of this Mercury separated from Sulfur, but rather understood our "whole thing," which is composed of these united parts, Sulfur [🜍] and Mercury [☿] (namely, the Mercury of the Wise).

Matter, our Mercury [<term>☿</term>], our Stone, must be composed of both natures. These two have been compared in the Art to snakes: namely, a fearsome winged one, and another which has no wings but is much more fearsome, as evidence shows in practice.

### Cap. XXXIX. The **Practice** of the Work described in a riddle.

Cut the tail off the double, scaly snake that has hidden its head in red earth. You will find this snake in fields that have great moisture and in green meadows, for it likes to dwell in such places. When the tail is cut from the stinking body, tear off its head as well through the power of the strong **Vulcan** <note>The Roman god of fire, here representing the alchemical furnace or intense heat.</note>; for you will find that the head is fixed and does not fear the Fire [<term>🜂</term>]. From the tail, cut off the tip as well as you can; then join the head to the tail in such a way that the hidden moisture in the head comes out united with the moisture of the tail, so that the glorious medicine may be seen, for it is the radical moisture <note>original: "Wurzel=Feuchtigkeit" (radical moisture). In alchemy and early medicine, this was the essential life-fluid that allowed growth and vitality.</note>. Increase within it the solar and heavenly powers through the power of the tail, which has been drawn from the firmament; thus you will see how the earthly powers receive a wonderful attraction, so that the snake's head begins to rise up and live. Its open mouth will also be so ravenous that it can hardly be satisfied in any way, and it will continually devour its own tail, even if it is of considerable size.

### Chapter XL. Another Practice.

The place of our matter is a mineral cave, or a stony and Saturnine ore [<term>saturnine minera</term> <note>Saturn is the alchemical name for lead; a "Saturnine ore" refers to the dark, heavy starting material of the Work.</note>], which is dedicated to the eternal GOTT alone, and is revealed only to the wise, even though it is unknown to the eyes of the common people despite its preciousness, yet known to them by its lowly value. Know then, that **black ravens** are commonly found in old walls and enjoy flying about there; but **earthly toads** are not infrequently encountered in slimy puddles, in stinking dung heaps, and in fatty subterranean caves. What more? Along with the toad and the raven, which feed on carrion, you will encounter those who seek out detestable things, so that it is not absurdly claimed by the wise: We make the medicine out of the greatest poison. It is indeed wonderful that from those poisoned mineral bodies, which spring from the coldest Chaos, the most noble son of the Sun is born; and from the Water [<term>$\nabla$</note>] the Fire [<term>$\Delta$</note>] is produced, from the poison the medicine, and from death, life. Therefore, see to it that an eagle comes from the raven, and a lion from the toad <note>These animals represent stages of transformation: the raven is the black decay, the eagle is sublimation or rising vapors, and the lion is the fixed, strong result.</note>, which will then happen when you can whiten the fatness of the earth by its own graduated movement of the spirit from the dew of heaven. The belly should not be washed out too cleanly (*dilutus* <note>original Latin: "diluted" or "washed away"</note>); bring it into a clear Water [<term>$\nabla$</note>], in which the soft, tender female is washed until white, she who is as eager for the red man as matter is for form. But unite and prepare them naked, so that you suffer no harm; mix water with water, and digest it under clear clouds. The wedding must be completed in the House of Nature, and the mixing must occur several repeated times, so that the union becomes more eager and the conception all the more certain. The vessel of the wise is their Water [<term>$\nabla$</note>]; but we need two of them to finish more quickly. Consider what the matter throws away during the extraction of the redness; for it creates a very large foam (*ampullositatem* <note>original Latin: "bubbling" or "frothing"</note>). The shortcut consists in the diligent separation of the excrement <note>In alchemy, "excrement" refers to the useless dross or impurities that must be purged to reach the pure essence.</note>; therefore, when you separate them with a philosophical sieve, you have need of nothing more. If you are chosen, you will understand better things than these, or I will be able to give better.

### Chapter XLI. Another Clearer Practice.

Take of the congealed **dew of heaven** and the **fat of the earth** <note>These terms often refer to primordial salts or nitre collected from the atmosphere and soil, believed to contain the universal spirit.</note> as much as you wish; rub them and mix their bodies, and lay them in a well-sealed **marriage bed**: (chamber of delight) <note>original: "Cameram delectionis"</note>. And because they are cold on the outside and have no desire without the stimulating movement, provoke them with a masculine Fire [<term>$\Delta$</term>] so that they may be ignited and, through their secret mingling, may release their seed—that is, a smoke or exhalation in which that very spirit is enclosed which we seek and greatly need. This spirit, which is congealed from the air in the belly of the wind or the exhalation, runs drop by drop in a very clear water into a well-sealed receiver, leaving our dry, stout Lato [<term>Laton</term> <note>Laton, or Lato, refers to the "impure body" or the base metallic matter that must be purified and whitened during the alchemical process.</note>], weakened and thirsty from the coitus, at the bottom of the vessel. Heal this Lato with that same Water [<term>$\nabla$</term>], which is a Water [<term>$\nabla$</term>] of life, and replenish the Lato again, who lacks the spirit; let him drink as often and as much until he, saturated by our spiritual water, visibly swells up. Thereafter, he must be brought into the bedchamber to fall asleep, so that he may transform his nourishment—because it is metallic—through a good digestion by our living Water [<term>$\nabla$</term>]. Whatever is foreign then goes out as a sweat through the imperceptible exhalation.

You should also not wonder when you see many kinds of internal colors appearing mixed together upon its face, for it cannot be otherwise; because our Water [<term>$\nabla$</term>] is purifying, it sweeps out all accidental impurities which cannot be transformed into the true essence and its matter. And thus, during the expulsion of the superfluous, slimy moisture, one sees all kinds of unstable colors, all of which are volatile, until the white appears. But before you reach the white, you must know a great secret, and that consists in the knowledge of the time in which the actual conception occurs. You must therefore know the way in which **Luna** <note>The Moon, representing silver or the "cold" feminine principle.</note> is to be cooled so that you may find the warmth of **Sol** <note>The Sun, representing gold or the "hot" masculine principle.</note>, which no foolish artist succeeds in doing, because the perfection of the work consists in the rising of the Stone.

When Lato has become white, then break the books and rejoice, for in the white color the spirits are fixed, and Lato fears no stronger Fire [<term>$\Delta$</term>] anymore, until he is cooked to the highest degree and colored with an internal redness, and becomes the blessed Stone itself, which colors all metals into Sol [<term>$\odot$</term> <note>The symbol for Gold.</note>]. If, therefore, you can understand or learn nothing from what I have said, then you are not called by fortune. I have described the matter of the **Philosopher's Stone**, and how one should proceed with it, more clearly than it ought to have been. If you are sensible, you have here everything you desire; but if you are ignorant, I shall have said nothing for you.

<summary>This chapter provides a more "practical" allegorical guide to the alchemical process, describing the distillation of a spiritual "water" from "dew" to purify the "Lato" (base matter) until it reaches the white and finally the red stage of the Philosopher's Stone.</summary>
<keywords>Dew of Heaven, Fat of the Earth, Laton, Sol and Luna, Albedo, Rubedo, Fixation of Spirits, Alchemical Fire, Alchemical Water</keywords>

# Appendix.
## George Ripley’s Song of the Newborn Chemical King. <note>George Ripley (c. 1415–1490) was an influential English alchemist. This poem, originally in English but translated here from the German version in the manuscript, uses the metaphor of a King to describe the transformation of matter into the Philosopher's Stone.</note>

->I.<-

1. I will now bring forth the secrets of the philosophers,
And sing of them an elegant song with a raised voice,
Out of a joyful spirit, which drives me to such things,
And it shall ring most lovely in the hearts and minds of those who hear.

2. Once, when **Mercury** <note>In alchemy, Mercury represents the fluid, transformative principle and the universal solvent.</note> held a wedding at the furthest ends of the earth, it happened that I had to help complete the appointed feast; as it proceeded with great abundance, I learned what new things I now wish to send into the world.

3. A born King was entirely sterile and without heirs, highly noble and so beautiful that no painter could color anything more beautiful, for whose favor every man must strive; of a **sanguine nature** <note>Sanguine refers to the "blood" temperament, associated with air, heat, and moisture. In alchemy, it often signifies the red stage of the work or the "living" quality of the metal.</note>, he lamented his ruin,

4. Speaking: "Why am I, despite such mighty rule, King and Head of the Bodies, able to adorn all lands with growth and fertility, but yet cannot bear the name of a Father, who had ever begotten anything from his own loins?"

5. "Indeed, the cause may well be quite natural and well-founded, or perhaps an innate defect is found within me; though by nature I am pure and have never sinned, and am nourished by the radiance that the **Sun** <note>original: "Sonn". In this context, the Sun represents the source of celestial heat and the archetypal Gold.</note> itself kindles for us."

6. "Whatever grows out of the earth multiplies itself from its seed, just as every animal species turns to its own kind, mates and increases, as nature has taught, so that a young generation is there when the old is destroyed."

7. "But my very strong body is so firmly locked, that no seed can be poured out from it of its own accord; therefore I am barren, have never enjoyed **coitus** <note>Alchemical "coitus" refers to the union of the active (masculine/sulfur) and passive (feminine/mercury) principles within the vessel.</note>, and until this time, nothing has sprouted from my lineage."

<meta>catchword: 8. Ways:</meta>

<summary>This page introduces an allegorical poem by George Ripley where a noble but sterile King (representing Gold or the fixed principle) laments his inability to produce an heir (multiply his substance) despite his purity and power.</summary>
<keywords>George Ripley, Chemical King, Mercury, Alchemy, Sanguine, Sterility, Multiplication, Philosophical Song</keywords>

--- Page 705 ---
<meta>This page continues the allegorical "Song of the Newborn Chemical King" by George Ripley. In the previous stanzas, the King (representing Gold or the fixed principle) lamented his sterility and inability to produce heirs despite his majesty. Here, the allegory transitions into the chemical processes of dissolution and putrefaction, framed as a biological return to the womb and a subsequent "death" before rebirth.</meta>

### Appendix.
#### George Ripley’s Song of the Newborn Chemical King.

8. Because of such firmness of my body, my strength
Always remains, for the moisture of my body does not leave me
Through evaporation; even if I am made hot, burned, or toasted,
Indeed, in the greatest fire, I am only elevated without any loss. <note>In alchemy, gold is known as the "fixed" metal because it does not lose mass or oxidize when heated in a furnace, unlike "volatile" or base metals.</note>

9. My mother bore me at home as a **round being**,
And so by nature I am inclined toward roundness;
I am so pure through and through that my brilliance deceives many;
Every King preens with me when he shows himself in honor. <note>The "roundness" refers both to the perfection of the sphere and to gold coins. The "Mother" refers to the Mercurial source from which metals were thought to be generated in the earth.</note>

10. Therefore, I know now for certain that it is not possible
For me to be fruitful unless others stand by me;
For I am old and aged, and can expect nothing for myself
Other than that all my days shall pass childless.

11. My youth is gone, and I have nothing further to hope for
Than that I shall one day be struck by death’s arrow;
Yet it seems to me that the door of **the promise** <note>A reference to the biblical concept of being "born again" (John 3:3), which Ripley applies to the chemical "rebirth" of the Stone.</note> also stands open to me:
That one must come anew, enclosed from the mother’s womb.

12. For otherwise I cannot reach the **Kingdom of Heaven**,
Unless I am received a second time into birth;
Therefore, I long to return to my mother’s lap,
And to be **regenerated**; I wish to begin this very soon. <note>In the alchemical process, "regeneration" involves dissolving the solid metal back into a liquid state (the "mother's womb") so it can be purified and "reborn" with greater power.</note>

13. The Mother herself urged this King to do this,
Hastening to receive him soon with motherly love;
Which great wonder-work she actually did perform:
She received into herself, as a child, this **King among seven**. <note>The "seven" are the seven metals of antiquity: Gold, Silver, Mercury, Copper, Iron, Tin, and Lead. Gold is the King.</note>

14. It was wondrous to see how soon from both of them
A mixed being arose, looking white almost like **chalk**;
The child clothed itself entirely in the motherly blood,
So that henceforth the two can never be separated. <note>This describes the "Conjunction," where the solid (King) and the solvent (Mother/Mercury) merge into a white, paste-like substance.</note>

15. Thereupon the mother betook herself to a pure **white bed**,
Whose whiteness vied even with the bright Moon;
She locked the chamber door fast, so that she would have no unrest
From strangers; yet she became ill in that lonely place. <note>The "white bed" and the "Moon" represent the *Albedo* or white stage of the work. The "locked door" refers to the hermetic sealing of the glass vessel (the Philosopher's Egg).</note>

16. Yes, she came into the **agony of death**, and her previously
White body went into an **ugly rotting**; yet no help could be given,
Even though her distress was seen through the window from time to time;
She was locked away, and no one was allowed to rush to her aid. <note>The "ugly rotting" is the *Nigredo* or black stage (putrefaction). The "window" is the glass of the laboratory flask, through which the alchemist observes the transformation but must not interfere by opening the seal.</note>

<summary>This page uses the allegory of a King returning to his mother's womb to describe the alchemical stages of dissolution and putrefaction. The King (Gold) merges with his Mother (Mercurial solvent) to undergo a "second birth," resulting in a state of decay (Nigredo) necessary for his eventual transformation into the Philosopher's Stone.</summary>

<keywords>George Ripley, Cantilena, King of Metals, Alchemical Allegory, Regeneration, Nigredo, Putrefaction, Hermetic Seal, Fixed and Volatile</keywords>

--- Page 706 ---
<meta>This page continues George Ripley’s alchemical allegory, "The Song of the Newborn Chemical King." The previous page described the King’s realization that he must undergo a "rebirth" through a mother (the Mercurial solvent) to overcome his sterility. This page details the symbolic pregnancy, the multicolored stages of the "Great Work," and the controlled environment of the alchemical furnace.</meta>

### Appendix.

17. Meanwhile she had to enjoy **peacock meat** for food,
And have her drink poured for her by **Mercury**,
Which the **Green Lion**, when he was slain, let flow;
And thus the poor woman had to do penance, as if in prison. <note>The "Green Lion" usually refers to a strong mineral acid or vitriol used to dissolve gold. The "Peacock" represents the *cauda pavonis* stage, where the chemical mixture displays a spectrum of colors.</note>

18. Yet during this pregnancy, she bore this quite well:
For a full forty weeks, though not without lamentation,
As she shed many tears over her heavy plagues,
Which flowed like milk before her days of childbirth. <note>The "tears" and "milk" refer to the condensation and white vapors (the "White Stone" stage) that appear during the long heating process.</note>

19. The skin of this woman was very multicolored to behold:
Black and green and ash-grey, and like a **peacock’s tail**.
Also bright red, like blood flowing from hacked-up veins;
Often she could also be seen moving up and down. <note>The movement "up and down" describes distillation and reflux within the sealed glass vessel, where matter vaporizes and then drips back down.</note>

20. One hundred and fifty days she spent in this weakness,
And during this time shed tears and made much complaint;
Finally, after thirty more, our **King** awoke anew,
And in the beautiful springtime smiled upon the world once again.

21. His belly, which at first was in proportion to his limbs,
Could now hold a thousand times more than before;
Just as the beginning is best confirmed by the end,
His proof may be seen in the **fire** as often as one wishes. <note>This refers to "Multiplication," the stage where the power of the alchemical medicine is increased so that a small amount can transform a large mass of metal.</note>

22. A comfortable **little chamber** was prepared there,
Beautifully paneled everywhere and smoothed to the highest degree,
Built high up and sealed as tightly as possible,
So that the delicate fruit would not be destroyed by cold air. <note>The "chamber" is the Alchemical Egg or glass flask, which must be perfectly sealed—the "Hermetic seal"—to prevent any loss of substance.</note>

23. Therefore, for this purpose, a **little oven** was also present
By the prepared bed, as it was of the highest importance
That the room be maintained with very gentle heat
To ward off all cold, which is entirely contrary to the fruit. <note>The "little oven" is the Athanor, a furnace designed to maintain a steady, low temperature over many months.</note>

24. The chamber door was also well provided with lock and hinge,
So that no one could go in or out without permission;
The chimney hole was secured, and no air could blow through,
So that if strength departed, no damage might occur.

25. Here the child’s little limbs were reduced to pillars <note>original: "gesäulet", likely meaning fixed or calcined into a stable structure</note> anew,
And everything became ashes and was divided into delicate dust,
Black and ugly; and as time was spent there,
The brilliance of the **Moon** and **Sun** hurried forth once again. <note>The "Moon and Sun" represent the final white and red stages of the work, resulting in the creation of silver and gold.</note>

<summary>This page describes the alchemical "gestation" of the Stone, moving through the multicolored peacock stage and the black stage of putrefaction. It emphasizes the need for a sealed vessel and a controlled, gentle heat in the furnace to achieve the final transformation.</summary>
<keywords>Green Lion, Mercury, Peacock's Tail, Athanor, Hermetic Seal, Multiplicatio, Nigredo, Alchemical King</keywords>

<meta>This page continues the allegorical poem describing the final stages of the "Great Work." Having undergone the "blackness" of the previous stages, the King is now being reborn in a purified form, signaling the transition from the Albedo (white) stage to the final Rubedo (red) stage.</meta>

### Appendix.

26. When the time had finally come for the child to be born into the world
By the mother, whom she had conceived before,
She gave birth for a second time to a truly chosen Heaven-Child,
A King of his own race, restoring that which was lost.

27. Previously, the mother’s bed was prepared with four corners,
But after the appointed time, it stretched itself into a circle,
And gradually became completely round, like the rim of a basin,
White and shining like the moon, and without blemish or stain. <note>The transition from "four corners" to "round" symbolizes the alchemical "squaring of the circle," representing the unification of the four elements into a single, perfected substance.</note>

28. Thus, the four-cornered form of the bed was now seen as round,
And the formerly black color was seen rising up bright and white,
And soon thereafter rising into the highest redness,
In which this great King shall unceasingly endure. <note>These colors—black, white, and red—represent the three primary stages of alchemy: *Nigredo* (decay), *Albedo* (purification), and *Rubedo* (perfection).</note>

29. Now God has opened wide the gates of Paradise,
Where the radiance of the bright moon shone magnificently in all places,
And, according to the words of the philosophers, rose higher and higher
Toward the Sun-Circle, adorned with ruby-red golden borders.

30. This King’s coat of arms was the sign of the four elements;
In the middle stood a Virgin, who had no equal,
Full of white and red roses plucked from the bushes,
Which fully attained the power of the <term>Quintessence</term> <note>The "Fifth Essence" or the purest, most concentrated essence of a substance, beyond the four physical elements.</note>.

31. This Virgin is adorned with the most beautiful gemstones,
Which shine most excellently with their luster and glow;
They also belong to the Wise alone, and do not belong to the swine,
To keep whom away, they strongly hedge in their garden. <note>A reference to "casting pearls before swine." Alchemists were notoriously secretive, believing their knowledge should only be accessible to the spiritually worthy.</note>

32. In the Virgin’s lap, one saw the <term>Green Lion</term> <note>A common symbol for strong mineral acids or "vitriol" capable of dissolving gold.</note> lying,
To whom the <term>Eagle</term> <note>The Eagle represents "sublimation"—the process where a solid is heated into a vapor and then recollected as a purified solid.</note> brought food, whose nature is to fly high;
From the Lion’s body flowed blood, he who usually triumphs with strength;
This blood <term>Mercury</term> <note>The messenger of the gods, here representing the "Universal Solvent" or the spirit that mediates between the fixed and the volatile.</note> gave as a drink to our Virgin with pleasure.

33. Wondrous was the milk which came from her breasts,
Which the Lion drank and for which he felt a great longing;
She was also busy preparing a bath-sponge,
In order to wash him with milk to sustain him in health.

34. She was also crowned with a crown of unspeakable value,
And enthroned upon a great throne very high in the air;
Her clothes are beautifully adorned all around with stars,
So that the hearts of all the Wise long for such beauty.

Following the rebirth of the King mentioned on the previous page, the text now describes his celestial coronation and his role as a source of universal healing and incorruptible wealth, signaling the final perfection of the Philosopher's Stone.</meta>

### Appendix.

35. The twelve signs <note>original: "zwölf Zeichen"; referring to the signs of the Zodiac.</note> stood around his head, as did the planets,
While the clouds and darkness all retreated far from her,
And she was now entirely freed from the aforementioned trials,
And her King, newly born, is now nevermore to be killed.

36. Who is a supreme victor over every enemy,
The most powerful ruler over all kings as well,
A perfectly rich adorner with health and wealth,
Whom everyone serves, from the great and small to the lowliest kitchen-stoker.

37. He can richly endow both spiritual and worldly people,
Refreshing all those who have become sick back to health;
Who would not gladly have something from his treasure in their possession,
Since it is not consumed by rust, worms, or moths? <note>This is a biblical allusion to Matthew 6:19-20, suggesting that the alchemical "Stone" is a spiritual treasure that does not decay like worldly metals.</note>

38. May God grant grace to those who are now of good will,
To partake in these things, and forgive us all our sins;
Let these and other gifts flourish to His glory,
And help us so that we may rejoice with Him eternally.

A complex circular mystical diagram titled "The Great Mystery or MYSTERIUM MAGNUM." The diagram is contained within a rectangular frame and consists of two large intersecting circles (forming a central mandorla shape) surrounded by and containing numerous concentric rings, arcs, and radial lines. 

At the top vertical axis, a small circle contains the Hebrew Tetragrammaton (יהוה) and the word "LIGHT". At the bottom vertical axis, a corresponding circle contains the Hebrew name (אדני) and the word "NIGHT". 

The diagram is labeled with theological and cosmological terms in English. The top hemisphere represents "The Abyss of Mercy" and includes terms like "Word [made] Flesh," "Jerusalem," and "Abraham's Bosom." The bottom hemisphere represents "The Abyss of Wrath" and includes "Damnation of the Devil" and "Abyss of Darkness."

A horizontal divider across the center is labeled "Hem of the Knowledge of Good and Evil." Within the central intersection of circles is a small triangle and the phrase "Bond of Love." 

On the right side, a list of seven names (archangels) is written vertically: Zaphkiel, Zadkiel, Camael, Raphael, Hanäel, Michael, and Gabriel. Numerous other labels describe spiritual states or zones, such as "Tree of Life," "Paradise," and "The Forecourts."

### Figures 12 through 15: The Geometry of Vision
<note>These diagrams illustrate the early modern understanding of optics, focusing on how light rays interact with surfaces and the eye.</note>

**Numbers 12 and 13**
Geometric diagrams showing the projection of light rays from spheres and planes. The intersecting lines and coordinates (labeled A through Z) demonstrate how a three-dimensional object is represented on a two-dimensional surface.

**Number 14**
A demonstration of a sphere (b) illuminated by a conical beam of light (g, h). This illustrates the concept of "point-source" illumination and the casting of shadows.

**Number 15**
A perspective drawing of a cubic and pyramidal frame. This diagram likely explains the "visual pyramid," a core concept in Renaissance and Baroque art theory where the eye is the apex of a pyramid of light rays extending to the object.

***

### Figures 16 through 34: Universal Geometry and Proportions
<note>This section explores circular and linear divisions, culminating in sacred geometry.</note>

**Numbers 16–22**
Simple circular divisions and cylindrical tubes, used to explain how light is channeled or restricted through apertures.

**Number 24**
A hexagram or "Star of David" inscribed within a circle. 
<note>In this context, the hexagram often represents the "as above, so below" principle, where the upward-pointing triangle (fire/light) and downward-pointing triangle (water/darkness) interlock to form the world.</note>
